significance.explanation: Ranking round only: no one is eliminated, and seeds are the sole prize. It shapes the brackets but decides no medals.

experience.explanation: Not ticketed, so there is no live seat to judge. The late-afternoon ranking arrows are a practice-style affair.

starPower.explanation: Kim Wu-Jin and Brady Ellison's circle will be shooting, but nobody is playing for a trophy on this day.

uniqueness.explanation: Women's compound shoots ranking arrows at a Games for the first time. A quiet first, but still only a seeding session.

demand.explanation: No tickets on sale, so demand is effectively nil. It sits at the floor of the scale.

scorecard.overall: Nobody can buy a seat, and that is the point: this is the paperwork that writes the bracket. Watch the scores for who gets the soft draw, and save your ticket money for the elimination days.

significance.explanation: Seeding only. Men's compound and women's recurve scores set the draws, but nobody goes home.

experience.explanation: Not ticketed, and a 9:30 AM ranking round is the quietest format archery offers.

starPower.explanation: Kang Chaeyoung and Zhu Jingyi will post scores here, though the round has no head-to-head drama.

uniqueness.explanation: Men's compound gets its first Games ranking round, a small historic footnote on a seeding morning.

demand.explanation: Not ticketed, so there is nothing to chase. It bottoms out the scale by default.

scorecard.overall: A closed-door seeding morning that still carries real weight: Korea's women get measured here, and the compound debut gets its first numbers. Fascinating on paper, but you can't attend.

significance.explanation: Opens the archery medals and awards the first compound gold ever at a Games, all inside a single evening.

experience.explanation: Night archery under lights at Carson, with a full bracket from 1/8 to gold. Soccer-style sight lines keep everyone close.

starPower.explanation: India's Taniparthi and Jadhav, USA's Alexis Ruiz and Austria's Nico Wiener are the names. Recognition is high in archery, modest outside it.

uniqueness.explanation: First compound medals in Games history, and the first new bowstyle since 1972. You can say you were there.

demand.explanation: A medal night with a debut tag will sell, and India's travelling fans add pressure. It's still a niche sport.

scorecard.overall: The first compound gold ever awarded, with India chasing its first archery medal of any kind. Millimeter finishes and a debut-night buzz make this the best ticket of the opening archery days.

significance.explanation: Round of 64 for both individual events. Real elimination, but a long way from a podium.

experience.explanation: A morning slate with dozens of matches across the field, so you can pick an archer and follow along.

starPower.explanation: Kim Wu-Jin and Im Si-hyeon may open here, and the Indian newcomers will be shooting too. Top seeds usually get the easiest draws.

uniqueness.explanation: The standard opening round of an established discipline. It is the first look at brackets, not a headline event.

demand.explanation: Easier to book than the medal nights, though a Games morning still draws a crowd.

scorecard.overall: The cheapest way to see Paris champions Kim Wu-Jin and Im Si-hyeon in elimination play. Relaxed and low-pressure for spectators, with enough early upsets to keep it lively.

significance.explanation: Rounds of 64 and 32 only. Upsets matter for the bracket, but no medals change hands.

experience.explanation: Evening lights at a soccer stadium make a better setting than the morning shift. Pick a target and settle in.

starPower.explanation: Kim Woojin, five-time champion, and Mete Gazoz are the draws. Marie Horackova and Zhu Jingyi sit on the women's side.

uniqueness.explanation: One of several elimination sessions. The Carson setting adds some color, but the format is routine.

demand.explanation: Prime-time slot gives it a slight edge over the mornings. Comfortably gettable by Games standards.

scorecard.overall: Night elimination archery with Kim Woojin in the mix, and a Gazoz rematch possible later. Pleasant under lights, and a good value pick before the medal sessions get pricey.

significance.explanation: Round of 64 and 32 matches, where early exits cost seeds rather than medals.

experience.explanation: A Sunday morning with a full range of matches. Light and easygoing, with a target-by-target rhythm.

starPower.explanation: Kang Chaeyoung, Lee Woo-seok and Oh Yejin could appear. Korea's depth means a Korean star is likely somewhere on the line.

uniqueness.explanation: Another early-round session in a long bracket. Nothing about the date or format sets it apart.

demand.explanation: A morning slot and non-medal stakes keep it on the softer side of the archery schedule.

scorecard.overall: A relaxed Sunday morning for fans who like to follow one archer through a match. Korea's new wave is the storyline, and the lighter crowds make it an easier ticket.

significance.explanation: Rounds of 64 and 32 only. Everyone advances toward medals, but none are awarded.

experience.explanation: Sunday night under the lights with a home crowd rooting for Americans. That atmosphere beats the morning sessions.

starPower.explanation: Brady Ellison, the Paris silver medalist and world No. 2, leads a cast that includes Lisa Barbelin and Mete Gazoz.

uniqueness.explanation: A home-soil appearance by Ellison gives it some extra color beyond a routine early round.

demand.explanation: American fans and a Sunday evening slot lift interest above the other early sessions.

scorecard.overall: The pick for U.S. fans who want to see Brady Ellison on home soil before the medal rounds. Gazoz and Barbelin are fine supporting acts on a good-looking night.

significance.explanation: Early women's rounds. The field narrows, but no medals and no semifinals yet.

experience.explanation: A short women's-only morning keeps the focus tight. Daylight session, smaller crowd.

starPower.explanation: Kang Chaeyoung, Zhu Jingyi, Marie Horackova and 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod give the field real depth, even if Im Si-hyeon may be absent.

uniqueness.explanation: A standard women's elimination morning with no format twist or debut.

demand.explanation: Weekday morning and an early round make this one of the more available tickets.

scorecard.overall: A compact two-hour look at the strongest women's field in the sport without any men's matches to split your attention. Good value if you want to scout the new Korean standard.

significance.explanation: Men's team medals, bronze and gold in one evening. A single medal event, but the final is a major night for archery.

experience.explanation: Evening team finals at Carson mean three-archer matches and a loud crowd. Fast, readable, and built for a stadium.

starPower.explanation: Kim Woojin chasing a fourth straight team gold, plus Ellison's USA and France as challengers. Household names in the sport.

uniqueness.explanation: Korea's streak adds a historical hook, but this is a standard team final in an established event.

demand.explanation: A medal night with prime-time timing. Strong demand, though archery is not a marquee sport.

scorecard.overall: Kim Woojin goes for a record-extending fourth straight team gold, with France and the U.S. closing the gap. A full medal bracket in one evening is the best-value way to see archery's top end.

significance.explanation: Rounds of 64 and 32 for men. Real pressure, but still a long way from any medal.

experience.explanation: A midday slot with the field thinning. Calm, approachable, and good for settling in with the sport.

starPower.explanation: Kim Woojin, Lee Woo-seok, Gazoz and Bommadevara are all in the draw. Top names are likely to appear.

uniqueness.explanation: A routine men's elimination session. The evening team finals are the real event on this date.

demand.explanation: Easier ticket than the evening medal session, though the lineup quality keeps it solid.

scorecard.overall: A morning for fans who want to watch the men's favorites survive a dangerous round. Pair it with the evening team medals for a full day at Carson.

significance.explanation: Women's team medals in one night. A single medal event, though the gold and bronze matches both carry a podium.

experience.explanation: Team finals at night under lights are fast and loud. Three archers per side mean plenty of swings.

starPower.explanation: Kang Chaeyoung, An San and the Indian and U.S. teams add names. Lim Sihyeon and Nam Su-hyeon may not be there.

uniqueness.explanation: Korea's reign is under real threat after India's Asian Games upset. That makes this an open, interesting final.

demand.explanation: Medal evening with an open field. Hot but not at the level of marquee sports.

scorecard.overall: Korea's women arrive with a title streak under pressure from India, Chinese Taipei and the U.S. The most open women's team final in years, which is the reason to go.

significance.explanation: Round of 16 for mixed team. The pairs are one win from the quarterfinals, and no medals yet.

experience.explanation: Mixed team matches are quick, with four arrows each and no hiding. The format is easy for newcomers to follow.

starPower.explanation: Spain's world champions Canales and Temino headline, with Korea's Kim Woojin and Oh Yejin possible.

uniqueness.explanation: The recurve version comes days after the compound debut, giving the 1/8 round a little extra context.

demand.explanation: A late-morning early round. Easy to fit into a day with the evening finals.

scorecard.overall: A fast, easy-to-follow format with the reigning world champions from Spain in the draw. Come for the speed, stay for the evening mixed team medals.

significance.explanation: Mixed team recurve medals are decided here, from quarterfinal through gold. One medal event, but with high drama.

experience.explanation: Wednesday night lights and a format built for shoot-offs. Matches can turn on a single arrow.

starPower.explanation: Kim Woojin, Spain's Canales and Temino, and likely Chinese and U.S. pairs. A loaded set of recognizable names.

uniqueness.explanation: One of two mixed team medals, and a rematch of the 2025 world final is possible. Shoot-off potential gives it extra bite.

demand.explanation: Medal night with an open field. Fans will want in, though archery sits below the marquee sports.

scorecard.overall: Spain against Korea again would be the headline, but the quick format makes any pairing dangerous. A single arrow can flip a match, which is ideal for a night crowd.

significance.explanation: Round of 16 for men, one win from the quarterfinals. Stakes are rising, but no medal is on the line.

experience.explanation: A tight two-hour morning where every match matters. Home support for Ellison could lift the roar.

starPower.explanation: Brady Ellison, Temino, Gazoz, Bommadevara and Korea's stars. Most of the men's top names could be in the draw.

uniqueness.explanation: Ellison at a home Games adds spice. Otherwise a normal men's 1/8 round.

demand.explanation: Late rounds and a big-name field push interest above the early sessions.

scorecard.overall: The point where the men's bracket turns serious, with Ellison's home crowd and Temino's target on his back. Great value if you can't get the evening final.

significance.explanation: Men's individual gold and bronze are on the line, the headline event of the recurve program.

experience.explanation: Thursday night finals at Carson, with 27,000 watching shot by shot. Shoot-off potential makes it theatrical.

starPower.explanation: Kim Woojin, Brady Ellison, Temino and Bommadevara are the big names. A Paris rematch is possible.

uniqueness.explanation: An Ellison–Kim rematch on U.S. soil would add a rare storyline, though the format itself is standard.

demand.explanation: The flagship archery final. Expect it to be the hardest archery ticket of the Games.

scorecard.overall: Archery's marquee night: the individual gold, with Kim Woojin and a home-crowd Brady Ellison on a collision course. If you buy one archery session, make it this one.

significance.explanation: Round of 16 elimination: no medals awarded, but a single bad end sends a world-class archer home. Real stakes, just a few rounds shy of the podium.

experience.explanation: Morning light, arrows at 70 meters and a 27,000-seat soccer stadium with close sight lines. Pleasant and intimate, though without prime-time buzz.

starPower.explanation: Korean contenders like world champion Kang Chaeyoung, plus China's Zhu Jingyi and Czechia's Marie Horackova, are all likely in this field. Names are known mostly to archery fans.

uniqueness.explanation: Early knockout round in an established sport, but at a venue hosting archery for only ten days. Teen sensation Kumkum Mohod of India adds a storyline.

demand.explanation: Morning elimination session that should be an easier ticket than the evening medal card. Still, Games scarcity and a compact archery schedule keep it moving.

scorecard.overall: The bracket gets cruel here, and top seeds can fall to a single arrow. It is the cheaper way to see the same stars, and you can sit close, but save the real drama for that night's medal session.

significance.explanation: Two medals are decided, bronze and gold, and the quarterfinals and semifinals feed straight into them. A non-marquee sport, but this is the final medal session of the archery program.

experience.explanation: Night archery under lights in a 27,000-seat stadium, with a hush before each shoot-off arrow. The closing slot of the program adds tension and atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Reigning world champion Kang Chaeyoung, World Cup Final winner Marie Horackova and China's Zhu Jingyi headline. Elite names within archery, though not household ones.

uniqueness.explanation: It closes the archery program, with the first-ever medals for compound archery already awarded earlier in the week. A rare chance to see Korea's dominance challenged live, perhaps by teenager Kumkum Mohod.

demand.explanation: Evening medal session in a mid-tier sport, on the last night of archery. Expect strong competition for seats, a notch below marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: Archery's final medal is decided on a hushed night in Carson, with Korea's grip on this event under real threat. If you want one archery ticket, this is the one: gold-medal pressure, one arrow at a time.

significance.explanation: Opening-morning heats and Round 1 runs. The stakes are advancement rather than medals, but every sprinter here is chasing a Games place.

experience.explanation: Early 9am start under Southern California sun. The Coliseum atmosphere is building, but the crowd is still filling in.

starPower.explanation: Top sprinters often run early rounds, so Jefferson-Wooden or Richardson could appear, though the headliners are less certain than in finals.

uniqueness.explanation: Day-one card at the Coliseum with several event types. Still one of many routine early rounds, though the opening-day context helps.

demand.explanation: Morning day-one sessions at the Coliseum still sell, but this is one of the easier sessions to book.

scorecard.overall: A morning mix of 100m heats, distance rounds and field qualifying on day one at the Coliseum. Best for fans who want the Games to open before the medals start; the sprint names are the draw.

significance.explanation: Women's 100m final on day one, with the 10,000m and shot put medals also decided. Gold-medal sprint stakes at the top of the program.

experience.explanation: Evening final at the Coliseum on the opening night of athletics. The open bowl should be at its loudest for the sprint.

starPower.explanation: Jefferson-Wooden, Alfred and Richardson are all in contention, and the 10,000m adds Chebet-level distance names.

uniqueness.explanation: Women's 100m final opening the athletics program at the Coliseum is a once-only combination of marquee event and iconic venue.

demand.explanation: Opening-night finals of the Games' top track event. Expect this to be among the most sought-after sessions.

scorecard.overall: Day one's headline night: the women's 100m semifinal and final at the Coliseum, plus the 10,000m and shot put finals. Jefferson-Wooden, Alfred and Richardson lead a sprint final that opens the athletics program.

significance.explanation: Decathlon openers and qualifying rounds, with the mixed 4x400m first round. Real stakes for advancement, though no medals are decided here.

experience.explanation: Sunday morning at the Coliseum. Good weather and a big bowl, though the field events build slowly for casual viewers.

starPower.explanation: Decathletes and throwers may compete here, but the top names are more likely in the evening finals.

uniqueness.explanation: Routine qualifying and decathlon opener in a standard format, even at an iconic venue.

demand.explanation: Early-morning sessions of multi-event and field qualifying draw specialist fans, and seats still move steadily.

scorecard.overall: Sunday morning with decathlon openers, several qualifying rounds and the mixed 4x400m first round. Best for field-event fans who like watching up close; the stars are saved for the evening.

significance.explanation: Men's 100m final headlines a night that also decides the shot put, hammer and mixed 4x400m medals. Fastest-man stakes at their peak.

experience.explanation: Sunday night 100m semifinals and final at the Coliseum. The most electric setting the Games can offer on track.

starPower.explanation: Lyles's injury trims the field, but Bednarek and Thompson keep the 100m a superstar final.

uniqueness.explanation: Men's 100m final at the Coliseum on the second night of athletics, alongside a debut mixed relay final.

demand.explanation: Athletics finals night with the men's 100m. Among the hardest tickets in the athletics program.

scorecard.overall: Sunday night headliner: the men's 100m semifinals and final, with shot put, hammer and mixed 4x400m medals also decided. Bednarek and Thompson keep the fastest-man question wide open.

significance.explanation: Single medal final in the women's triple jump, with early rounds around it. One live final with real stakes.

experience.explanation: Monday morning session with the sun climbing over the open bowl. A pleasant setting, but without evening energy.

starPower.explanation: Triple jump final with a few recognizable names, though the 400m and steeplechase rounds bring less star power.

uniqueness.explanation: Single triple jump final plus routine early rounds. A standard format at a famous venue.

demand.explanation: A live medal final in a field event draws steady interest, with the early rounds easing pressure on seats.

scorecard.overall: A Monday morning session with the women's triple jump final and early rounds in the 400m, 3000m steeplechase and hurdles repechage. A good pick for fans who want one clean final before the field fills out.

significance.explanation: Men's pole vault final decides a gold medal in a marquee sport, with the debut mixed 4x100m final on the same night.

experience.explanation: Evening pole vault final at the Coliseum, where the bar rising under the lights builds real tension.

starPower.explanation: Duplantis is the headline draw, and the 1500m repechage adds Kerr and Ingebrigtsen names.

uniqueness.explanation: The debut mixed 4x100m relay final shares a night with a Duplantis-led pole vault final at the Coliseum.

demand.explanation: Pole vault finals with Duplantis are a sellout draw, and the debut relay adds further pull.

scorecard.overall: Monday night's pole vault final with Duplantis, plus the debut mixed 4x100m relay, makes this a must-see session. The 800m and 1500m rounds give middle-distance fans a second layer.

significance.explanation: Qualifying and Round 1 heats across several events. Advancement is the stake, not medals.

experience.explanation: Tuesday morning start at the Coliseum. The hurdles and steeplechase water jump add color to a quieter card.

starPower.explanation: Early-round sprints and hurdles may include top athletes, though most headliners wait for the semifinals.

uniqueness.explanation: Routine qualifying and heats in a standard format, with the venue doing most of the work.

demand.explanation: Morning heats draw specialists and families, with seats easier to find than in the evening finals.

scorecard.overall: Tuesday morning qualifying and first rounds: women's pole vault and men's triple jump qualifying, plus heats in the 400m, 110m hurdles and steeplechase. Accessible, close-up action for detail-focused fans.

significance.explanation: Four medal finals in one evening, including the women's 800m and 5000m. Gold-medal stakes across the card.

experience.explanation: Evening session at the Coliseum with four finals across the infield and track. The 800m bend should be loud.

starPower.explanation: Chebet is out and Kipyegon is absent, but the men's high jump and 800m fields bring recognizable names.

uniqueness.explanation: Four finals and two semifinals in one night is a rich card, though the format is familiar.

demand.explanation: Multiple finals on a marquee evening at the Coliseum keep this in high demand.

scorecard.overall: Tuesday evening with four finals: women's 800m, women's 5000m, men's high jump and men's discus. A long, varied card at the Coliseum where the 800m final should bring the loudest roar.

significance.explanation: Women's steeplechase final is the one medal decided, with qualifying and repechage rounds around it.

experience.explanation: Wednesday morning at the Coliseum. The water jump is a highlight, but the energy stays low before prime time.

starPower.explanation: Steeplechase final with mid-tier names, plus qualifying with few headliners.

uniqueness.explanation: Standard steeplechase final and qualifying rounds in familiar formats.

demand.explanation: A single final at a famous venue draws steady interest, though the morning slot keeps seats easier to find.

scorecard.overall: Wednesday morning with the women's steeplechase final and qualifying in the men's hammer and women's long jump. A quieter session with one medal, suited to fans who enjoy messier racing.

significance.explanation: Men's 1500m final headlines a night that also decides the 400m hurdles, long jump and discus medals.

experience.explanation: Evening session at the Coliseum with the 1500m bell and hurdles finish. A packed stadium should lift the crowd.

starPower.explanation: Ingebrigtsen, Kerr and Hocker headline the 1500m, while Benjamin and Warholm lead the 400m hurdles.

uniqueness.explanation: Two of the sport's best races on one night at the Coliseum, though the format is standard.

demand.explanation: Marquee 1500m and 400m hurdles finals at the Coliseum keep this among the top tickets.

scorecard.overall: Wednesday evening features the men's 1500m and 400m hurdles finals, with women's discus and men's long jump medals also decided. Two of the sport's marquee races headline a packed Coliseum night.

significance.explanation: Men's steeplechase final is the one medal event, with qualifying and Round 1 heats around it.

experience.explanation: Thursday morning session at the Coliseum. The water jump adds drama, but the crowd builds slowly.

starPower.explanation: Steeplechase final with names like El Bakkali in the field, though the qualifying rounds draw fewer headliners.

uniqueness.explanation: Standard steeplechase final with routine qualifying rounds.

demand.explanation: Single morning final at a famous venue. Steady interest, with seats easier to book than the evening sessions.

scorecard.overall: Thursday morning with the men's steeplechase final, plus qualifying in women's javelin and high jump and Round 1 of the men's 800m. Laid back and close to the field action, with the steeplechase as the one medal.

significance.explanation: Three medal finals in one evening, including the women's pole vault and women's 400m hurdles.

experience.explanation: Evening session at the Coliseum where pole vault crowds are often among the loudest of the week.

starPower.explanation: McLaughlin-Levrone is out and Bol has moved to the 800m, but the 400m and 200m semis keep recognizable names in play.

uniqueness.explanation: Three finals and four semifinals on one night at the Coliseum, though each event follows a standard format.

demand.explanation: Multiple medal finals on a prime evening at the Coliseum keep this in strong demand.

scorecard.overall: Thursday evening with three medal finals: women's pole vault, men's hammer and women's 400m hurdles, plus semifinals in the 400m and 200m. Field and track drama packed into one session, with the pole vault crowd setting the tone.

significance.explanation: Men's triple jump final is the one medal event, with the heptathlon opening alongside it.

experience.explanation: Friday morning at the Coliseum. Good for the open bowl and the triple jump, though prime-time energy is absent.

starPower.explanation: Triple jump final with Díaz and Pichardo-level names, while the 5000m heats add Ingebrigtsen-level names.

uniqueness.explanation: Single final with heptathlon openers and early rounds in a standard format.

demand.explanation: Morning session with one final and a multi-event opener. Interest is steady, and seats are easier than the evening finals.

scorecard.overall: Friday morning opens the women's heptathlon and decides the men's triple jump final, with 5000m and 100m hurdles first rounds and an 800m repechage. A good session for fans who like variety.

significance.explanation: Men's 200m final is a gold-medal sprint decider, with the 10,000m and 110m hurdles medals also on the card.

experience.explanation: Friday night 200m final at the Coliseum. The bend will be loud as the sprinters come off it.

starPower.explanation: Bednarek and Tebogo headline the 200m, with Jefferson-Wooden and Chebet-era distance names around the card.

uniqueness.explanation: Men's 200m final at the Coliseum with a live rivalry, alongside three finals on one night.

demand.explanation: Finals night with the men's 200m and a 10,000m final. Among the hardest sessions to book.

scorecard.overall: Friday night with the men's 200m final, the women's 10,000m and the men's 110m hurdles final. Bednarek and Tebogo carry the headline sprint, with the 10,000m offering a longer build around the stadium.

significance.explanation: Men's 400m and women's 200m finals headline a day with four gold-medal decisions. Peak medal stakes on the track.

experience.explanation: Saturday afternoon start at the Coliseum. Heat is a factor, though the four finals keep the stadium lively.

starPower.explanation: Jefferson-Wooden leads the 200m, Hall and the 400m field bring Paris 2024 names, and Hall headlines the heptathlon.

uniqueness.explanation: Four medal finals in one afternoon at the Coliseum, though most individual events follow standard formats.

demand.explanation: Multiple sprint and jump finals in one afternoon keep this among the most sought-after sessions.

scorecard.overall: Saturday afternoon's biggest medal session: women's 200m, men's 400m, women's 400m and long jump finals, plus the heptathlon finish. Jefferson-Wooden and Hall headline a card with four decisions in one afternoon.

significance.explanation: Five medal finals in one afternoon, from the 800m to the 4x100m relay, in the marquee sport at the Coliseum. Few sessions pack this much gold.

experience.explanation: Late-afternoon sun, an open bowl and a tight 800m homestretch. Not quite the evening-lights peak, but the Coliseum on a finals day is hard to beat.

starPower.explanation: Wanyonyi, Sedjati and Arop in a rematch of the closest world final in years, plus Mahuchikh in the high jump and Yan Ziyi in the javelin. Relay anchors add sprint heat.

uniqueness.explanation: Medal finals at the Coliseum are special, but this is one of several finals days. The 800m photo-finish potential and the defending Canadian relay title add real texture.

demand.explanation: Five golds on a Sunday at the Coliseum make this one of the hottest tickets in the sport. Only the opening-night sprint session and the final stadium day compete.

scorecard.overall: A five-gold Sunday at the Coliseum, anchored by what could be the tightest 800m in Games history. The javelin, the high jump and a relay with a surprise defending champion keep your eyes busy from first call to last.

significance.explanation: Six finals close the stadium program, including the 5000m, the 100m hurdles and both 4x400m relays. It is a gold rush in the marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Last stadium session of track and field means the bowl is primed for a send-off. Late-afternoon light and back-to-back relay finals build the noise lap by lap.

starPower.explanation: Ingebrigtsen against Hocker, hurdles record holder Masai Russell, Tebogo and Botswana against the US, and possibly McLaughlin-Levrone on anchor. Few sessions carry more marquee names.

uniqueness.explanation: The final stadium session at a Coliseum hosting track a third time is a bookend moment. It stops short of a 10 because it is not a ceremony or the single biggest night.

demand.explanation: Closing-day track finals with the rematch of the 5000m and two 4x400m relays. Expect this to be among the toughest tickets of the entire track program.

scorecard.overall: The last stadium session of the Games sends you out with the Ingebrigtsen-Hocker rematch and two relay finals to close. If you want one session to cap the Coliseum's third Games, this is the one.

significance.explanation: Two gold medals decided back-to-back, straight finals with no heats. Athletics is a marquee sport, but race walk sits a notch below the track finals in the pecking order.

experience.explanation: Free-flowing road course at 7:30 a.m., with venue still unannounced. Watching walkers pass and re-pass on a loop is a great street-side party, if less seat-and-spectacle than the Coliseum.

starPower.explanation: María Pérez arrives as world-record holder, with Paris champions Yang Jiayu and Brian Pintado also in the mix. Big names within the sport, though not household ones worldwide.

uniqueness.explanation: Debut of the 21.1 km distance at the Games, replacing the 20 km walk. Two medal events in one morning on a road course, and the mixed relay is gone, so this is the lone walking session.

demand.explanation: Free-roaming morning road event with two golds, but it doesn't carry the pull of the track finals. Expect interest, and a comparatively easier ticket among athletics sessions.

scorecard.overall: Pérez's world-record debut at the distance headlines the first-ever half-marathon walks, with two golds up for grabs before lunch. It's a street-side morning for genuine fans, and a chance to see a brand-new Games event at its start.

significance.explanation: A single-race gold-medal final in the sport's oldest distance event. Athletics is a marquee sport, and the marathon title is one of the Games' signature prizes.

experience.explanation: Roadside viewing on the Venice boardwalk at 7:15 a.m. has real beach-scene charm, but there are no stadium seats, the finish and route are unannounced, and you see only the start.

starPower.explanation: Paris champion Hassan, Assefa and Tesfay, with her 2:10:51 debut, are all in the mix. Injuries cloud who will actually show up, but the field is deep with global names.

uniqueness.explanation: The Games have never visited Venice Beach, and a marathon start on the boardwalk is a one-off pairing of iconic setting and medal stakes. The open question is how much of the race you can actually see.

demand.explanation: Free-roaming roadside spots and an early start soften competition, though the Venice setting and final-weekend timing still pull a crowd. A gold-medal athletics event keeps it from being easy.

scorecard.overall: Nobody can say who the favorite is, with Assefa and Hassan both nursing Achilles trouble and Tesfay emerging. Go for the Venice Beach sunrise and an open race; just know you'll catch the start, not the finish.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal marathon final that closes the entire athletics program on the last morning. It is a defining medal of the Games in a marquee sport.

experience.explanation: A beachfront start with palms, Pacific and boardwalk buzz makes for a great atmosphere at 7:15 a.m. You get a roadside moment, not a stadium view, and the finish location is still unknown.

starPower.explanation: Caitlin Clark, Jackie Young and Breanna Stewart are marquee names, and Spain's Iyana Martin adds a rising star.

uniqueness.explanation: A late semifinal with the gold game at stake adds drama. It's still a standard format in an established sport.

demand.explanation: Prime-time women's semifinal with the US star power. Likely one of the hardest women's tickets before the final.

scorecard.overall: The late semifinal is the women's tournament at its most electric, with big names and a late tip. If you can't get the gold game, this is the next best women's ticket.

significance.explanation: Men's semifinal in a marquee sport. The winner is one game from gold, the loser drops to bronze.

experience.explanation: A 4 PM semifinal at the Dome, full house and The Wall in voice. Great basketball, just short of the prime-time glow.

starPower.explanation: The post-LeBron US team and Wembanyama's France are the central draws. NBA names fill the semifinal field.

uniqueness.explanation: A men's semifinal, with a new US generation and a possible France rematch. Memorable, but one of two semis the same day.

demand.explanation: Men's semifinal basketball is among the hottest tickets at the Games. The afternoon slot is only marginally easier.

scorecard.overall: The first men's semifinal shows a changing of the guard, with the US trying to hold off Wembanyama and the field. Slightly more accessible than the night game, but still a major ticket.

significance.explanation: Late men's semifinal with a sixth straight US title in sight. The loser plays for bronze.

experience.explanation: A 9:30 PM semifinal under the lights, with The Wall roaring. Peak knockout basketball at a purpose-built arena.

starPower.explanation: NBA stars from the US, Wembanyama's France, and other top contenders make this the biggest night of men's names before the final.

uniqueness.explanation: A late semifinal where a surprise could upend the US-France storyline. Strong drama, but not the final.

demand.explanation: Prime-time men's semifinal is among the top tickets in the sport, trailing only the gold medal game.

scorecard.overall: The nightcap semifinal is the best men's ticket outside the final: big names, loud arena and a possible US-France collision. If you want one men's night in the Dome, this is it.

significance.explanation: A women's bronze medal is on the line. The semifinal losers get a final chance at the podium.

experience.explanation: Friday 4 PM at the Dome has a looser mood, with great sightlines and a full arena. Less tension, still strong hoops.

starPower.explanation: Top European and Australian players likely appear, but the US probably won't. Strong names, just short of marquee.

uniqueness.explanation: A bronze game in an established sport. The relaxed tone is its own flavor, but the format is routine.

demand.explanation: A medal game in a hot sport, but without the US final. An easier ticket than the semifinals.

scorecard.overall: The value pick of the women's schedule: a medal game, a loose atmosphere and real talent without the final's price. Best for fans who want a medal moment without the biggest crowd.

significance.explanation: A men's bronze medal decides the podium. Pride and a medal are at stake for two semifinal losers.

experience.explanation: Saturday noon at Intuit Dome has a relaxed vibe, with a looser game and a good view. Daytime tip tempers the energy.

starPower.explanation: France with Wembanyama could land here, or Serbia with its stars. NBA-level talent fills both rosters.

uniqueness.explanation: A bronze game is a standard format. A Wembanyama-led France chasing a medal would add a special touch.

demand.explanation: A men's medal game at the Games is a sought ticket, though less so than the final or semifinal night.

scorecard.overall: A hungry France or a repeat-minded Serbia plays for a medal in a looser setting. It's a more affordable shot at men's medal basketball than Sunday's final.

significance.explanation: Women's gold medal game, with the US chasing a ninth straight title. Marquee sport, medal decided, no further rounds.

experience.explanation: Gold medal basketball at Intuit Dome, with 4,500 on The Wall and the halo board overhead. The best women's ticket of the Games.

starPower.explanation: A'ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart, Caitlin Clark and a possible France rematch. The brightest names in women's hoops on one floor.

uniqueness.explanation: A ninth straight US gold on home soil is a historic streak. The setting is brand-new, but it isn't a one-time-only venue pairing.

demand.explanation: The women's gold medal game is the top women's ticket and a sell-out certainty. Expect the hardest seats in the sport.

scorecard.overall: This is the women's tournament's crown jewel, with the US seeking a ninth consecutive gold at home. If you can get in, you're seeing history made.

significance.explanation: Men's gold medal game, a few hours before the Closing Ceremony. The ultimate prize in a marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Final day, the gold game, The Wall and the halo board at full tilt. The best seat in the basketball schedule.

starPower.explanation: Wembanyama against a young US team featuring names like Flagg and Holmgren. The sport's brightest names on the final stage.

uniqueness.explanation: A sixth straight US title versus Wembanyama's France, on closing day. Few basketball games carry this much once-only weight.

demand.explanation: The men's basketball final is the ticket of the Games. Expect it to be the hardest basketball seat to land.

scorecard.overall: A sixth straight US title versus Wembanyama's France on the final day of the Games. If you get one basketball ticket, this is the one, with the Closing Ceremony hours later.

significance.explanation: Qualification only: twelve spots per gender, no medals. One bailed tailwhip ends a campaign, so the stakes are real even without hardware.

experience.explanation: Late-July morning at a temporary open-air park in the Sepulveda Basin. Riders are fresh and the tricks are big, but it lacks prime-time atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Sun Sibei, Rimu Nakamura and Anthony Jeanjean are the names in the field, and Paris champion Deng Yawen could be here too. Real BMX stars, though not mainstream household names.

uniqueness.explanation: Third Games appearance for the discipline, in the Southern California heartland of BMX culture. Still a qualifying round, so the novelty outweighs the rarity of the event itself.

demand.explanation: Qualifying morning at a temporary venue, so an easier ticket than the final. Still part of a Games where scarcity is the rule.

scorecard.overall: Come see every rider in the field before the pressure peaks, and watch a podium contender crash out in real time. A cheaper way into BMX in its Southern California home, with the medal drama saved for Saturday.

significance.explanation: Two gold medals decided in one session. BMX isn't a marquee sport, but a double-final session still carries serious stakes.

experience.explanation: Two 60-second runs per rider means constant action and crowd noise at an open-air park. The 10:30 AM start and temporary venue keep it a notch below an evening session.

starPower.explanation: Sun Sibei and Hannah Roberts on the women's side, Nakamura, Jeanjean and Kieran Reilly on the men's. Top names in action sports, if not mainstream stars.

uniqueness.explanation: Two golds at the third Games for the sport, in the birthplace of BMX culture. Standard format at a temporary venue, but the pairing of place and stakes is hard to repeat.

demand.explanation: Medal session of a mid-tier sport. Expect competition for seats, though less than the marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: One clean run can decide a medal, and Paris showed how thin the margins are, with the men's podium split by barely a point. Two golds in three hours, in BMX's home region, makes this the best action-sports ticket of the week.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinals and last chance runs: real elimination stakes for every rider, but no medals change hands and the pressure peaks the next day.

experience.explanation: Mid-morning sun on a temporary dirt course in the Sepulveda Basin. Short heats keep the action constant, though the venue is a smaller stage than a stadium.

starPower.explanation: Shriever, Sakakibara, Smulders and a deep French men's squad should all be on the gate, since every top rider has to come through these rounds.

uniqueness.explanation: One of two BMX sessions at a standard-format event at a generic temporary venue. The Valley's first Games hosting adds a touch of local color.

demand.explanation: Early-round BMX at a temporary park venue should be the easier ticket in the sport, though Games scarcity still means it will likely sell.

scorecard.overall: The scouting-report session: see the whole field, a few favorites sweating through last chance runs, and a cheaper way into BMX in its Southern California home. The medals wait a day.

significance.explanation: Two gold-medal finals plus the bronze and silver on the line in one session, with semifinals first. Three-plus medal events puts it near the top for a non-marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Semifinals into finals under the late-morning sun, with eight riders and one gate. Under a minute per race gives nonstop payoff, even on a temporary course.

starPower.explanation: Shriever, a four-time world champion, Paris gold medalist Sakakibara and Smulders on one side. On the other, France's Pilard and Rencurel, plus the chance of Daudet.

uniqueness.explanation: BMX medals decided in the sport's home region, in the Valley's first Games hosting. A possible Sakakibara and Mahieu sequel adds a story.

demand.explanation: Medal-day BMX is the sport's hottest ticket, and a Sunday-morning finals slot should draw well. It trails marquee finals, but expect it to sell.

scorecard.overall: Two golds in under three hours, with France's men looking to repeat the Paris sweep and a tight women's field. It's chaotic, loud and fast, and the best way to see BMX where it was born.

significance.explanation: Round-of-32 bouts mostly, with a +90kg round of 16 as the sharpest edge. One loss ends a tournament, but no medal is guaranteed yet.

experience.explanation: Noon start in an award-show theater where every seat faces one raised ring. Clean sightlines, but daytime energy and early rounds keep it modest.

starPower.explanation: Aibek Oralbay, the reigning world champion at +90kg, could appear, and Japan's Rui Yamaguchi is in the 55kg mix. Mostly specialist names, though.

uniqueness.explanation: Opening boxing session of the Games, the sport's return, and the first time Peacock Theater hosts medal-level sport. Still early rounds, so it stops short of the top tier.

demand.explanation: Opening-day novelty and a downtown location help. Early-round boxing at a 7,100-seat theater is a softer ask than the medal sessions.

scorecard.overall: Be there for the first bell of boxing's return, not for the stakes. Big heavyweights and a ring on a stage make a quirky, memorable debut at an easier price of admission.

significance.explanation: Same early bracket slate as the noon session: round-of-32 survival and a +90kg round of 16. Elimination stakes, no medals locked.

experience.explanation: Saturday night under stage lights, with the ring as the only thing lit. Evening crowd energy lifts it over the noon card.

starPower.explanation: Lin Yu-ting at 60kg would be the draw, with Oralbay and Jalolov's shadow over the heavies. The names are not guaranteed to appear.

uniqueness.explanation: Opening-day evening of boxing's return, with the Paris 2024 gender-row storyline hovering over any Lin bout. Early-round, but charged.

demand.explanation: Saturday primetime on opening weekend downtown is the hottest ticket of the early-round slots.

scorecard.overall: The better of the two opening-day sessions: Saturday night, a rowdy room, and the chance of Lin Yu-ting walking in. Early rounds, but with real atmosphere.

significance.explanation: Round-of-32 bouts and a pair of rounds of 16. Eliminations, with the medal rounds still days away.

experience.explanation: Sunday lunchtime at a theater with tiered seating facing one ring. Good sightlines, quiet-ish daytime mood.

starPower.explanation: Wu Yu, Paris 2024 flyweight champion and world number one, could open her defense here, with Nikhat Zareen and world champion Turabek Khabibullaev adding depth.

uniqueness.explanation: One of many prelim cards in boxing's return week. The Wu Yu possibility gives it a little extra spark.

demand.explanation: Sunday and a champion's possible debut make this an easier but still popular ticket.

scorecard.overall: A Sunday-lunch chance to see Paris champion Wu Yu start her defense and a reigning world champion at 90kg. Early rounds, but a rich bracket.

significance.explanation: Round-of-32 and round-of-16 bouts. Everyone fights to avoid elimination, no medal guaranteed yet.

experience.explanation: Sunday night run past ten, with the room warmed up and the ring lit. Theater sightlines are the same for everyone.

starPower.explanation: Turabek Khabibullaev, the reigning 90kg world champion, plus Wu Yu and Paris bronze medalist Aira Villegas in the 51kg pool.

uniqueness.explanation: A mid-week-style prelim card, but Sunday night in the first boxing week gives it a bit more event feel.

demand.explanation: Evening slot and a recognizable 51kg cast make it more sought-after than the daytime cards.

scorecard.overall: Sunday-night boxing with a world champion at 90kg and Wu Yu's 51kg bracket in play. An evening prelim with real bite and a late finish.

significance.explanation: Round of 16 with a quarterfinal berth, one win from a guaranteed bronze, on the line. Closer to the medals than the opening rounds.

experience.explanation: Monday lunchtime at Peacock, with clean views of the ring. Daytime keeps the volume lower.

starPower.explanation: Lin Yu-ting and Kellie Harrington both fought at 60kg in 2026, two Paris champions who say they want to be here.

uniqueness.explanation: A possible Lin and Harrington collision in the same weight class is rare. Still a round of 16, so it is not a medal bout.

demand.explanation: Two household boxing names in one division pushes interest up even for a Monday lunch.

scorecard.overall: If the draw is kind, you could catch two Paris champions at 60kg in the same building. A knockout-round lunch with a famous cast.

significance.explanation: Round of 16, where a win puts a boxer one fight from a guaranteed bronze. Real pressure, no medal yet.

experience.explanation: Monday evening session running past ten, with the ring lit and a crowd that has settled into the format.

starPower.explanation: Harrington's bid for a third straight gold and Lin Yu-ting's return headline, with Rui Yamaguchi and Carlo Paalam at 55kg.

uniqueness.explanation: Harrington chasing a rare third title is a real story. Round-of-16 stage keeps it below the medal bouts.

demand.explanation: Evening slot plus two star names make this one of the more competitive early tickets.

scorecard.overall: The evening twin of a potential Harrington versus Lin card, with a rare three-peat on the line. Monday night boxing with a real storyline.

significance.explanation: +90kg quarterfinals guarantee a medal to the winners. The rest of the card is earlier-round work.

experience.explanation: Tuesday lunch at Peacock, with heavyweights as the main course. Great sightlines, subdued daytime mood.

starPower.explanation: Aibek Oralbay, the world champion, headlines the heavies. Jalolov's status is unconfirmed, and world champions at 54kg and 57kg sit in the draw.

uniqueness.explanation: Quarterfinal medal-clinching bouts among the biggest men in boxing, with a possible three-gold chase in the background.

demand.explanation: Weekday lunch is the easier slot, though medal-clinching heavyweights still draw interest.

scorecard.overall: Heavyweights fighting to lock in a medal, at lunchtime on a Tuesday. A solid, easier-to-get ticket for fans who like power.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinal winners at +90kg walk away with at least a bronze. Other bouts are rounds of 16 and 32.

experience.explanation: Tuesday night in the theater, with big men throwing big punches under the lights.

starPower.explanation: Oralbay's rivals and Jalolov's knockdown-fueled return story, plus Asian Games gold medalist Ankush Panghal at 80kg.

uniqueness.explanation: Medal-clinching heavyweight quarterfinals in an evening slot. A bit of a special feel for a midweek card.

demand.explanation: Evening heavyweights are an easy sell, and the crowd should be full.

scorecard.overall: Big-man boxing under the lights, with bronze medals decided in the heavyweight quarters. A fine Tuesday-night pick for power punchers.

significance.explanation: Women's 60kg and 70kg quarterfinals guarantee bronze medals to the winners. Men's rounds of 16 fill out the card.

experience.explanation: Wednesday lunchtime with a medal-clinching atmosphere. Good sightlines, smaller daytime crowd energy.

starPower.explanation: Lin Yu-ting and Kellie Harrington could both be in the 60kg quarterfinals, and Abdumalik Khalokov is in the men's draw.

uniqueness.explanation: A medal-clinching round with two Paris champions possibly in the same bracket is uncommon.

demand.explanation: Marquee women's names and guaranteed medals make this a tougher book than the early rounds.

scorecard.overall: A midday card where quarterfinal wins mean medals and two Paris champions may still be alive at 60kg. Worth a lunch break.

significance.explanation: Women's quarterfinals at 60kg and 70kg clinch medals. The men's 60kg and 70kg rounds of 16 are a notch down.

experience.explanation: Wednesday night theater boxing, with lights on the ring and a medal-minded crowd.

starPower.explanation: Lin Yu-ting, Harrington, and Paris champion Abdumalik Khalokov all could appear across the bracket.

uniqueness.explanation: Khalokov's first look at 60kg and a possible Lin-Harrington path make this card more than routine.

demand.explanation: Evening quarterfinals with star names pull stronger demand than the daytime twin.

scorecard.overall: The better Wednesday: women's medal-clinching quarters with Lin and Harrington potentially on the same bill as Khalokov's debut at 60kg.

significance.explanation: Men's 65kg and 90kg quarterfinals lock in bronze for the winners, with women's rounds of 16 around them.

experience.explanation: Thursday matinee at Peacock. Close-up views of the ring, but a daytime atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Wu Yu, world champions Alua Balkibekova and Aida Abikeyeva, and Asian Games gold medalist Parveen Hooda form a deep women's cast.

uniqueness.explanation: A world champion and a world number one possibly in the same 51kg draw makes the matinee more than routine.

demand.explanation: Weekday daytime is a softer ask, though the champions in the draw keep interest healthy.

scorecard.overall: A Thursday matinee with a real 51kg puzzle: the reigning world champion against the Paris champion and world number one.

significance.explanation: Round-of-16 eliminations and men's quarterfinals that guarantee a bronze make for a tense mix.

experience.explanation: Thursday night in a packed theater with a quarterfinal edge, and bouts running past ten.

starPower.explanation: Wu Yu, Aira Villegas, Aida Abikeyeva and Turabek Khabibullaev span the card.

uniqueness.explanation: Deep women's 65kg field and 51kg storylines give this evening more flavor than a typical prelim.

demand.explanation: Evening quarterfinals with multiple champions should be one of the harder-to-book weeknights.

scorecard.overall: Thursday evening has a deep women's 65kg round and a fierce 90kg quarterfinal. Lean forward, because medals start getting decided.

significance.explanation: Men's 55kg and 80kg quarterfinals clinch bronze for the winners, and the women's rounds of 16 sit just below.

experience.explanation: Friday lunchtime at Peacock, with a clean view and a daytime crowd.

starPower.explanation: Julia Szeremeta, Jaismine Lamboria, Lovlina Borgohain, Aoife O'Rourke and Ankush Panghal bring a strong cast.

uniqueness.explanation: A possible Szeremeta-Jaismine rematch carries weight, while quarterfinal stakes add to the card.

demand.explanation: Friday lunch is easier to get, but the champions on the card keep it popular.

scorecard.overall: A Friday lunch with a possible 57kg rematch between two recent final opponents and medal-clinching men's quarters. A smart daytime pick.

significance.explanation: Men's quarterfinals at 55kg and 80kg lock in at least a bronze. Women's rounds of 16 sit just beneath.

experience.explanation: Friday night at Peacock, with the weekend nearly here and a crowd ready to roar.

starPower.explanation: Panghal, Javokhir Ummataliev, Khyzhniak, Lovlina Borgohain: a solid mix of champions.

uniqueness.explanation: An 80kg bracket with a surprise Asian Games champion, a world champion and a Paris gold medalist feels special.

demand.explanation: Friday evening quarterfinals with champions in the draw are a hotter ticket.

scorecard.overall: Friday night quarterfinals with an upset-minded 80kg bracket and Lovlina Borgohain in the women's rounds. A strong late-week pick.

significance.explanation: Men's +90kg and women's 70kg semifinals send winners to gold-medal bouts, with several quarterfinals also clinching bronze.

experience.explanation: Saturday lunchtime with a stacked card, before medal rounds move to DTLA Arena. Long and rewarding session.

starPower.explanation: Oralbay, possibly Jalolov, Wu Yu, Huang Hsiao-wen, Balkibekova, Abikeyeva and Parveen Hooda crowd the card.

uniqueness.explanation: Last Peacock session before the arena move, with semifinal-level heavyweight boxing. Still short of a final.

demand.explanation: Semifinals, a stacked Saturday and the final Peacock card make this the hardest ticket in the venue.

scorecard.overall: The best card Peacock Theater offers: heavyweight semifinals, a stacked list of champions and the last look at this ring before the medal rounds move on.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinals plus two semifinals where losers still take bronze. Medals start getting locked in, but no gold is awarded tonight.

experience.explanation: Saturday night, 7,100 seats all facing one raised ring, and a card stacked with eight-plus bouts. Boxing in a theater setting feels like fight night.

starPower.explanation: Bakhodir Jalolov, two-time super-heavyweight champion and unbeaten pro, is the draw if he's in the field. Asian Games medalists and world-level names fill out the rest.

uniqueness.explanation: Boxing's return after a governance fight and a first-ever Games at an awards-show theater give it novelty, though these are still early medal rounds.

demand.explanation: Saturday prime time, a long multi-weight card, and a possible Jalolov appearance make this one of the hotter boxing tickets before finals.

scorecard.overall: Prime-time Saturday boxing in an awards-show theater, with a chance to see Jalolov chase a third straight title. Eight-plus bouts mean quarterfinal chaos and bronze-clinching drama, all up close.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinal wins at 57kg and 75kg guarantee a bronze, and the men's 55kg semifinal sends two boxers to a gold-medal bout.

experience.explanation: A noon start is lower on atmosphere than a Saturday night card, but the theater's sightlines and air conditioning make it comfortable, and the session wraps early.

starPower.explanation: Paris silver medalist Julia Szeremeta, world champion Jaismine Lamboria and Paris middleweight champion Li Qian headline a strong list of names.

uniqueness.explanation: A possible world-final rematch at 57kg adds spice, and boxing in a theater is new, but these are still not the finals.

demand.explanation: Sunday midday is an easier slot than the night cards, yet medal-clinching bouts and the sport's return keep interest high.

scorecard.overall: A great midday pick if you want medal-clinching bouts and a possible Lamboria-Szeremeta rematch without giving up your evening. It lacks the weight of a Saturday-night crowd but has plenty of real stakes.

significance.explanation: One women's 70kg final, plus three semifinals where a win locks in silver. Real medal stakes, but only a single gold is handed out at midday.

experience.explanation: Noon start at DTLA Arena. The steep bowl puts upper rows right over the ring, though daytime semis lack the prime-time buzz.

starPower.explanation: Wu Yu and Parveen Hooda are the draws, with Turabek Khabibullaev lurking at 90kg. Strong names, but no marquee headliner.

uniqueness.explanation: Standard boxing semis-and-final card at a generic arena. Good fights, but one of several similar midday sessions.

demand.explanation: A midday session with a single gold is an easier ticket than the evening cards, though it should still sell.

scorecard.overall: The softest-stakes card of the knockout block, but semifinalists fight like finalists with silver on the line. A smart pick for fight fans who want Wu Yu and Hooda without paying evening-card prices.

significance.explanation: Men's 55kg final is the lone gold, flanked by three semifinals with guaranteed medals. Prime-time, but a single title.

experience.explanation: A 6 PM start gives the downtown bowl a night-out feel, with semis building toward the 70kg and 80kg bouts.

starPower.explanation: Makhmud Sabyrkhan, Rui Yamaguchi, Torekhan Sabyrkhan and Zeyad Eashash are strong names to boxing fans, but not household.

uniqueness.explanation: Evening session with an open 55kg title and a likely 70kg rematch. Compelling matchups, though format is routine.

demand.explanation: Evening slot in the knockout phase at a big downtown arena makes this a hotter ticket than the midday sessions.

scorecard.overall: An evening card with an unpredictable 55kg gold and 70kg semis that could play like finals. Good value if you want prime-time boxing before the multi-gold nights.

significance.explanation: Men's +90kg gold is on the line, with two 60kg semifinals guaranteeing medals. One final, but a heavyweight one.

experience.explanation: Friday midday at DTLA Arena. Heavyweight thuds carry in the steep bowl, though daytime lacks evening energy.

starPower.explanation: Lin Yu-ting, Abdumalik Khalokov and possibly Kellie Harrington's weight class, plus the Jalolov question hanging over the heavyweights.

uniqueness.explanation: Lin's 60kg move after her sex-test clearance and a possible Oralbay-Zokirov trilogy give this card real narrative.

demand.explanation: Midday slot with one gold keeps it a bit easier than evening finals, but the names will draw buyers.

scorecard.overall: Heavyweight gold plus the 60kg semis make this the best midday pick of the week. Lin Yu-ting's story and a third Oralbay-Zokirov meeting give it edge.

significance.explanation: Women's 51kg final is the lone gold, with 65kg men's and 75kg women's semis guaranteeing medals.

experience.explanation: Friday evening in downtown LA, with a technical final up top and strong semis. Prime-time atmosphere at a solid venue.

starPower.explanation: Wu Yu, Muydinkhujaev, Erislandy Alvarez, Li Qian and Lovlina Borgohain: a stack of Paris champions and Asian Games winners.

uniqueness.explanation: Two Paris champions on a possible 65kg collision course adds spice, but the card is standard in format.

demand.explanation: Friday night, a final and star-heavy semis. Expect competition for seats.

scorecard.overall: Friday night is stacked with Paris champions: Wu Yu going for gold while Muydinkhujaev and Alvarez circle in the 65kg bracket. One of the best-value evening cards.

significance.explanation: Two gold medals, women's 65kg and men's 90kg, plus 57kg semifinals. Two titles in one sitting lifts the stakes.

experience.explanation: Saturday noon at DTLA Arena. Two finals bring energy, but daytime lacks the nighttime buzz.

starPower.explanation: Khabibullaev is a dominant champion and Hooda is a rising star, though the wide-open 57kg adds anonymity.

uniqueness.explanation: Open 57kg without a defending champion and Hooda's split-decision gold bring intrigue, but nothing special in format.

demand.explanation: Weekend with two golds makes this a competitive ticket, even at midday.

scorecard.overall: Weekend lunchtime with two finals and a dominant 90kg favorite. A great way to see gold-medal boxing without the evening premium.

significance.explanation: Four golds in two hours, led by the women's 60kg title. Few sessions at the Games hand out this much hardware.

experience.explanation: Saturday night in downtown LA at DTLA Arena. Four finals back to back feel like a full fight card.

starPower.explanation: Lin Yu-ting, Kellie Harrington, Viktoriya Grafeyeva, Abdumalik Khalokov and Javokhir Ummataliev. Plenty of recognizable names.

uniqueness.explanation: Lin versus Harrington's division with Grafeyeva in between is a storyline you will not get twice. Four golds in a night.

demand.explanation: Saturday prime time with four finals is the hottest ticket in boxing. Expect it to go fast.

scorecard.overall: The best card of the tournament: four golds, Saturday night, and the women's 60kg final with Lin, Grafeyeva and Harrington in the mix. Book this one first.

significance.explanation: The tournament's last four golds are decided: women's 57kg and 75kg, men's 65kg and 70kg.

experience.explanation: Sunday afternoon at DTLA Arena. Four finals bring energy and closure, though the slot is daytime.

starPower.explanation: Muydinkhujaev, Alvarez, Torekhan Sabyrkhan, Borgohain and Li Qian bring plenty of recognition for boxing fans.

uniqueness.explanation: Closing day of boxing with an open 57kg and a 65kg final that could pair two Paris champions. Memorable, not unprecedented.

demand.explanation: Four golds and the final day of the tournament draw heavy interest, even on a Sunday afternoon.

scorecard.overall: Boxing's farewell gives you four golds and a potential Muydinkhujaev-Alvarez clash at 65kg. Slightly less glamorous than Saturday night, but just as rewarding.

significance.explanation: Opening-round game, so the stakes are seeding and bragging rights. Real, just far from medal-deciding.

experience.explanation: Late-morning sun at Dodger Stadium, with the pastel decks and skyline views. Daytime keeps it relaxed, but it's a ballpark made for this.

starPower.explanation: Rosters are unsettled while MLB participation hangs on union talks. National-team names are likely, though who suits up is still unknown.

uniqueness.explanation: The first pitch of the returning baseball tournament, a day before the Opening Ceremony, in a park that hosted the 1984 demonstration. A true first-inning bragging-rights seat.

demand.explanation: Dodger Stadium plus the tournament's first pitch pulls in curious fans. A late-morning weekday slot makes it a slightly easier get.

scorecard.overall: Be there when the whole 2028 Games throws its first pitch, a day before the Ceremony. It's a low-stakes game with real bragging rights and a rare look at the rosters before the pressure builds.

significance.explanation: Group-stage night game. Seeding matters, but nobody's medal hopes end here.

experience.explanation: Night baseball under the lights at Chavez Ravine, with the hills and skyline behind the outfield. Hard to beat for atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Venezuela's World Baseball Classic champions, with names like Suárez, Abreu and Garcia, could take the field. MLB participation is the open question.

uniqueness.explanation: Venezuela's first-ever Games baseball night, on the eve of the Ceremony. A debut with a champion's pedigree.

demand.explanation: Prime-time ballpark session with a possible USA or Venezuela headliner. Evening slots at Dodger Stadium go fast.
