scorecard.overall: An easy-to-fit day game on the last day of group play, with potential Mooney-led Australia on show. The evening is louder; this is the calmer way in.

significance.explanation: The last group games decide who plays for gold and who for bronze, the most consequential non-medal session.

experience.explanation: Full house under Pomona's evening light, with a crowd knowing the table the moment the toss is done.

starPower.explanation: Last-night billing makes it likely Australia, Great Britain and other leaders are involved; Nat Sciver-Brunt may lead Great Britain.

uniqueness.explanation: A winner-takes-the-table decider in a sport's first Games in 128 years. It's a group game, but a rare one.

demand.explanation: Evening, last-day drama, and a path to medal matches make it the group stage's top ticket.

scorecard.overall: The best group-stage ticket: last chance, loud crowd, and a table that settles the medal matches. If you want drama before the finals, this is it.

significance.explanation: A bronze-medal match, a real medal contested, but one level below the gold match.

experience.explanation: Morning bronze match with real stakes and a close-to-the-boundary setting. A smaller crowd energy than the final.

starPower.explanation: Likely involves two of the sport's leading sides, such as South Africa, India or Great Britain.

uniqueness.explanation: The first cricket medal match at a Summer Games since 1900, so the whole session is historic.

demand.explanation: A medal match in a new sport, with strong curiosity, though behind the gold match.

scorecard.overall: A bronze with history attached: the first Games cricket medal in 128 years. It's a morning game with real stakes and a more attainable ticket than the final.

significance.explanation: The first women's cricket gold medal at a Summer Games, in a sport outside the marquee tier.

experience.explanation: A sold-out Pomona crowd near the boundary for a gold match, though a morning start takes off some prime-time sheen.

starPower.explanation: Australia, with Beth Mooney and seven world titles, are the likely finalist, with England's Nat Sciver-Brunt a possible opponent.

uniqueness.explanation: Inaugural women's gold in a returning sport, a first-of-its-kind moment that will be remembered.

demand.explanation: The top women's cricket ticket and a historic final, though cricket is not a marquee sport in the US market.

scorecard.overall: History on a Thursday morning: the first women's cricket gold of the Games era. Australia are the team to beat, and a rematch with England would add some edge.

significance.explanation: Men's opening group game. It starts the table, but there's a long road to the medal matches.

experience.explanation: A Saturday-morning opener with a buzzing crowd, close seats and the sport's global fans present.

starPower.explanation: Defending T20 world champions India, a likely hosts US side, and England and Australia in the mix, so major men's names are likely.

uniqueness.explanation: Opens the men's Games tournament, the first in 128 years, with India and the host side among the draws.

demand.explanation: Saturday timing and India's global following make this the strongest group-stage demand of the morning slots.

scorecard.overall: The men's tournament starts on a Saturday morning with India, the world champions, as the story. A group-stage seat, but one with the biggest crowd and star pull.

significance.explanation: Group-stage opener in a six-team field, so every result matters early, but no medal is decided.

experience.explanation: Evening start in Pomona with cooler air and a close-to-the-rope 10,000-seat ground. Opening-day buzz helps.

starPower.explanation: Top-ranked T20 nations are in the field, though which stars appear depends on who qualifies.

uniqueness.explanation: Cricket's first Games men's match since 1900 is the draw. Early round, but the return itself gives it a special feel.

demand.explanation: Opening-night curiosity and a passionate cricket diaspora make this a sought-after seat, even without medals at stake.

scorecard.overall: The first men's cricket under Games lights in 128 years, with sixes landing near your seat. A group match, not a final, but opening-night novelty makes it the best entry point for curious fans.

significance.explanation: Early group match; teams are still feeling out the format and nothing is decided yet.

experience.explanation: Sunday 9 a.m. start under climbing inland sun. Pleasant for devotees, less atmospheric than an evening slot.

starPower.explanation: India or South Africa could be on the field, and either brings recognizable names to a morning slot.

uniqueness.explanation: Early-round cricket in a returning sport; novelty carries it more than the stakes.

demand.explanation: Morning session is an easier ticket, though Sunday timing and India's fan base will fill plenty of seats.

scorecard.overall: A relaxed Sunday-morning way to see the sport's return, with a good chance of India or South Africa on the field. Pick it for easier logistics and a first taste of T20.

significance.explanation: Group-stage match; Great Britain has time to recover from a slip, so stakes are real but not final.

experience.explanation: Sunday evening start puts the heat behind you, and a short boundary rewards big hitters.

starPower.explanation: Brook and Buttler headline a Great Britain side that holds the world number one ranking.

uniqueness.explanation: Early round, but a world number one side in a sport's return gives it extra pull.

demand.explanation: Sunday prime-time slot with Britain's travelling support makes this one of the group stage's warmer tickets.

scorecard.overall: Great Britain's powerhouse batters on a Sunday night at a ground built for sixes. If you want the group stage's best pairing of star power and a good time slot, start here.

significance.explanation: Group play with the field still taking shape; real stakes for advancement, but no medal on the line.

experience.explanation: Monday 9 a.m. start means a smaller, cricket-savvy crowd and a quieter atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Lineups depend on the qualifier, so big names are possible but not guaranteed.

uniqueness.explanation: Early-round returning sport, with some intrigue over who emerged from the qualifier.

demand.explanation: Weekday morning slot is the softer ticket in the men's schedule, though still a Games seat.

scorecard.overall: A weekday-morning session for people who want to see who won the last-chance qualifier. Easier on the wallet and the crowds, with less star wattage.

significance.explanation: Last men's first-round session; group positions begin to form but nothing is final.

experience.explanation: Monday evening under the lights at a ground where the Knight Riders' fans already know how to make noise.

starPower.explanation: Depends on the draw; if the US or Australia appears, familiar faces will be on show.

uniqueness.explanation: A possible host-nation debut in a returning sport gives it an American-story angle.

demand.explanation: Evening slot and home-team interest make it more competitive than the morning games.

scorecard.overall: The best chance of a home-crowd moment in the group stage, with the United States potentially facing a heavyweight. An upset would be loud, and evening light helps.

significance.explanation: Second-round group match; teams are jockeying for knockout positions but no medal is decided.

experience.explanation: Tuesday 9 a.m. start gives a clear view of the table forming, with a smaller morning crowd.

starPower.explanation: India, Britain, Australia or South Africa could be on show, though pairings are not set.

uniqueness.explanation: Mid-group round in a returning sport, special mainly for being at the Games.

demand.explanation: Weekday morning is a more accessible slot, though the sport's novelty keeps interest healthy.

scorecard.overall: A good morning for watching the table take shape, with a chance to see India's new-look squad. A workmanlike pick for fans, not a marquee one.

significance.explanation: Second-round evening match with group seeding tightening, so each result has more weight.

experience.explanation: Tuesday evening under softer light with batters swinging close to the boundary rope.

starPower.explanation: England and India, the top two ranked sides, are projected to be in the field.

uniqueness.explanation: Group-stage cricket with a possible India-England storyline, but not a one-off moment.

demand.explanation: Evening slot with the biggest names projected makes it a stronger ticket than the day sessions.

scorecard.overall: If the rankings hold, this is the evening to see whether England's rise over India is real. Prime-time light and top-two teams make it one of the better group tickets.

significance.explanation: Group match with advancement at stake; the format means any slip can matter.

experience.explanation: Wednesday 9 a.m. is a quieter, cricket-first crowd, with a short boundary providing action.

starPower.explanation: Lineups are unsettled until qualification ends, so star appearances are a coin flip.

uniqueness.explanation: A returning sport's mid-group round, with upset potential giving it a little spark.

demand.explanation: Midweek morning is among the easier tickets in the men's schedule.

scorecard.overall: A midweek morning for fans who value close finishes over star billing. T20 allows upsets, and a one-run thriller here would be a story to tell.

significance.explanation: Evening second-round match with group positions firming up and knockout places in view.

experience.explanation: Wednesday 6 p.m. is cricket's best slot here: cooler air, a building crowd and sixes into the stands.

starPower.explanation: India's two-time world champions are the headline if they land in this session.

uniqueness.explanation: Group cricket in a returning sport, lifted by the Shreyas Iyer storyline.

demand.explanation: Prime-time slot and India's huge fan base make seats competitive.

scorecard.overall: Evening cricket with a possible India redemption arc under a new captain. Check the card before booking, but this slot has the best atmosphere of the midweek group games.

significance.explanation: Penultimate day of group play, where results start to decide who reaches the medal matches.

experience.explanation: Thursday 9 a.m. under the Pomona sun; tense table, but a daytime crowd.

starPower.explanation: By now the stronger sides are fighting for places, so recognizable names are likely.

uniqueness.explanation: A late group round of a returning sport with the table taking its final shape.

demand.explanation: Morning slot is easier, though the higher stakes lift interest above earlier days.

scorecard.overall: The morning where group scenarios get real, with sides fighting for medal-match spots. A good pick for tension without the evening crowd.

significance.explanation: Final group night decides who plays for medals on July 28 and 29, so every run counts.

experience.explanation: Thursday evening with extra tension, a full crowd and the best light of the day.

starPower.explanation: With the table on the line, top sides like England, India and Australia are likely to feature.

uniqueness.explanation: Last group session before the medals, with elimination pressure unique to this night.

demand.explanation: Prime-time slot on the last group night is the hardest group-stage ticket to land.

scorecard.overall: The final group night, where a bad over can end a medal hope. It is the group stage's pressure cooker, in the best evening slot, and the one to book if you only pick one.

significance.explanation: A bronze-medal match: two teams that just missed gold playing for a medal rather than going home empty-handed.

experience.explanation: Friday 9 a.m. under the sun with a medal at stake, though less buzz than the gold match.

starPower.explanation: Late-stage teams will include at least one heavyweight, with names depending on the knockouts.

uniqueness.explanation: The first men's cricket bronze match at a Summer Games, a medal moment in a returning sport.

demand.explanation: Morning bronze match is a decent get compared with the final, but the medal tag lifts interest.

scorecard.overall: The first cricket bronze in Games history, played with real urgency. It is the smart-money alternative to the sold-out final, with medals and a morning crowd.

significance.explanation: The gold medal match closes cricket's return, with the first Games men's title since 1900 on the line.

experience.explanation: Morning start for a final and a modest 10,000-seat ground, but the crowd will be loud from the first ball.

starPower.explanation: Bumrah, Samson, Brook and Buttler are the kind of names likely to feature in a final.

uniqueness.explanation: First cricket gold in 128 years, with a possible India-England clash for the title.

demand.explanation: The tournament's top ticket, with a huge global fan base chasing a few thousand seats.

scorecard.overall: Cricket's first gold since 1900, decided in Pomona with the sport's global fan base packed around the boundary. Smaller than a stadium final, but this is the match people will say they saw.

significance.explanation: Semifinal in a smaller sport: no medals awarded, but one missed top can end a favorite's bid for the first standalone Boulder title.

experience.explanation: Morning Boulder on the Long Beach waterfront. Short, loud attempts suit the format, though a 9:30 AM start lacks prime-time buzz.

starPower.explanation: Sorato Anraku, the reigning world champion and Paris silver medalist, headlines a field with Lee Dohyun and Mejdi Schalck.

uniqueness.explanation: Opening cut of a brand-new standalone Boulder medal event, in a temporary stadium built on a convention center lot.

demand.explanation: Morning semifinal in a mid-tier sport. Still a Games ticket, but one of the easier climbing seats to land.

scorecard.overall: Come early to watch Anraku and the whole field before the cut, with the Pacific behind the wall. No medals yet, but it's a cheap way into the new standalone Boulder format.

significance.explanation: Qualification seeds the knockout bracket. Real stakes for athletes, but no medals and no head-to-head drama yet.

experience.explanation: Afternoon qualifying with men and women back to back. Fast, easy to follow, and a good primer, though it lacks the knockout tension.

starPower.explanation: Zhao Yicheng's 4.54 record, Sam Watson, Emma Hunt and Mirosław could all be on the wall, even in qualifying.

uniqueness.explanation: Speed runs are routine in form, but this is the first time Speed qualifying feeds its own bracket in a full six-medal climbing program.

demand.explanation: Qualifying of a niche-leaning sport at a temporary venue. Easier to book than finals, though still a Games seat.

scorecard.overall: A smart, cheaper look at the fastest humans on a wall, with world-record chasers like Zhao and Hunt on show. Come for the times, knowing the medal races come later.

significance.explanation: Semifinal cut toward the first women's Boulder medal. Stakes are real, but nobody leaves with hardware.

experience.explanation: Tuesday morning, short problems and a seaside setting. Watchable, if short of evening energy.

starPower.explanation: Janja Garnbret and her 10 world titles lead a field that includes Zélia Avezou, Erin McNeice and Oriane Bertone.

uniqueness.explanation: Sets up the first standalone women's Boulder medal. A semifinal, so a step below the final's novelty.

demand.explanation: Garnbret's pull helps, but a morning semifinal remains an easier climbing ticket.

scorecard.overall: Garnbret is beatable now, and this is where the chasing pack gets its first shot at her. A good-value look at the sport's biggest name before the final.

significance.explanation: Lead semifinal: one route, one attempt, and a fall can end a medal hope. No medals yet.

experience.explanation: Evening session under the lights with the whole stadium leaning in on each climber. Short and tense.

starPower.explanation: Lee Dohyun, Neo Suzuki, Sorato Anraku and Paris champion Toby Roberts make a strong, if niche-famous, field.

uniqueness.explanation: First step toward standalone Lead medals. The evening slot adds atmosphere, but it is still a semifinal.

demand.explanation: Prime-time slot lifts interest above the morning semifinals, though it remains a lower-tier climbing ticket.

scorecard.overall: One-shot tension at golden hour on the Long Beach coast. It's brief, but the evening slot and Roberts's comeback storyline make it the better semifinal pick.

significance.explanation: Two medal events decided in ninety minutes, from quarterfinals to both finals. Gold and bronze change hands here.

experience.explanation: Knockout racing is instantly understandable and loud, though the 9 AM start trims the atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Zhao Yicheng, Sam Watson, Emma Hunt and Mirosław bring record-setters and a home-crowd favorite.

uniqueness.explanation: Medal round of a sport with its first full standalone program, with world records plausible in the same morning.

demand.explanation: Two gold medals plus American contenders in Hunt and Watson make this the hottest morning ticket in climbing.

scorecard.overall: The best value in climbing: every race ends in seconds, and the top two medal events come in one sitting. With Zhao's record and Hunt and Watson racing at home, this is the one to book.

significance.explanation: Lead semifinal: a single route that sorts the field before the first standalone women's Lead medal.

experience.explanation: Evening route climbing, one athlete at a time, with the stadium leaning in on every move.

starPower.explanation: Janja Garnbret, with 33 Lead wins and a 9b+ ascent this year, plus Annie Sanders, the 2026 Lead champion.

uniqueness.explanation: A semifinal on the path to the first women's Lead medal, with the evening slot adding some polish.

demand.explanation: Garnbret and a home-crowd Sanders in prime time make this a solid draw among semifinals.

scorecard.overall: Watch the greatest climber ever work a route, with Sanders as the American rival. A tidy evening session that beats the morning semifinals on atmosphere.

significance.explanation: First standalone men's Boulder gold ever awarded. A medal final in a non-marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Four problems and a crowd that gasps in unison, with the Pacific behind the wall. Morning start trims the energy.

starPower.explanation: Sorato Anraku, the reigning world champion and four-time series champion, is a genuine climbing star, with Lee Dohyun chasing.

uniqueness.explanation: The inaugural men's Boulder title on a temporary coastal stadium. A one-time first that can't be repeated.

demand.explanation: Medal final in a mid-tier sport. Competitive to book, though below the marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: History in four problems: the first men's Boulder champion crowned on his own merit, likely Anraku. A morning final worth building a trip around.

significance.explanation: First women's Boulder gold decided on its own, with a medal podium at stake in a smaller sport.

experience.explanation: Friday morning Boulder is tense and tactile, and the seaside setting helps, though the slot is not prime time.

starPower.explanation: Janja Garnbret is among the most recognizable names in any Games sport, with Bertone and Avezou in pursuit.

uniqueness.explanation: The first standalone women's Boulder title, with a real chance of an upset of the sport's greatest.

demand.explanation: Garnbret's name and a medal on the line make this the top Boulder ticket.

scorecard.overall: Garnbret versus a field that finally believes it can beat her, with a medal first on the line. This is the Boulder final to pick if you pick one.

significance.explanation: First standalone men's Lead medals, decided on a single route with no second chances.

experience.explanation: Afternoon Lead is a short, clean session. Tense, but the daytime slot lacks evening glow.

starPower.explanation: Lee Dohyun, Neo Suzuki and possibly Anraku or Roberts: climbing stars, though few household names.

uniqueness.explanation: Inaugural men's Lead gold, with the possibility of a Boulder-and-Lead double from Anraku.

demand.explanation: Medal final in a mid-tier sport at a small venue. Competitive, but shorter and less hyped than the Boulder finals.

scorecard.overall: A seventy-five-minute final that could crown a Boulder star in a second discipline or a Lead specialist. Short, sharp and a rare first.

significance.explanation: Closes the climbing program and awards the first standalone women's Lead gold, with Garnbret's pursuit of another title.

experience.explanation: Saturday-morning finale with the Pacific behind the wall and a last-medal charge. The slot is early but the moment is big.

starPower.explanation: Garnbret leads the field, with Annie Sanders, Brooke Raboutou and Jessica Pilz adding star depth.

uniqueness.explanation: Last climbing medal of the Games and the first standalone women's Lead title, with a shot at Garnbret history.

demand.explanation: Finale billing, Garnbret and a home contender in Sanders make this a top climbing ticket.

scorecard.overall: A fitting finale: Garnbret chasing another gold, an American rival at home and one route that decides everything. Book it for the last gasp of the climbing program.

significance.explanation: Two gold medals decided in one session, with a women's title guaranteed to change hands. Non-marquee sport, but two finals in a single day carry real weight.

experience.explanation: Roadside viewing in Griffith Park with no fixed seats and a few seconds of each rider. Big screens and the hillside atmosphere help, but it's no stadium night.

starPower.explanation: Evenepoel, Ganna and Van Aert set the men's bar from Paris, and Dygert is a US name. Nobody is confirmed yet, so the top end stays a notch below the marquee sports.

uniqueness.explanation: The zoo has never hosted a Games event, and a start ramp in the Griffith Park hills with a finish at the Observatory is a one-off setting. The format itself is standard.

demand.explanation: Two medal events and a free-roaming roadside setting make this a solid pick, but it lacks the scarcity of a stadium final. Expect it to sell, with less scramble than track or pool finals.

scorecard.overall: Come for the Griffith Park backdrop and the rare chance to see two medals settled against the clock in one morning. You'll catch each rider for seconds, so this suits cycling fans who like to follow the splits, not anyone after stadium theater.

significance.explanation: A gold-medal final in a non-marquee sport, and road cycling's one-day race is a pure winner-take-all shot. Medals are decided on a Griffith Observatory climb built to split the field.

experience.explanation: Roadside at Venice Beach with palm trees, skaters and a peloton rolling out is a fun scene. But the race then leaves for the hills, so you see a start, not a finish, and there are no fixed seats.

starPower.explanation: Faulkner, Vos and Kopecky are Paris medalists, and Vollering arrives as reigning world champion. Not household names to casual fans, but a deep cycling cast for a mid-tier sport.

uniqueness.explanation: Venice Beach Boardwalk has never hosted Games competition, and the finish at Griffith Observatory is a first too. A beachfront start for a women's road race is a one-time Los Angeles pairing.

demand.explanation: Free-roaming roadside viewing makes this a different ticket chase than a stadium final. A home-soil medal story and a Saturday start keep interest high, but it's a mid-tier sport.

scorecard.overall: Catch the peloton rolling out beside the Pacific on a Saturday with a US champion defending on home roads and Vollering hunting the one gold she lacks. It is a start-line spectacle rather than a finish-line seat, but a rare one.

significance.explanation: A men's road race gold is cycling's single biggest one-day prize at the Games. Evenepoel defends, and a 250 km grind ends on a climb designed to decide it.

experience.explanation: A 9:00 AM boardwalk start has charm, with the beach scene and a huge peloton, but you're watching a rollout from the roadside. Most of the 250 km happens somewhere else.

starPower.explanation: Evenepoel, Pogacar's stated ambitions, and reigning world champion McNulty make this one of the most star-heavy fields outside the marquee sports. Van der Poel and Matthews add more.

uniqueness.explanation: The first men's road race to start from Venice Beach and finish at Griffith Observatory. Coming two weeks after the Tour de France, the field and storylines are unlike any other year.

demand.explanation: Cycling fans will chase this one, and Sunday plus the star lineup help. Still, roadside starts are looser than stadium seating, so it is less of a scramble than the marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: Evenepoel defends, McNulty brings a home-soil world title, and Pogacar may crash the party. Go for the Venice Beach start energy and a field this stacked; just know the finish drama unfolds up in the hills.

significance.explanation: Two-run heats where the job is simply advancing. Real stakes for every paddler, but no medals change hands.

experience.explanation: Morning heats beside the Oklahoma River with the OKC skyline behind the channel. Open-air summer heat, and a long session of runs.

starPower.explanation: Jessica Fox and world champion Jakub Krejci both paddle the heats, along with Paris champion De Gennaro. Big names, early round.

uniqueness.explanation: First competition session of the Games, ahead of the Opening Ceremony. A neat bragging-rights angle, even if it's still a heat.

demand.explanation: Early-round session of a mid-tier sport, nearly 1,200 miles from LA. An easier book than the finals sessions.

scorecard.overall: You can say you saw the Games begin before the Opening Ceremony lights came up. Fox and Krejci feeling out the course makes it a fun, lower-pressure way to see the sport.

significance.explanation: Women's K1 medals on the line, one of the first golds of the Games. Semifinal and final in a single morning.

experience.explanation: Single-run final on a concrete channel with the skyline behind. Morning slot and summer heat keep it short of prime-time energy.

starPower.explanation: Jess Fox, the Paris champion and returning world champion, against Evy Leibfarth. Few slalom names are bigger.

uniqueness.explanation: Fox's comeback from kidney surgery meets the first medals of the Games. One run, no second chances.

demand.explanation: Mid-tier sport final with a strong US storyline. Likely one of the hotter slalom tickets.

scorecard.overall: Fox's comeback arc meets an American podium threat in Leibfarth, with one of the first golds of the Games at stake. This is the slalom session to prioritize.

significance.explanation: Men's K1 gold decided after a semifinal on the same morning. A full medal session in a non-marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Sunday morning on the Oklahoma River bank, with a single run deciding the final. Good sport to watch, quieter than prime time.

starPower.explanation: World champion Krejci, silver medalist Pasiut and Paris champion De Gennaro form a strong podium trio, though few are household names.

uniqueness.explanation: A standard medal round in an established sport, with a tight three-way fight for the title. Not a debut or novelty.

demand.explanation: Mid-tier sport final, with a weekend slot helping. A decent ticket pull for slalom fans.

scorecard.overall: A tight, three-way fight between Krejci, Pasiut and De Gennaro with one run to settle it. A sharp pick for paddling fans, with a smaller crowd than the marquee finals.

significance.explanation: Heats sorting the C1 field. Paddlers are fighting just to reach the semifinal.

experience.explanation: Kneeling paddlers and single blades are harder to read at first. A compact morning, about two and a half hours.

starPower.explanation: Fox and Leibfarth in the women's boats, plus world champion Miquel Trave in the men's. Recognizable names, early round.

uniqueness.explanation: Routine heat session in an established sport. The pull is seeing both C1 fields before the finals.

demand.explanation: A Monday morning heat session for a niche boat class. Easier to get, but still a Games ticket.

scorecard.overall: A good way to scout both C1 fields before the medal rounds. Pick it for Fox, Trave and Leibfarth, not for drama.

significance.explanation: Women's C1 gold is decided after a morning semifinal. Fox is chasing back-to-back titles.

experience.explanation: Two rounds across one morning on the channel, with each clean line cheered. Daytime heat keeps it grounded.

starPower.explanation: Jess Fox, the Paris double champion, headlines, with Leibfarth chasing a rebound. Strong marquee-in-slalom names.

uniqueness.explanation: Fox's title defense gives it a hook. Otherwise a standard medal round in an established event.

demand.explanation: Mid-tier sport final with Fox and a US hopeful. Solid but not top-tier slalom demand.

scorecard.overall: Fox defends the C1 half of her Paris double against a deep Slovak and Czech field. Leibfarth's home-crowd comeback story is a bonus.

significance.explanation: Men's C1 gold decided after a semifinal on the same morning. A complete medal session.

experience.explanation: A Wednesday morning on the Oklahoma River bank with back-to-back rounds. Tension high, atmosphere moderate.

starPower.explanation: Trave, Burgess, Gestin and Kratochvil headline. Elite within the sport, though not globally famous.

uniqueness.explanation: Burgess chasing a first gold after Paris and 2026 silvers is a good story. Format is standard.

demand.explanation: Mid-tier final with a wide-open field. Likely sells, but with less competition for seats than K1 finals.

scorecard.overall: A wide-open final where silver specialist Burgess finally has a shot at gold. Trave and Gestin keep it unpredictable for paddling fans.

significance.explanation: Round 1 and repechage knockouts. Elimination is real, but there are no medals yet.

experience.explanation: Multi-boat racing and contact make it more fun to watch than timed runs. Morning heat, but loud and chaotic.

starPower.explanation: Butcher, Clarke, Fox and the Marx siblings could all be racing. Big names, early rounds.

uniqueness.explanation: Kayak cross is only on its second Games appearance. Early round, but the repechage adds a second-chance twist.

demand.explanation: Early-round session of a newer event. Easy to enjoy, easier to book than finals.

scorecard.overall: Kayak cross is slalom's wild card, and this is where favorites get bumped. A fun, chaotic morning for fans who want surprises.

significance.explanation: Heats where only the quickest advance. Stakes are real, but medals are still a day away.

experience.explanation: Four-boat heats with contact are fun to watch live. Short two-hour morning session.

starPower.explanation: Alena and Dimitri Marx, Prindis and Prigent are expected. Recognizable to slalom fans, early round.

uniqueness.explanation: Second Games for kayak cross, with head-to-head racing as the hook. Still an early round.

demand.explanation: A Friday morning heat session for a niche event. Fills up, but easier than finals.

scorecard.overall: Short, fast and full of bumps, with the Marx siblings as the watch-list headline. A good low-stakes look at kayak cross before finals day.

significance.explanation: Two gold medals, men's and women's kayak cross, in a single session. Knockout rounds lead into both finals.

experience.explanation: Elimination racing from quarterfinals to finals in 2 hours 20 minutes. Loud, chaotic, and the last slalom session of the Games.

starPower.explanation: Noemie Fox, Butcher, Clarke, the Marx siblings and Prindis, plus a possible Jess Fox cameo. Great slalom names.

uniqueness.explanation: Only the second kayak cross medals ever awarded. Slalom closes for the Games with two golds.

demand.explanation: Two medal events and a closing-day Saturday slot make this a top slalom ticket. Likely the most contested.

scorecard.overall: Two golds, chaotic racing and the last slalom of the Games all in under 2.5 hours. If you only see one kayak cross session, make it this one.

significance.explanation: Heats and quarterfinals only: crews are fighting for semifinal spots, not medals. Real stakes for the athletes, but nothing gets decided yet.

experience.explanation: A 9 AM start on a saltwater channel with shoreline viewing and Belmont Shore behind you. Pleasant and close to the water, but a quiet-round morning.

starPower.explanation: Fuksa, Fejes and the Harrison versus Vincent versus Luzan C1 200m storyline put real names in the heats, even in an early round.

uniqueness.explanation: Early rounds on a course built for 1932 add some history, but this is one of several heat sessions in the week.

demand.explanation: Early-round sprint at a smaller venue. Games scarcity keeps it a sell-through candidate, though it should be one of the easier bookings.

scorecard.overall: A scouting morning: Harrison's comeback, Vincent's record-setting 200m and Fuksa's C1 duel all start here. Cheaper entry to a 1932 landmark, but the medals come later in the week.

significance.explanation: Three medal events, with A finals in both K2 500m races and the men's C1 1000m. That's a true medal morning.

experience.explanation: Semis and finals back to back keep the energy rising along the channel. Still a morning slot at a modest, shoreline-style venue.

starPower.explanation: Fuksa and Queiroz headline the C1 1000m, and a possible Carrington return in the K2 would add serious wattage. Few household names beyond the sport, though.

uniqueness.explanation: Standard-format medal finals in an established sport. The 1932 rowing-course setting adds some flavor, but no debut hook.

demand.explanation: Medal finals in a mid-tier sport are a sought-after ticket, but the setting is smaller and less competitive than the marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: Three golds in one morning, with Fuksa's C1 defense and a possible Carrington K2 comeback as the draws. It's a smaller stage than the stadium finals, but real medal drama on a historic channel.

significance.explanation: Heats and quarterfinals across six events. Crews are chasing semifinal berths, and no medals are awarded.

experience.explanation: The longest morning of the week, with big K4 and C2 crews on the water. Good variety at the channel, but it's a heat-stage session.

starPower.explanation: Pimenta, Kopasz, Dostal and Jagsch are all in the field, and a Carrington return in the women's K1 is a possibility. Strong names, early round.

uniqueness.explanation: Routine heats in a standard-format sport. The 1932 channel gives it some atmosphere, but this session is one of several like it.

demand.explanation: Early rounds of a mid-tier sport at a modest venue. Still a Games ticket, just a less competitive one to book.

scorecard.overall: Come to see the men's K1 1000m field and the women's K1 500m contenders before the medal rounds. It's a long and loose morning, and a good value way to see the full range of boats.

significance.explanation: Finals in the women's K1 500m, the women's C2 500m and the men's K1 1000m. Three golds are decided in one session.

experience.explanation: The K1 1000m is a heavyweight race along the channel, and the finals bring a bigger crowd. Still a morning slot at a modest venue.

starPower.explanation: Carrington's possible comeback, plus Pimenta, Kopasz, Dostal and Jagsch, makes this the deepest star lineup of the week.

uniqueness.explanation: Established-format medal finals at a historic 1932 course. Carrington chasing a record ninth gold adds a rare storyline, but it's not a debut.

demand.explanation: Marquee names in K1 events make this one of the week's hotter tickets. Morning timing and a small venue keep it below the stadium finals.

scorecard.overall: The best card of the week, with the K1 events as the showpiece. If Carrington is in the boat, this is the one to be at, and Pimenta, Kopasz and Dostal are a heavyweight fight over 1000m.

significance.explanation: Four medal events close the program: the women's C1 200m, the men's C2 500m, and both K4 500m finals.

experience.explanation: Closing-day finals with the loud K4 boats and a sprint that ends in seconds. A morning slot, but it has the biggest atmosphere of the week.

starPower.explanation: Vincent, Harrison and Luzan headline the 200m, and Carrington could be in a K4. Strong names, but not mainstream stars.

uniqueness.explanation: Closing day of canoe sprint, with a world-record holder defending a gold by 0.01s. Standard format, but a rare finale.

demand.explanation: Four finals and the closing-day atmosphere make this the week's most wanted. Still a mid-tier sport at a modest venue.

scorecard.overall: Four golds on closing morning, led by a 200m sprint that was decided by one hundredth in Paris. The K4 finals are the noisiest boats, so it's a fun way to finish the week.

significance.explanation: Qualifying only: times set the first-round bracket, but no medals change hands. Real stakes for seeding, just a step before the finals.

experience.explanation: A 9 AM start in a compact 2,450-seat indoor bowl. Every standing launch is up close, though the morning slot has no prime-time buzz.

starPower.explanation: Lavreysen's Dutch squad and Britain's Finucane are likely in the start gate, with world-title-winning China as the other draw.

uniqueness.explanation: One of several routine qualifying blocks at Carson. Nice for sprint nerds, but the real drama arrives later in the day.

demand.explanation: Opening-day morning at a small track. It should still sell given Games scarcity, but it is the easier ticket of the day.

scorecard.overall: The cheapest way to see the fastest launches in cycling, with Dutch and Chinese squads chasing seeding. Come for the speed and the intimacy; the medals are three hours away in CTR02.

significance.explanation: Two team sprint golds on the line, men's and women's, plus the opening of men's team pursuit. That is a stacked medal block.

experience.explanation: Midday finals in a tight indoor bowl where the roar bounces off the pine. Great seats everywhere, if without evening lights.

starPower.explanation: Lavreysen and Hoogland's Dutch men, Finucane's British women, Ganna and Milan in the pursuit qualifying. Plenty of big names.

uniqueness.explanation: Opening-day gold medals in a velodrome that stands near the 1984 track site. Special, but standard-format finals at a generic venue.

demand.explanation: Two gold medals on day one of cycling is the hot ticket of the opening stretch, and the small capacity makes it tighter.

scorecard.overall: Two team sprint golds in one sitting, seconds apart from a roaring crowd. This is the best opening-day value in the velodrome, with a Denmark-versus-Australia pursuit preview as a bonus.

significance.explanation: Qualifying, first rounds and repechages. Spots in the next rounds are at stake, with no medals decided.

experience.explanation: A 8:45 AM start with a long, mixed program. The flying 200m is gripping up close, but it is a daytime grind.

starPower.explanation: Men's sprint qualifying could feature Lavreysen and Richardson, plus Finucane's keirin ride and Britain's record-setting pursuit women.

uniqueness.explanation: The flying 200m is a pure speed spectacle, and the US women's pursuit redemption angle adds a hook. Still a qualifying-heavy session.

demand.explanation: Morning qualifying at a compact venue. It should sell, but it is among the easier cycling tickets to book.

scorecard.overall: The flying 200m qualifying is a pure stopwatch thrill, and could feature Lavreysen or Richardson. A good pick for sprint fans who want big names with fewer crowds than finals.

significance.explanation: A men's team pursuit gold is decided, though the rest of the card is early sprint rounds and keirin quarterfinals.

experience.explanation: Afternoon session with a four-minute team pursuit final that plays out right in front of you in a tight bowl.

starPower.explanation: Ganna and Milan with Italy, Denmark's world champions, and Australia's defending champions headline the final.

uniqueness.explanation: A standard medal round at a small venue, but Denmark-Australia-Italy is a compelling pursuit rivalry.

demand.explanation: One gold medal plus keirin quarterfinals in an afternoon slot makes for a steady, in-demand ticket.

scorecard.overall: Four minutes of team pursuit with Denmark, Australia and Italy's Ganna in the mix, then keirin quarterfinals for the scrum. It is a strong afternoon session with a single gold on the line.

significance.explanation: Women's team pursuit and keirin golds both on the card, plus the full men's omnium and sprint quarterfinals. Heavy medal load.

experience.explanation: A long daytime program that runs from 11 AM to 4 PM. The omnium is an all-day chess match, with the keirin final closing out.

starPower.explanation: Iuri Leitao in the omnium, Britain's record pursuit squad, and a keirin field that may include Finucane and Ellesse Andrews.

uniqueness.explanation: The US women's team pursuit defending Paris gold in front of a home crowd gives this session a storyline others lack.

demand.explanation: Two golds, a defending US champion at home, and a long program in a 2,450-seat bowl make this one of the toughest tickets.

scorecard.overall: Two golds plus a US pursuit team trying to reclaim its Paris crown at home. Settle in for the omnium, then stay for the keirin final, a late-day highlight of the week.

significance.explanation: Men's sprint semifinals are best-of-three duels, but the session is mostly early women's sprint rounds without medals.

experience.explanation: A 9 AM start. The semifinal tactics are fascinating up close, but the morning slot keeps the energy lower.

starPower.explanation: Lavreysen's eight straight world titles and a possible Richardson rematch, plus Finucane and Yuan Liying in early heats.

uniqueness.explanation: A possible Lavreysen-Richardson showdown is rare, and the story has weight. It is a semifinal, not the final.

demand.explanation: Star-heavy sprint semis draw interest, though the early start makes this a more attainable ticket than the final.

scorecard.overall: See Lavreysen's semifinal tactics before the final, plus Yuan Liying and Finucane warming up in women's sprint heats. A smart pick for fans who want star power with a slightly easier ticket.

significance.explanation: Men's sprint gold and women's madison gold in one session. Two titles, plus the women's sprint round of 16.

experience.explanation: Early afternoon at Carson with the sprint final's best-of-three and the madison's relay chaos. Great sightlines for both.

starPower.explanation: Lavreysen going for another sprint title, a potential Richardson rematch, and Britain's Anna Morris in a loud madison.

uniqueness.explanation: Lavreysen's sprint final defense is a marquee track moment, paired with a chaotic madison. Standard format, special pairing.

demand.explanation: The men's sprint final is cycling's top draw and the madison adds energy. Expect this to be among the first sold out.

scorecard.overall: The marquee sprint final with Lavreysen's dominance on the line, plus a madison that is organized chaos. If you only see one track session, this is the one.

significance.explanation: Men's madison gold is the headline, with women's sprint quarterfinals and keirin first round adding more stakes.

experience.explanation: Late-morning to early-afternoon madison with hand slings and points sprints, a delight in a tight 2,450-seat bowl.

starPower.explanation: Denmark's Bevort and Leth, Portugal's Leitao, plus Yuan Liying and Finucane in women's sprint rounds, and Lavreysen in keirin.

uniqueness.explanation: Madison is the sport's most chaotic format, and a Denmark-Portugal rematch is a good hook. Established event at a generic venue.

demand.explanation: One gold plus top women's sprint rounds on a Saturday. A busy ticket, but the sprint finals are tougher to get.

scorecard.overall: The men's madison is the most unpredictable final on the track, with Denmark and Portugal swapping blows. A fun, high-energy Saturday pick with women's sprint quarterfinals thrown in.

significance.explanation: Three golds in one morning: women's omnium, women's sprint and men's keirin. The closing track session of the Games.

experience.explanation: An 8:45 AM Sunday start, but the final-day crowd and three finals in a compact bowl bring real energy.

starPower.explanation: Lavreysen in the keirin, Yuan Liying, Finucane and Andrews in the sprint, and a potential Valente-Morris omnium.

uniqueness.explanation: Final day of track racing, with three golds and Lavreysen's possible keirin defense, gives it a finale feel.

demand.explanation: Three medal events on closing morning, with Lavreysen potentially going for gold. Expect strong competition for seats.

scorecard.overall: The track finale delivers three golds before lunch, led by Lavreysen's keirin and a loaded women's sprint. Worth the early alarm for the closing-day atmosphere and a deep list of stars.

significance.explanation: Prelim round: the cut line is real for every board in the field, but no medals change hands before the semifinal.

experience.explanation: A 10 AM start in the Arroyo Seco canyon: sunny, unhurried, and close to the well, though without final-night buzz.

starPower.explanation: Paris champion Chen Yiwen is the headliner, with Britain's Spendolini-Sirieix a comeback storyline further down the order.

uniqueness.explanation: A standard opening round in an established sport at a smaller outdoor pool; routine format for diving.

demand.explanation: Diving's first session of the Games should still sell, but it is an easier ticket than the finals.

scorecard.overall: Get an up-close look at the entire springboard field before the pressure rises. It's a relaxed morning with Chen Yiwen in the mix, and an easier way into the Rose Bowl pool than the medal sessions.

significance.explanation: Semifinal in a smaller sport: one bad dive ends a medal run, though nothing is awarded.

experience.explanation: Tense morning diving in open air, with every list fighting for a final spot.

starPower.explanation: Chen Yiwen and Maddison Keeney, the Paris gold and silver medalists, are the names to watch.

uniqueness.explanation: Standard semifinal in an established event; the format is familiar from every Games.

demand.explanation: Solid draw for diving fans, with the final that afternoon likely to be the bigger ask.

scorecard.overall: The round where favorites get nervous. If you want to see Chen Yiwen's control and the chasing pack up close without final-session pricing pressure, this is a smart morning.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal final and the first individual diving medals of the Games, in a non-marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Afternoon final in the Arroyo Seco, a short and tense 75 minutes with the hills behind the pool.

starPower.explanation: Chen Yiwen defends against Paris silver medalist Keeney, with China's depth looming behind.

uniqueness.explanation: Opening individual medals add a little occasion, but it's a standard-format final at a modest venue.

demand.explanation: Diving's first medal session should be among the most sought after for the sport.

scorecard.overall: The first individual diving gold of the Games, with a chance to see whether anyone can crack China's springboard machine. Short, sharp, and easily the best springboard ticket for women.

significance.explanation: Morning prelim: world-class advancement stakes, though medals are two rounds away.

experience.explanation: Morning diving in the canyon is relaxed, with a chance to watch the whole field.

starPower.explanation: Osmar Olvera, the reigning world champion, and Paris champion Xie Siyi are both likely in the field.

uniqueness.explanation: A routine opening round, with the interest mostly in Olvera's regional pull.

demand.explanation: Mexican fans in Southern California add some pull, but prelims remain the easier ticket.

scorecard.overall: A relaxed look at Olvera and Xie before the pressure ramps up. A good pick for Mexican fans and diving followers who want to see the full field without the final-day squeeze.

significance.explanation: A semifinal in a smaller sport sets the final field; no medals yet but real stakes.

experience.explanation: Afternoon start with good light and a strong field.

starPower.explanation: The Paris podium trio of Xie, Wang Zongyuan, and Olvera makes this loaded with names.

uniqueness.explanation: Standard semifinal; the Paris rematch angle is the only real extra.

demand.explanation: Strong field with a Mexico-China storyline makes it a notch above typical semifinals.

scorecard.overall: The Paris podium trio gets a first full test here. If you can't get the final, this is the best way to watch Olvera take on China's springboard pair.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal final in a non-marquee sport, with a chance at a historic third straight title for Xie.

experience.explanation: Afternoon final in a compact setting where every dive is audible; tight and tense.

starPower.explanation: Xie Siyi, Wang Zongyuan, and world champion Osmar Olvera are the names to chase.

uniqueness.explanation: A potential Xie three-peat gives it some historical weight, though format and venue are standard.

demand.explanation: One of the premier diving finals, with Mexican fans adding a boost.

scorecard.overall: Olvera against China's best, with Xie chasing a historic third straight title. Seventy-five minutes of diving where one wobble decides everything, and a top-tier ticket for the sport.

significance.explanation: Preliminary round; advancement is the only prize, whoever shows up.

experience.explanation: Morning prelim with a 10m tower, which looks dramatic even before medals are on the line.

starPower.explanation: Quan Hongchan's status is uncertain, but Chen Yuxi and the Chinese platform stars give it name value.

uniqueness.explanation: Quan's possible return adds intrigue to what is otherwise a routine early round.

demand.explanation: Platform draws curiosity, and a Quan appearance could lift it, but prelims stay easier to get.

scorecard.overall: The first look at whether Quan Hongchan is back. Even without her, Chen Yuxi's presence makes this a worthwhile morning on the tower.

significance.explanation: Semifinal in a smaller sport: it feeds a medal final but awards nothing itself.

experience.explanation: Afternoon tower diving is dramatic, with each dive lasting barely two seconds.

starPower.explanation: Chen Yuxi, the Diver of the Year, and a possible Quan return make this a strong lineup.

uniqueness.explanation: Quan's uncertain return gives it a bit more than a typical semifinal.

demand.explanation: Tower semifinal with big names; a bit stiffer competition for tickets than the prelims.

scorecard.overall: If Quan Hongchan is back, this is where you'd see her first test after the layoff. If not, Chen Yuxi still makes it a worthy afternoon on the tower.

significance.explanation: Preliminary round; the cut to semifinals is the only objective.

experience.explanation: Morning tower diving with a loose, open feel and plenty of space to move around.

starPower.explanation: Cassiel Rousseau, Tamai, and Williams give it recognizable names even in an early round.

uniqueness.explanation: Routine prelim of an established event; the Paris podium rematch is the only angle.

demand.explanation: Early rounds remain easier to book, though the Games floor still applies.

scorecard.overall: A loose morning to scout Rousseau and the Paris medalists before the medal rounds. Pick it for access and cost, not for stakes.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal final in a non-marquee sport, with a possible Quan Hongchan three-peat.

experience.explanation: Afternoon platform final in the canyon, five dives of nerve and a very engaged crowd.

starPower.explanation: Quan Hongchan is among the best-known divers in the world, with Chen Yuxi as backup.

uniqueness.explanation: A possible Quan comeback and three-peat make this one of the standout diving stories of the Games.

demand.explanation: Likely the most sought-after diving ticket, especially if Quan's status clears up.

scorecard.overall: The most emotional ticket in diving, if Quan Hongchan makes it. Even with Chen Yuxi alone at the top of the tower, this is the final to chase.

significance.explanation: Semifinal in a smaller sport; twelve advance and the rest go home.

experience.explanation: A late-morning tower session with the wide open field and shifting leaderboard.

starPower.explanation: Rousseau, Tamai, Williams and Cao Yuan's possible presence offer recognizable names.

uniqueness.explanation: Same-day final and an open field give it a little extra, though the format is standard.

demand.explanation: Fans who miss the final can still catch strong talent here at a gentler price.

scorecard.overall: Platform's most open field in years makes this a smart pick. Go to see who emerges as the challenger, then stay for the final if you've got both tickets.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal final on men's platform, the diving event most open to an upset.

experience.explanation: Afternoon platform final where one entry can swing the podium; a short, dramatic session.

starPower.explanation: Rousseau, Tamai and Williams lead a field that may include Cao Yuan.

uniqueness.explanation: A non-Chinese champion is plausible, but the session is still a standard final format.

demand.explanation: Closing individual platform final should be one of the top diving tickets.

scorecard.overall: The diving final with the most realistic path to a non-Chinese champion. Rousseau, Tamai and Williams make this the best bet for a genuine upset.

significance.explanation: Single-shot gold-medal final with no prelims and no second chances.

experience.explanation: Late-morning synchro final, brief but precise, best for people who love the sport's choreography.

starPower.explanation: Chen Yiwen with new partner Chen Jia headlines, and the U.S. silver pair adds home appeal.

uniqueness.explanation: Host-nation silver medalists at home give it an extra storyline beyond the standard format.

demand.explanation: American fans and a clean medal decision should keep this a competitive ticket.

scorecard.overall: One hour, one final, and a home crowd hoping the U.S. can close the gap on China's new Chen pairing. A compact and tidy diving ticket.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal final decided in a single round with no safety net.

experience.explanation: Afternoon synchro rewards close watching; short, but each dive is a puzzle of timing.

starPower.explanation: Olvera and Celaya, Laugher and Harding, and China's Wang Zongyuan add real names.

uniqueness.explanation: No non-Chinese pair has won since Rio, so a Mexico or Britain win would be rare.

demand.explanation: Mexican and British fans should make this an active ticket.

scorecard.overall: Can anyone end a streak of Chinese wins in men's synchro? Mexico and Britain both have a case, and the one-hour final leaves no room for error.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal final in one shot, with the challenge of closing a 30-point gap.

experience.explanation: Afternoon tower synchro: brief, precise, and best for fans who like timing and unison.

starPower.explanation: Chen Yuxi, possibly Quan Hongchan, and North Korea's silver pair give it star appeal.

uniqueness.explanation: New partnerships and Quan's uncertain status make it a less predictable final than usual.

demand.explanation: Tower diving is a crowd pleaser, and the last synchro final is likely to be well sought.

scorecard.overall: A tower synchro final with a real question about who stands beside Chen Yuxi. North Korea's pair needs about 30 more points to catch up, which makes this a good watch for the margin alone.

significance.explanation: One gold medal, one shot. A single-final synchro event means no semifinal cushion, so every dive carries full medal weight in a non-marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Late-afternoon sun, an open-air pool in the Arroyo Seco, and hills behind the tower. Diving is easy to follow live, though the venue is smaller than a stadium.

starPower.explanation: Lian Junjie and Yang Hao headline as Paris champions, and Noah Williams brings British interest. Diving names travel less widely than track or swimming stars.

uniqueness.explanation: Standard-format medal round in an established sport at a generic aquatic venue. Its single-final drama and a possible upset of China's run add some distinction.

demand.explanation: A mid-tier sport final with a medal ceremony attached, in a compact venue. Expect it to sell, but it will be a softer ask than the swimming or track finals.

scorecard.overall: Eight dives, one chance, and a China-led field that Tom Daley and Matty Lee once proved beatable. A smaller stage than the marquee finals, but a tense and easy-to-love hour for anyone who likes a medal decided by a single clean entry.

significance.explanation: Opening dressage tests set the eventing standings, but no medals move today. Real stakes for riders, yet the verdict is still days away.

experience.explanation: A 9 AM start in the historic Santa Anita grandstand with mountains behind. Quiet, precise sport, so atmosphere is more hush than roar.

starPower.explanation: Jung, Collett and Canter are the names that anchor eventing, and top riders ride early. Not household names outside horse circles.

uniqueness.explanation: First equestrian session of the Games, on grounds that hosted the 1984 competition. A real opening-day hook for a routine dressage round.

demand.explanation: Morning dressage at a racetrack is among the easier equestrian tickets. Still the opening session, so it should sell.

scorecard.overall: Be there for the first scores of the equestrian program and the Jung-without-Chipmunk question. It is a quiet, early prelim, but a rare chance to watch the opening act at a 1984 venue.

significance.explanation: Another dressage block feeding the cross-country standings. A low score here is a head start, not a medal.

experience.explanation: Late-afternoon light over Santa Anita is the better slot for dressage, with a bigger crowd and golden-hour mood.

starPower.explanation: Defending and world-level eventers are in the draw, led by the British and German contenders. Big in the sport, modest beyond it.

uniqueness.explanation: Routine dressage block, lifted slightly by the benchmark-chasing storyline after Jung's record scores.

demand.explanation: Afternoon slot should sell better than the morning run, but remains a lower-pressure ticket in a niche sport.

scorecard.overall: The nicer-light dressage session of Day 1, where a leader can emerge for the next three days. A solid pick for sport fans who want atmosphere without medal-day prices or pressure.

significance.explanation: Last chance to bank dressage points before cross-country. Positions are shaped here, but no medals are awarded.

experience.explanation: Sunday morning at 9 AM with a scoreboard-watching crowd. Pleasant setting, subdued energy.

starPower.explanation: Collett and other late starters keep recognizable eventing names in the ring. Strong for the sport's followers.

uniqueness.explanation: Closing dressage in eventing, with the standings locking in. Useful context, but a familiar format.

demand.explanation: A morning prelim in a niche sport at a big, open venue. Easier to book than the finals.

scorecard.overall: This is the session where the cross-country pecking order locks in. Good for fans who like knowing who is chasing whom, though it is a lower-key morning.

significance.explanation: Cross-country reshuffles the standings more than any other phase, so stakes are higher than a typical prelim, though medals wait for jumping.

experience.explanation: Eventing's most dramatic phase, with fences, speed and crowd noise on an early-morning course. The best live day before the finals.

starPower.explanation: Jung, Collett, Canter and Burton all take on the course. Medal-level eventers in full flight.

uniqueness.explanation: Cross-country on Santa Anita's grounds, where 1984's course ran. Not a medal round, but distinct from the arena sessions.

demand.explanation: The most popular eventing day short of the finals. Expect a livelier crowd than the dressage blocks.

scorecard.overall: If you only see one eventing day before the finale, make it this one. Cross-country is the sport's real drama, with clear rounds greeted by roars from the grandstand.

significance.explanation: Team and individual eventing medals are decided in one night. Two golds, though in a non-marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Evening session under lights, with a hush before each round and a tense six-hour run at Santa Anita.

starPower.explanation: Jung's quest for another title, plus Collett, Canter and Burton, make for confirmed medal contenders. Equestrian's best-known cast.

uniqueness.explanation: A double medal night at a venue with 1984 history, with a new-horse Jung storyline adding color.

demand.explanation: Equestrian's biggest eventing ticket, with two medal events in prime time. Expect competition for seats.

scorecard.overall: A long, nerve-shredding night where one rail can flip two medals. The best eventing ticket of the Games, and a fine introduction for newcomers.

significance.explanation: Grand Prix qualifier: world-class riders chasing the team final and freestyle spots, with no medals yet.

experience.explanation: A 9 AM dressage start in a historic grandstand. Elegant, quiet, and best for those who love the sport.

starPower.explanation: Werth, Hemmer and possibly von Bredow-Werndl headline a German-led field. Strong names for a qualifier.

uniqueness.explanation: Dressage returns to the ground where Klimke won in 1984. A nice historical echo, but still a qualifier.

demand.explanation: Morning qualifier in a niche sport. Likely to sell, with less competition than the medal days.

scorecard.overall: An early look at a wide-open dressage field, with Germany's depth under question after von Bredow-Werndl's horse losses. A calm morning for fans who like to scout the favorites.

significance.explanation: Qualifier round, where advancement matters but no medal is awarded.

experience.explanation: Afternoon dressage with a fuller crowd and softer light. A better slot than the morning for atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Charlotte Fry and Glamourdale, double world champions in 2026, are the marquee draw. Plus German, Danish and Belgian standouts.

uniqueness.explanation: Routine qualifier session, with the chance to compare top nations side by side.

demand.explanation: Afternoon slot with the world's top combination likely to ride. Pricier and busier than the morning blocks.

scorecard.overall: The qualifier session most likely to feature Fry and Glamourdale at full stretch. Worth it for a first look at the world champion before the medal rounds.

significance.explanation: Day 2 qualifier keeps team and freestyle hopes alive, but no medals change hands.

experience.explanation: Friday 9 AM at Santa Anita is a calm, close-to-the-arena setting. Easy to enjoy, short on buzz.

starPower.explanation: Laudrup-Dufour, a two-time world silver medalist, headlines a field with other top European names.

uniqueness.explanation: Qualifier in an established sport, with a redemption storyline for Laudrup-Dufour as the hook.

demand.explanation: Morning qualifier with comfortable seat availability by Games standards. Fan-of-the-sport pick.

scorecard.overall: A quiet morning to see Laudrup-Dufour try to turn silver into something shinier. Good for dressage devotees and anyone who likes an easier, intimate ticket.

significance.explanation: Last qualifier session, where the final team and freestyle fields are set. Elimination stakes raise it above a typical prelim.

experience.explanation: Friday evening in Arcadia with a tense, full grandstand. A better atmosphere than the morning qualifiers.

starPower.explanation: Werth, von Bredow-Werndl if selected, Fry and Laudrup-Dufour could all appear. Strong, deep star pull.

uniqueness.explanation: Final cut-off session with some rare drama, but still a qualifier in a standard format.
