uniqueness.explanation: Japan's Paris upset against Italy's world titles makes a good narrative, but it is an early team round.

demand.explanation: Morning team foil with a U.S. squad should sell, with a softer ticket than finals.

scorecard.overall: Japan, Italy, Hong Kong and the U.S. all come in with a claim. A good, lower-pressure way to see foil's best team bracket.

significance.explanation: Bronze and gold medals in one evening, with team foil as the headline. Non-marquee sport, but two medals are decided.

experience.explanation: Saturday prime time in a temporary arena of about 7,000 seats. Team relay swings keep the room loud, though it's a convention hall, not a stadium.

starPower.explanation: Italy's Macchi and Marini, the U.S.'s Itkin and Massialas, and Hong Kong's Edgar Cheung bring real names. Fencing fame stops short of household.

uniqueness.explanation: A standard-format medal round in an established sport, lifted by a likely Japan-Italy Paris rematch and a home-nation American threat.

demand.explanation: Saturday-night medal session with U.S. medal hopes should sell briskly, though fencing finals sit a notch below the marquee sports.

scorecard.overall: Italy has owned the world titles since losing to Japan in Paris, and the Americans are hunting a first team foil podium moment on home soil. Saturday-night relay drama makes this the best men's team ticket of the fencing run.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinals and semis decide who reaches the medal bouts, but no gold is awarded here; classification bouts carry little weight.

experience.explanation: A morning-to-early-afternoon marathon in a convention hall. Sabre's speed helps, but it's a long sit without prime-time energy.

starPower.explanation: Kharlan's possible return and Apithy-Brunet's comeback add names, plus world champion Eifler's Germany. Depth is wide but faces are less famous.

uniqueness.explanation: Early rounds of an established event, with a Kharlan comeback storyline as the one-off hook.

demand.explanation: Morning elimination session on the final day; easier to book than the evening medal bouts, though the Games still draw crowds.

scorecard.overall: Eight teams become four in a single morning, with the Kharlan question hanging over the strip. It's the pick for sabre fans who want volume and chaos; the medals come later that night.

significance.explanation: Bronze and gold in women's team sabre close out fencing at the Games, so two medals are decided in one evening session.

experience.explanation: Closing-night fencing in a roaring 7,000-seat hall. Sabre's noise and speed make the format a crowd-pleaser, even in a convention-center setting.

starPower.explanation: Possible comeback arcs for Kharlan and Apithy-Brunet, plus world champion Eifler, give it star weight. Real names, but not mainstream icons.

uniqueness.explanation: A standard-format medal round in an established sport, but the final fencing session and wide-open field give it a finale feel.

demand.explanation: Sunday-evening medal bouts on the last day of fencing should be a hot ticket among non-marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: The wide-open field, with France, Hungary, Korea and Ukraine all plausible, makes this a genuine toss-up on the sport's last night. Sabre is fastest and loudest, and the comeback stories add a human thread.

significance.explanation: Opening-day group games. Real advancement stakes with six teams chasing four semifinal spots, but no medals are decided.

experience.explanation: Saturday afternoon, the day after the opening ceremony, in a tight soccer-built stadium. Debut-day buzz lifts it, though daylight lacks night-game energy.

starPower.explanation: Rosters are unset, but the U.S. men's seven-time world champions and Canada's reigning women's champs are expected, and NFL names are possible.

uniqueness.explanation: The first snaps of Games flag football. A debut-day session in a new sport earns real rarity, even as a prelim.

demand.explanation: Curiosity about the debut will fill seats, but it is a group-stage afternoon and the easier ticket in the sport.

scorecard.overall: Be there for the first drives in Games history. It is a group-stage slate, so you are buying the novelty and bragging rights rather than medal drama.

significance.explanation: Group play with semifinal berths at stake, but early enough that one loss is survivable.

experience.explanation: Saturday night under lights in a 22,000-seat bowl with steep stands and a noisy safe-standing end. The best slot of the opening weekend.

starPower.explanation: World champions from the U.S. and Canada are in the field, with possible NFL crossover names, but rosters remain unconfirmed.

uniqueness.explanation: Prime-time prelims in a debut sport. Fresh format and a cramped field make it distinctive, though it is not a medal round.

demand.explanation: Saturday night in the opening weekend is the most sought-after prelim slot, with a built-in LA crowd.

scorecard.overall: The pick for prelim fans: Saturday night, lights on, a new sport with a crowd on top of the field. Upsets like American Samoa's win over the U.S. make any game live.

significance.explanation: Early group games with advancement points to earn; every result shapes seeding but nothing is decided.

experience.explanation: Sunday afternoon at a compact stadium where every snap is visible. Fun and fast, just short of night-game atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Mexico's women, former top-ranked and World Games champions, and Italy's men as world silver medalists add credible names.

uniqueness.explanation: Early round of a brand-new Games sport. The sport carries the rarity, not this particular slate.

demand.explanation: A relaxed Sunday-afternoon family slot in a debut sport; popular but less contested than evenings.

scorecard.overall: A good first-full-day look at the sport, with Mexico's women as a defending-champion-caliber draw. Easier to get than the night sessions, and still plenty of fun.

significance.explanation: Group-stage games where seeding and semifinal paths take shape; no medals yet.

experience.explanation: Sunday night under lights with a rematch feel and the north-end terrace making noise. A strong prime-time prelim.

starPower.explanation: U.S. and Canadian women, last final's rivals, headline, with a chance of NFL names on rosters.

uniqueness.explanation: Potential U.S.-Canada rematch energy in a brand-new sport, but still a group-stage night.

demand.explanation: Evening slot with the biggest women's rivalry on the board draws a louder ticket chase.

scorecard.overall: Sunday night is where the rivalry energy lives, with the U.S. women chasing Canada. Great atmosphere for a prelim, and an easier path than medal days.

significance.explanation: Midweek group games; teams still jockeying for top-four finishes.

experience.explanation: Monday afternoon daylight at a small venue. Pleasant and close to the action, but quiet next to the evening sessions.

starPower.explanation: Italy's men and a possible Great Britain team with analyst Phoebe Schecter, but qualifiers decide who actually shows up.

uniqueness.explanation: Early round of a debuting sport, with qualifier-dependent matchups making it the most open slate.

demand.explanation: Monday afternoon is among the easier flag tickets, though the sport's novelty keeps interest firm.

scorecard.overall: A cheaper-feeling Monday-afternoon way into the debut sport, with a decent chance to see a qualifier underdog get its first Games crowd.

significance.explanation: Round-robin games where seeding matters but elimination is not yet on the line.

experience.explanation: Monday night games at a close-in stadium. Lights and high scoring help, even if it is a weeknight prelim.

starPower.explanation: Top contenders including the U.S. men and defending-champion-level women could appear, with matchups still unsettled.

uniqueness.explanation: Evening prelims in a new sport; routine in format, special in setting.

demand.explanation: Night slots draw better than afternoons, and the sport's novelty carries the Monday crowd.

scorecard.overall: Come for scoreboard fireworks and a close-up view of a game with no kicking. A solid weeknight choice, not a must-have.

significance.explanation: Late group games with seeding at stake; the cut is approaching but not here.

experience.explanation: Tuesday afternoon daylight. Good sight lines, but a smaller crowd feel than the evening games.

starPower.explanation: Canada's MVP quarterback Sara Parker and a bronze-winning men's team lead the possible names.

uniqueness.explanation: Mid-tournament prelims of a new sport; the qualifier-driven Mexico storyline adds a little spice.

demand.explanation: A midweek afternoon is among the easier flag tickets, with steady novelty-driven interest.

scorecard.overall: A low-key Tuesday afternoon with a chance to watch Canada's quarterback up close. Nothing medal-adjacent, but a fine value pick.

significance.explanation: Seeding pressure builds with only four of six advancing, though no medals are decided.

experience.explanation: Tuesday night games on a shrunken field with temporary stands, so the crowd is close. Good, if not peak, energy.

starPower.explanation: Women's teams that have met in the Grand Slam series may bring familiar faces and big quarterbacks.

uniqueness.explanation: Evening prelims in a new sport, with a compact field as the distinguishing touch.

demand.explanation: Evening slots draw more interest than afternoon prelims, with women's rivalries lifting it.

scorecard.overall: A night to watch seeding pressure start to bite. Good atmosphere for a prelim, with a compact field that exposes every defensive slip.

significance.explanation: Final afternoon of group play, with semifinal spots on the line for teams that still need wins.

experience.explanation: Wednesday afternoon with sorting-day tension raising the stakes of every snap in a tight stadium.

starPower.explanation: Contenders like Canada's women and the U.S. men are likely in the mix as seeds get settled.

uniqueness.explanation: Last-chance prelims where elimination looms. A narrative-rich day in a debut sport.

demand.explanation: Do-or-die stakes make this a hotter afternoon ticket than earlier days.

scorecard.overall: The best afternoon prelim of the week: teams have to win, and close finishes are common in this sport. Real tension without medal-day prices.

significance.explanation: Final night of group play. Four of six teams survive, so every result matters.

experience.explanation: Wednesday night with the north-end terrace roaring on late scores. Elimination stakes and lights make it the best prelim atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Top men's and women's teams will be fighting for seeds, and the NFL angle might add names.

uniqueness.explanation: Last night of a debut sport's group stage, with cut-line drama a one-time thing.

demand.explanation: The prime-time elimination slot is the top-selling prelim ticket of the tournament.

scorecard.overall: The prelim finale carries real jeopardy: six teams, four spots, and a noisy crowd. If you want knockout-style tension before the medal rounds, this is it.

significance.explanation: Two men's semifinals, with winners into a gold medal game and losers left with a bronze shot. Medals are one step away.

experience.explanation: Thursday afternoon knockout flag football at a tight venue. Win-or-bronze stakes and close finishes lift it.

starPower.explanation: The seven-time champion U.S. men and MVP Doucette headline, with Italy and Canada as credible rivals.

uniqueness.explanation: The first men's semifinals in Games history, in a sport making its debut.

demand.explanation: Semifinal stakes plus U.S. interest make this a hot ticket despite the daytime slot.

scorecard.overall: Two knockout games where the 2026 semifinals went down to five points or fewer. The U.S. is the favorite, but it is a one-flag-pull sport.

significance.explanation: Women's semifinals decide who plays for gold and who drops to bronze, with the first medals a day away.

experience.explanation: Friday early afternoon with knockout tension in a small stadium. Intimate, though the slot is quieter than night.

starPower.explanation: Sara Parker, Diana Flores and Vanita Krouch are the quarterbacks to see, pending rosters.

uniqueness.explanation: The first women's semifinals at a Games, with a U.S.-Canada-Mexico rivalry in play.

demand.explanation: Semifinal stakes and the sport's best women's teams make this tough to get, even in the afternoon.

scorecard.overall: The women's field is deeper and tighter than the men's, and the quarterbacks are stars. This is the knockout round where a new champion can be born.

significance.explanation: Men's bronze and gold medal games, the first men's flag football medals awarded in Games history.

experience.explanation: Friday evening medal games in a loud, compact stadium. Peak energy for the men's tournament.

starPower.explanation: Doucette-led U.S. men, plus Italy and Canada, and perhaps NFL players on rosters.

uniqueness.explanation: First men's medals in a sport making its Games debut, in an LA stadium full of football culture.

demand.explanation: Medal night in the home country's most-hyped new sport is the toughest men's ticket.

scorecard.overall: Seeing the first men's gold in the sport is the draw, with the dominant U.S. team likely in it. It is a smaller stage than marquee finals, but a historic one.

significance.explanation: Women's bronze and gold games award the sport's first women's medals at a Summer Games.

experience.explanation: Saturday midday medal games with a full house and daylight finishing the tournament. Festive, close to the field.

starPower.explanation: Canada's Sara Parker, Mexico's Diana Flores and the U.S. women's stars give the sport's best names.

uniqueness.explanation: The first women's flag football gold, decided on the tournament's closing day.

demand.explanation: Closing-day medal games with four serious contenders make this the sport's toughest women's ticket.

scorecard.overall: The first women's gold medal, with Canada, the U.S., Mexico and Great Britain all in the conversation. The closing-day party at the tournament's best-attended session.

significance.explanation: Opening subdivision of men's qualification. Nobody wins a medal here, but every routine shapes the team, all-around and apparatus fields.

experience.explanation: Late-morning start in a steep indoor bowl where upper rows still look straight down on the floor. Calmer crowd, but a clean view of a full six-event rotation.

starPower.explanation: Hashimoto or Yulo could land in this subdivision, but the draw decides it. Strong depth of world-level names either way.

uniqueness.explanation: Opening gymnastics session of the Games at a famous arena, which adds some first-day charm. Still one of three men's qualifiers.

demand.explanation: Easiest-value ticket of the opening day. Gymnastics is popular and the building will still fill, just with less of a scramble.

scorecard.overall: The soft-opening way into men's gymnastics: Kobe's old building, a relaxed late-morning crowd, and a chance to catch a few big names before the stakes harden. Best for fans who want gymnastics on a budget.

significance.explanation: Middle qualifier, so advancement is the only prize. Still, team spots and apparatus finals are being earned routine by routine.

experience.explanation: Afternoon session with a filling arena and a view that stays good from every row. Better energy than the morning, short of the evening session.

starPower.explanation: Armenia brings world champions Davtyan and Manukyan, though the field's biggest names may sit in other subdivisions.

uniqueness.explanation: One of three near-identical men's qualifiers. The Armenian pommel and vault storylines add flavor but not rarity.

demand.explanation: A mid-afternoon Saturday slot makes it easier to book than the evening, though gymnastics demand keeps it competitive.

scorecard.overall: A smart pick for specialists. Armenia's pommel and vault stars are the draw, and the pommel horse alone can turn a medal hope upside down in seconds. Less glamour than the night session, but easier on the wallet.

significance.explanation: Last men's qualifier, and it closes the books on the team final and all-around fields. Real stakes, but no medals.

experience.explanation: Saturday-night prime time in a packed downtown bowl. The energy is the best of the three men's qualifiers.

starPower.explanation: Zou Jingyuan, Lan Xingyu and Tang Chia-hung headline a night full of world champions on their best events.

uniqueness.explanation: Mixed-team qualifying implications give it an extra wrinkle. Otherwise it is a standard qualification night.

demand.explanation: Saturday night in L.A. Live is the hot slot of the qualifying day, so expect a more competitive booking.

scorecard.overall: Pick the late session if you want the best atmosphere of men's qualifying. Zou, Lan and Tang give it specialist firepower, and the mixed-team qualifying question adds a fresh wrinkle.

significance.explanation: Opening women's qualifier. Nobody medals, but the team, all-around and apparatus fields start to take shape.

experience.explanation: Morning start, but this is when women's competition begins, with fresh nerves and a clear view from every steep row.

starPower.explanation: Blakely and Nemour are likely names, and any Biles comeback would be the biggest in the sport. Plenty of world-level depth already.

uniqueness.explanation: Kickoff of women's competition carries first-day buzz and the Biles question hangs over it. Still a qualifier.

demand.explanation: Women's gymnastics is the hottest ticket in the sport, which keeps even a morning session competitive.

scorecard.overall: Women's gymnastics begins here, so you get the first look at the field and the possibility of a Biles cameo. A morning start keeps it easier to book than the evening sessions.

significance.explanation: Qualifier with advancement stakes only. Brazil's team spot is not even secured yet.

experience.explanation: A compact 100-minute afternoon session. Fine seats and a lively Brazil crowd, but it lacks the prime-time pull.

starPower.explanation: Rebeca Andrade is the draw. A three-time world vault champion and Paris medalist, she brings real star wattage.

uniqueness.explanation: Andrade is likely in her final Games, without floor, so watching her on vault and beam is a rarer treat.

demand.explanation: Short afternoon slot between the big sessions. Still gymnastics, so booking is no gimme.

scorecard.overall: This is the Andrade ticket. Seeing the Paris silver medalist on vault and beam, in what she calls likely her last Games, is worth the short afternoon slot.

significance.explanation: Fourth of five women's qualifiers. Advancement is on the line, nothing more.

experience.explanation: A 6:15 PM start fills the bowl by the second rotation, so the energy is much stronger than daytime sessions.

starPower.explanation: Nemour, the 2026 world bars and beam champion, plus Italy's Esposito, who took beam bronze in Paris.

uniqueness.explanation: Italy's post-Paris rise and Nemour's tiebreak-winning beam give it a nice storyline, but it is still a qualifier.

demand.explanation: Early-evening Sunday slot with big names. It is more competitive to book than the morning and afternoon sessions.

scorecard.overall: A good-value evening session with real stars. Nemour and Italy's Esposito make this a solid way to see the sport's rising powers before finals pricing kicks in.

significance.explanation: Last women's qualifier, and it locks every final field. Plenty of tension, but no medals yet.

experience.explanation: Past 9 PM under full-house lights. It is a long night, but the late-session energy is hard to beat.

starPower.explanation: Blakely, Pease, Esponda and Melnikova are all in the mix, with Biles possibly looming in the background.

uniqueness.explanation: Sets the whole field and might include mixed team qualifiers. It is still the same qualifying format.

demand.explanation: The late-night marquee slot holds the strongest American names, so it books faster than the daytime qualifiers.

scorecard.overall: If you want one qualifier with real firepower, this is it. The U.S. stars take the floor late, and the field gets finalized before midnight.

significance.explanation: First gymnastics medals of the Games, and the team final is a gold-medal event in a marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Monday-evening medal session in a steep, packed downtown bowl. Five-per-team, no-reserve pressure makes every routine tense.

starPower.explanation: Hashimoto leads defending champion Japan, with China and the neutral Russian team pushing. Strong, if not household, names.

uniqueness.explanation: Japan-China rematch of Paris, and the first gymnastics medals of these Games. Medal-round format is standard.

demand.explanation: Marquee-sport medal session in prime time, so competition for seats will be fierce.

scorecard.overall: The first gymnastics gold of the Games, decided with no safety net. Japan and China resume their Paris rivalry in a format where one fall can change everything.

significance.explanation: Women's team gold in gymnastics, a marquee sport. It is the biggest team title on the program.

experience.explanation: Tuesday-night medal session in an arena built for roars. Three rotations of tension with every row looking down on the floor.

starPower.explanation: Blakely, Pease and Esponda lead the U.S. against China, with Andrade for Brazil and a possible Biles comeback.

uniqueness.explanation: A 0.233-point loss to China at the 2026 Worlds sets up a home-soil revenge story. Biles uncertainty adds drama.

demand.explanation: The hottest ticket in gymnastics: U.S. women on home soil competing for team gold.

scorecard.overall: This is the gymnastics event of the Games for many fans. The U.S. women chase gold at home with China looking to repeat its 0.233 upset, and a possible Biles return would raise it further.

significance.explanation: Men's all-around gold, the crown of men's gymnastics, in a marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Wednesday-night final where each athlete faces six events, giving the arena a long, tense duel.

starPower.explanation: Hashimoto, a four-time world champion, chases Uchimura's record, with Oka, Yang Haonan and Zhang Boheng in pursuit.

uniqueness.explanation: Hashimoto's bid for Uchimura's streak makes this one of the sport's defining storylines. Format is standard.

demand.explanation: Marquee final in prime time, so seats are hard to find, though demand trails the women's finals.

scorecard.overall: Watch Hashimoto chase history. His 1.799-point margin at the 2026 Worlds was the biggest in 13 years, and Oka and the Chinese contenders are waiting for any slip.

significance.explanation: Women's all-around gold, the sport's most prestigious individual title. Marquee final.

experience.explanation: Thursday night with the bowl full to the rafters and every rotation in view. About as good as gymnastics gets.

starPower.explanation: Biles may return, Blakely is world champion, and Andrade plans a fourth Games. The strongest star lineup in the sport.

uniqueness.explanation: A home-soil all-around with a possible Biles comeback and the American podium streak on the line.

demand.explanation: The top gymnastics ticket at the Games. Home crowd, big names and gold on the line.

scorecard.overall: The headline night of gymnastics: possibly Biles at 31, Blakely defending her world title, and a U.S. podium streak stretching back to 2003. If you only get one session, this is it.

significance.explanation: Multiple apparatus golds are decided, so this session carries several medal events in a marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Late-morning slot with one routine at a time, easy to follow and family friendly. Less drama than an evening final.

starPower.explanation: World champions such as Nemour, Andrade and Fred Richard are likely, depending on the events scheduled.

uniqueness.explanation: Standard apparatus-final format. The lineup of events is not set, which makes it a bit of a mystery box.

demand.explanation: Weekend late-morning finals with several medals draw strong interest, but are easier to book than the evening finals.

scorecard.overall: A good family-friendly medal session. You will not know which apparatus you get, but the chance of Nemour, Andrade or Richard in a one-routine, one-wobble medal fight is a strong bet.

significance.explanation: Several apparatus golds are decided here. A marquee sport with multiple medals on the line.

experience.explanation: Sunday morning with a hush on beam or a roar on vault. One athlete at a time keeps it easy to follow.

starPower.explanation: Zou Jingyuan, Davtyan, Nemour and Saraiva are among the likely names, depending on the events.

uniqueness.explanation: Typical apparatus-final format. Tiebreak-level margins on beam give it special tension, but nothing unprecedented.

demand.explanation: Weekend medal session with strong names. It is a bit easier than evening finals, but it still sells.

scorecard.overall: A Sunday-morning medal session that could hinge on tenths. Whether it is Nemour on beam or Zou on parallel bars, expect a few silent moments and one or two roars.

significance.explanation: Another triple-medal-style apparatus session with golds at stake, including possibly high bar.

experience.explanation: Monday morning slot, with high bar's long flights adding real spectacle. Lacks the prime-time electricity.

starPower.explanation: Oka, Tang Chia-hung, Pease and Esponda are all likely candidates, with Biles a wildcard if she returns.

uniqueness.explanation: Tang-versus-Oka on high bar is a fresh rivalry. The format is standard and the apparatus lineup is unconfirmed.

demand.explanation: Weekday-morning finals draw strong but less frenzied demand than the evening sessions.

scorecard.overall: The best pick for rivalry fans: Tang beat Paris champion Oka for the 2026 world high bar title, and a rematch could be on. Floor could bring the American one-two as well.

significance.explanation: A gold-medal final in a marquee sport, and the first mixed team champion in Games history.

experience.explanation: Tuesday late-afternoon medal session. The format is unknown, which adds mystery but also uncertainty.

starPower.explanation: Japan, China and the U.S. could bring Hashimoto, Blakely and other leading names, if they field their top pair.

uniqueness.explanation: A brand-new medal event with a format still not final. Being there for the first champion is the whole pitch.

demand.explanation: Novelty plus a gold medal in a marquee sport draws strong interest, with lingering format questions tempering it a bit.

scorecard.overall: A debut with plenty of unknowns, and that is the appeal. You can say you saw the first mixed team champion crowned, likely in a Japan-China-U.S. fight.

significance.explanation: Round 1 of four. Nobody is handed a medal, though a bad Wednesday can sink a gold bid early.

experience.explanation: Roam a canyon course off Sunset with no grandstands, pick a hillside and watch the whole field pass. Daytime and relaxed, but the open setting makes it a different kind of Games day.

starPower.explanation: Scheffler, Fleetwood and the world's top-ranked players all tee off across the day. Few prelim sessions in any sport offer this many household names.

uniqueness.explanation: Golf's return to the Games at a historic course is a draw, but this is one of four routine rounds. Hogan's Alley adds some pull.

demand.explanation: Golf fans will chase a Riviera grounds pass and the full men's field is on property. The easiest golf day to book, but still a hot ticket.

scorecard.overall: The best way to see every big name in one place without the pressure of a leaderboard. Pick a hole, plant yourself on the hillside and watch the world's best men come to you.

significance.explanation: Round 2 shapes the leaderboard, and the cut-line pressure is real, but no medals are decided.

experience.explanation: Thursday gives space to learn the course: the hillside clubhouse overlooks the 18th, and the slopes make a natural amphitheater. Walking golf at its best, if low on drama.

starPower.explanation: The full men's field is still in play, with Scheffler and Fleetwood likely among the names on the grounds.

uniqueness.explanation: Standard second round of a 72-hole event. The venue gives it character, but nothing about the day is singular.

demand.explanation: Weekday golf at a famous course with a star field. Easier than the weekend, though still competitive.

scorecard.overall: Thursday is where the leaderboard starts to take shape and the field begins to separate. A good, lower-pressure day to explore Riviera and watch the stars grind.

significance.explanation: Moving day sets the 54-hole order. Paris showed that leaders here can still fall away, so the stakes feel close to the medals.

experience.explanation: Friday crowds build around the finishing holes, with the 18th green framed by the clubhouse hillside. Tension rises as the leaders get close to the weekend.

starPower.explanation: Whoever survives the cut is a world-class contender, and the stars who are in the mix will be on show.

uniqueness.explanation: Round 3 is a familiar rhythm in golf. The Riviera backdrop and medal chase make it a notch above a routine day.

demand.explanation: Moving day is a prime golf ticket, and the leader-chasing story pulls in the crowds before the final round.

scorecard.overall: The last chance to watch a leaderboard form before the medal round, with Paris as a reminder that nobody is safe. If you can't get Saturday, Friday is the smart play.

significance.explanation: Medals are decided this evening at the end of 72 holes. Golf is not one of the marquee sports, so it falls just short of a top-tier gold.

experience.explanation: Final-round Saturday at Riviera, with fans stacked on the slopes above the 18th green and Hogan's statue nearby. As good as a live golf experience gets.

starPower.explanation: Scheffler is the defending champion and world No. 1, with Fleetwood and Matsuyama among the contenders. The sport's biggest names are in the mix.

uniqueness.explanation: A chance at the first back-to-back men's golds since golf returned, at one of America's best-known courses. Rare, though not once-in-a-lifetime in the Coliseum sense.

demand.explanation: Final-round golf with Games medals on the line and a hillside amphitheater. The hottest ticket in golf.

scorecard.overall: The men's medal round on a legendary course, with Scheffler going for history. This is the one golf ticket worth fighting for.

significance.explanation: Half of a new team medal, with 18 holes of four-ball setting the table for the final. Not decisive, but every shot counts.

experience.explanation: Best-ball scoring means birdies and aggressive play, and a new mixed-gender format brings fresh energy to a Sunday on the grounds.

starPower.explanation: Men's and women's stars share the course, with Scheffler and Korda both world No. 1s who could be paired if they make the US team.

uniqueness.explanation: Debut of a mixed team event, golf's first team medal since 1904. A genuine novelty that is also a prelim round.

demand.explanation: A new format and a Sunday slot make it a curiosity ticket. Strong interest, though less urgent than the individual finals.

scorecard.overall: Catch golf's team-medal experiment in its first act. Four-ball is the fun format, with men and women playing together and plenty of birdies.

significance.explanation: The first mixed-team golf medals in Games history are decided over 18 holes of foursomes. A non-marquee final, but a full medal event.

experience.explanation: Monday morning in the canyon, with pairs playing alternate shot and crowds following hole by hole. The early start is the only drawback.

starPower.explanation: Qualifiers come from the men's and women's top rankings, so national teams could feature names like Scheffler, Korda and Ko.

uniqueness.explanation: First golf team medal since 1904, in a format that rewards partnership. A true historical moment.

demand.explanation: A medal final in golf, with a debut story and compact 18-hole drama. Monday morning softens it slightly.

scorecard.overall: A medal-round debut with real nerves: one ball, two partners, no safety net. Golf's newest medal gets its first champion here, and you can say you were there.

significance.explanation: Round 1 of four for the women. A poor start hurts, but no medals are on the line.

uniqueness.explanation: The sport's reborn format debuts here, with the obstacle sprint replacing riding and the first Valley Zone Games competition. Opening day of a returning sport adds novelty.

demand.explanation: Niche sport, morning slot, semifinal round. Still a Games ticket, but one of the easier gets, and cheaper than the finals.

scorecard.overall: Your first look at the new obstacle-sprint format and the Guzi-Khalil rivalry, with Gulyás's status unresolved. A morning in a Valley park is a lower-key pick than the finals, but it's the sport's opening day.

significance.explanation: Men's semifinal where 18 start and only the top finishers advance to Tuesday's medal race. Survival matters here; medals don't get handed out.

experience.explanation: Morning fencing bouts, obstacle heats, a swim and a laser run in a temporary park venue. Easy to follow, but daytime and low on prime-time buzz.

starPower.explanation: Egypt's depth could bring Paris champion Ahmed El-Gendy and 2025 world champion Moutaz Mohamed, with Czech world No.1 Matej Lukes the man to beat.

uniqueness.explanation: Early round of a returning sport in a new format, at a venue that only exists for the Games. A taste of novelty without a medal attached.

demand.explanation: A niche sport semifinal on a Sunday morning. Likely to sell, though far less contested than the medal sessions.

scorecard.overall: A tight men's field with a two-point gap between the top two at the 2026 worlds makes this a lively cut-down morning. It's a lesser pick than Tuesday's final, but a good one for curious sports fans.

significance.explanation: Women's gold, silver and bronze are decided in one two-hour sitting. A non-marquee sport, but a genuine medal final.

experience.explanation: The laser run turns into a chase where the first across the line wins, so the finish is easy to read live. Monday morning at a temporary park venue holds it back.

starPower.explanation: Blanka Guzi, Farida Khalil and Kerenza Bryson are the names to watch, with a possible Michelle Gulyás return adding Paris champion status.

uniqueness.explanation: The first women's final in the new obstacle-race format, the sport's return to opening-week scheduling, and a gold decided by a head-to-head chase make this special.

demand.explanation: A mid-tier sport final, so it's easier to book than athletics or swimming, but it's the women's medal day and should draw well.

scorecard.overall: The best women's session of the sport: a short, sharp final decided on the course with no judges. If Guzi and Khalil renew their duel, with Gulyás possibly in the mix, a Monday morning gets very exciting.

significance.explanation: Men's medals and the sport's closing act of the Games. A non-marquee final, but gold is on the line.

experience.explanation: A two-hour final that ends in a laser-run chase gives clear drama, and the finish line tells you the winner. Tuesday morning in a temporary park venue is a quieter setting.

starPower.explanation: Paris champion Ahmed El-Gendy, world champion Matej Lukes and Egypt's Moutaz Mohamed give the field real recognition within the sport, though few are global household names.

uniqueness.explanation: The first men's final under the new obstacle format and the finale of modern pentathlon's opening-days return. El-Gendy's world record gives it a benchmark.

demand.explanation: A mid-tier sport medal final. Competitive to book given Games scarcity, but easier than the marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: Come for a final where no lead is safe: Lukes won the 2026 world title off the laser run, and Mohamed ran from last in fencing to fourth. A morning medal session with real chase-down drama.

significance.explanation: A gold-medal final in a non-marquee sport, decided in one mass start with no heats to bank anything. One race, one title, no second chances.

experience.explanation: Late-morning start on a hillside course with drops and jumps, and riders pass several times so you can work the loop. Watchable, though not a stadium-style spectacle.

starPower.explanation: Pidcock chasing a third straight gold anchors the field, with Hatherly, Koretzky and 2026 World Cup champion Luca Martin in the mix. Big in cycling circles, less so beyond them.

uniqueness.explanation: Brand-new course built for the Games and a possible Pidcock three-peat. The format itself is standard, which keeps this below the once-in-a-lifetime tier.

demand.explanation: Mid-tier sport final with a real medal on the line. Outdoor viewing areas along the course mean room to move around, so this is an easier ticket than the marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: Pidcock has made a habit of falling behind and winning anyway, and a three-peat attempt is the headline. Pick a technical drop on a brand-new hillside course and watch the field come through again and again. It's a rare cycling spectacle, minus the stadium crowd.

significance.explanation: A gold-medal final in a non-marquee sport, settled in a single mass start. No heats, so every rider arrives with everything to play for.

experience.explanation: Hillside loop with several passes by the field and spots to roam between viewing areas. A late-morning start gives a relaxed day outdoors rather than prime-time electricity.

starPower.explanation: Frei, the 2026 world champion, and Rissveds, the Rio 2016 champion who won the World Cup overall, headline. Home hope Haley Batten adds a familiar name for U.S. fans.

uniqueness.explanation: The first Games race on a course built just for 2028, with a wide-open post-Paris field. Standard format, so it stays a notch below the rarest sessions.

demand.explanation: A medal final in a mid-tier sport, boosted by a potential American on the podium. Plenty of trailside room keeps it a softer ticket than the marquee events.

scorecard.overall: The Paris champion has drifted toward the road, leaving the field wide open for Frei, Rissveds and a home-soil push from Haley Batten. A good pick for fans who want a hillside race with a genuine American silver-to-gold storyline.

significance.explanation: A gold-medal final in a non-marquee sport, with a brand-new champion guaranteed after van Rouwendaal's retirement. Medals only, one race, no second chances.

experience.explanation: Free-to-roam beachfront viewing near the pier is a vibe, but swimmers are specks offshore and the late-morning slot lacks stadium roar. Great atmosphere, less great sightlines.

starPower.explanation: Moesha Johnson arrives as the reigning world champion with a perfect World Cup season, and Taddeucci is a Paris bronze medalist. Strong names, but not household ones.

uniqueness.explanation: First women's 10km in years without van Rouwendaal, swum in the Pacific off Long Beach rather than a river. Open water is a rare live-spectator format.

demand.explanation: Mid-tier sport final at an outdoor beach venue, so a softer ticket than pool or track finals. Games scarcity still keeps it a worthwhile early booking.

scorecard.overall: A wide-open title race with no reigning champion and a clear favorite in Johnson, who has already won in these waters. Come for the beach-party setting and a finish decided by a hand's length; it's a smaller stage, but a distinctive one.

significance.explanation: Men's 10km gold, one of only two open water medal events. Winner takes the title in a single mass-start race, with no heats to soften it.

experience.explanation: Pack racing inside the Breakwater with fans on the sand and pier is a lively, offbeat setting. Distance and the late-morning slot cap the drama compared with a stadium.

starPower.explanation: Florian Wellbrock, a Tokyo champion and reigning world champion, headlines, with Paltrinieri and Paris champion Rasovszky lurking. Deep pedigree for a niche discipline.

uniqueness.explanation: Open water swimming at an American beach is a rarity, and this field could feature a Wellbrock-Paltrinieri rematch on a course Wellbrock has already won.

demand.explanation: A mid-tier sport final on open sand is an easier ticket than the marquee finals. Expect it to sell, but with less frenzy than pool or track.

scorecard.overall: Wellbrock has won on this course, yet this race rarely follows form: Betlehem, Paltrinieri and Rasovszky all have the tools to upset him. A scrappy finish within sight of the beach makes a fun, offbeat pick.

significance.explanation: Time trials and a last-16 knockout. Seeding and survival are on the line, but no medals get handed out before lunch.

experience.explanation: Morning surf on the Long Beach shoreline, with sand sprints and capsizes visible from the beach. Fun and open-air, though a daytime session on a temporary beach setup.

starPower.explanation: Chris Bak, Moritz Wolff and Isabella Scammell are the names to hunt for, though few are household names and none are confirmed for 2028.

uniqueness.explanation: First ocean rowing ever raced at a Games, so even the seeding rounds are a debut. But it's the early round, not the medal moment.

demand.explanation: Early-round session of a niche new sport at an open beach. Easier ticket by Games standards, though not an easy one.

scorecard.overall: Come early for the chaos: the first heats of rowing on open ocean at a Games, with flips and sprints through the surf. A curiosity pick, best for sport-hunters, with the medals arriving later in the day.

significance.explanation: Two gold medals are decided, men's and women's solo, in the first coastal rowing medals the Games has ever awarded.

experience.explanation: Afternoon finals with the finish line right in front of the sand crowd. Close races, loud beachfront energy and a Long Beach backdrop.

starPower.explanation: Chris Bak, the most decorated beach sprinter, may be chasing gold, plus Scammell and Lobnig. Strong names within a niche sport.

uniqueness.explanation: Debut medals in a brand-new discipline, raced in open surf. That's a true first, though a debut doesn't make it marquee.

demand.explanation: Two medal finals on the beach, a hot ticket for a niche sport. Expect competition for seats, but less than for the marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: Two golds in the first coastal rowing medal session ever, in a race so short that one missed buzzer or wrong buoy can end it. Unpredictable and loud, it's the best seat in the sport's debut.

significance.explanation: Time trials and last-16 knockouts for the mixed double. The stakes are advancement, with no medals awarded.

experience.explanation: Mid-morning on the Belmont Shore sand, where two-person crews launch together. A good look at the format, but it's a daytime prelim.

starPower.explanation: Lithuania's two-time champions and Germany's new world title pair are in the mix, but the names are mostly known only to rowing fans.

uniqueness.explanation: The first mixed-gender rowing event at a Games, but this is the early round, and the history is made later in the afternoon.

demand.explanation: Morning prelim of a niche new event at a beach venue. Among the easier tickets in the Games, relatively speaking.

scorecard.overall: A first look at mixed rowing's debut, with crews that may not look like the ones that qualified. It's a lower-stakes pick, but a good way to see chemistry crack before the final.

significance.explanation: A single gold-medal final in a non-marquee sport, in the first mixed-gender rowing event ever held at a Games.

experience.explanation: A short, intense final with the finish line on the sand. Afternoon sun and ocean make it a fun live show, though it's just one race program.

starPower.explanation: Lithuania's Jancionis and Kazlauskaite and Spain's Ander Martin are heavy hitters in beach sprint, but nobody here is broadly famous.

uniqueness.explanation: The first mixed-gender rowing medals in Games history, decided in the sport's own debut on open ocean. A real once-only moment.

demand.explanation: The final is the best ticket of the Tuesday session, but it's a niche sport on a beach with a smaller crowd draw.

scorecard.overall: Mixed rowing's first-ever medals come down to a sprint up the beach and a few seconds of surf. A smaller stage than the marquee finals, but a true piece of Games history to see in person.

significance.explanation: Heats only. Crews are chasing advancement, with no medals awarded and repechage safety nets behind them.

experience.explanation: Saturday late-afternoon opener on a historic 1932 channel, with shoreline viewing beside the lanes. Charming setting, but the racing itself is early-round.

starPower.explanation: Paris champion Karolien Florijn and 2025 world champion Fiona Murtagh headline the singles, with Romania's and Croatia's Paris golds in the men's boats.

uniqueness.explanation: Opening day of the first Los Angeles regatta since 1932, on the original course, and the first rowing ever at 1,500 metres. Heats, though.

demand.explanation: Opening-day novelty helps, but heats in a niche sport at a modest shoreline venue make this one of the easier regatta tickets.

scorecard.overall: Come for the first strokes of a regatta back on its 1932 water, with Murtagh and Florijn sniffing each other out. It's heat racing, not medal drama, but a rare chance to see the opener.

significance.explanation: Mostly heats, with men's double and pair semifinals as the only step up. Qualification stakes, no medals.

experience.explanation: A 9 AM Sunday start for heat racing at a shoreline venue. Pleasant for rowing fans, a sleepy slot for everyone else.

starPower.explanation: Zeidler, Ntouskos and Zalaty in the same single sculls heats means the sport's biggest names race in round one.

uniqueness.explanation: Seeing the Paris champion and reigning world champion on the early rounds is a nice wrinkle, but the session is routine regatta progression.

demand.explanation: Early Sunday heats of a niche sport. Still a Games ticket, but one of the softer asks.

scorecard.overall: A morning for rowing purists: Zeidler and Ntouskos open their rematch in heats while semifinals sharpen the doubles and pairs. No medals, but a cheap look at stars up close.

significance.explanation: The regatta's first medals go out here, in the men's double sculls and pair A finals, with B and C finals and quarterfinals alongside.

experience.explanation: Anthems at 9 AM beside the lanes make for a distinctive start. Morning light and a close shoreline, though a quieter stage than stadium finals.

starPower.explanation: Simon van Dorp, a Paris single sculls bronze medalist and 2026 double sculls world champion, leads a field with Romania and Croatia's reigning golds.

uniqueness.explanation: First medals of the regatta, over a first-ever 1,500 metres, on the 1932 course. A solid rarity for rowing fans.

demand.explanation: Medal races draw the crowd, but a 9 AM Monday slot in a niche sport keeps competition for seats modest.

scorecard.overall: The first anthem of the regatta rings out across Marine Stadium, with Romania and the Dutch battling in the double. Early, but it's the opening medal races in a shortened-course history.

significance.explanation: Two women's A finals, the double sculls and the pair, hand out six medals before 11:15 AM.

experience.explanation: Two medal races on a Tuesday morning with a heat-filled backdrop. Fast, compact, and close to the water.

starPower.explanation: Romania, the Netherlands and New Zealand's Paris champions are in the hunt, plus Zeidler in the men's single quarterfinals.

uniqueness.explanation: A world-best pair crew racing a first-ever 1,500 metres is intriguing, but this is standard-format medal racing in a classic sport.

demand.explanation: Women's medal finals plus Zeidler quarterfinals make it a decent pick, though a Tuesday 9 AM start keeps it an easier ticket.

scorecard.overall: Two women's medal races with world-best speed in the pair, and Zeidler's quarterfinal as a bonus. A good value morning if you want medals without the weekend crush.

significance.explanation: Men's quad and four A finals are the headliners, with six medals across two boats, plus single sculls semifinals.

experience.explanation: Crew boats sweeping down a narrow channel is great live theater, and a Wednesday 9 AM start keeps it compact.

starPower.explanation: The US four, Paris champions and 2026 world champions, race on home water against a Dutch quad, and Fiona Murtagh may appear in the semifinals.

uniqueness.explanation: A US four medal race in Los Angeles, on the 1932 course, is a strong homeland story.

demand.explanation: The US four on home water lifts this above typical rowing mornings, though weekday early timing keeps it moderate.

scorecard.overall: The best weekday pick for American fans: the reigning Paris and world champion four chasing gold at home. Compact, loud, and close enough to hear the catch.

significance.explanation: Women's quad and four A finals put six medals on the line, plus single sculls semis.

experience.explanation: Thursday morning crew finals at the shoreline, with a world-best crew in the mix. Fast and tight, though still a morning slot.

starPower.explanation: The US women's four, who set a 6:09.87 world best, face Dutch Paris champions, while Britain, the Dutch and the US contest the quad.

uniqueness.explanation: A world-best-setting US crew racing on home water in a first-ever 1,500 metres. Rare for a rowing session.

demand.explanation: Two women's medal finals with a home-team storyline draw interest, though the Thursday morning slot softens the scramble.

scorecard.overall: The US women's four, record-setters on home water, are the story, with a deep quad final for support. A strong pick for medals and speed.

significance.explanation: The men's eight A final is the regatta's flagship race, joined by the women's single sculls A final.

experience.explanation: The eight is rowing's loudest spectacle, and a Friday 10 AM slot with a packed shoreline gives it real energy.

starPower.explanation: Netherlands' double world champion eight, Britain's Paris gold crew, plus Florijn and Murtagh in the single sculls give this the regatta's deepest star list.

uniqueness.explanation: Men's eight final at the 1932 course, over a first-ever 1,500 metres. The race that defines the regatta.

demand.explanation: The eight is the regatta's marquee race, so this is the toughest ticket on the water, even at mid-morning.

scorecard.overall: This is the regatta's headline act: the Dutch eight against Britain's Paris gold crew, plus a single sculls final with Murtagh and Florijn. If you attend one rowing session, make it this one.

significance.explanation: The men's single sculls A final and women's eight A final close the regatta, both gold-medal races.

experience.explanation: A Saturday-morning finale on the shoreline, with a closing-day crowd and a single scull showdown. Atmospheric despite the quieter venue.

starPower.explanation: Zeidler versus Ntouskos headlines the single, with Romania's champion women's eight chased by a US crew.

uniqueness.explanation: The final rowing race on the water that closed a Los Angeles regatta in 1932. A bookend with real history.

demand.explanation: Closing-day finals with Zeidler and Ntouskos draw a crowd, but a 10:30 AM Saturday rowing slot is less fiercely contested than stadium finals.

scorecard.overall: Zeidler and Ntouskos could settle their rivalry in the final single scull, with a women's eight showdown to follow. A fitting close on historic water and a smart pick for rowing devotees.

significance.explanation: Opening pool play, with advancement the only prize. Every team gets two more matches to recover, so the pressure is real but not yet acute.

experience.explanation: Wednesday morning in Carson: six quick matches, close sight lines, and a stadium still warming up. Fun for rugby fans, short on night-game buzz.

starPower.explanation: New Zealand and Australia, the world's top two women's sides, will likely be on the pitch, plus Paris medalists Canada and the U.S. Names are known in rugby circles more than beyond.

uniqueness.explanation: Opening day of a returning sport at its first Games with the women leading off. The curtain-raiser has some novelty, though it is still pool play.

demand.explanation: A morning pool session is the easier ticket in a sold-out-leaning tournament. Rugby's Paris crowds suggest it will still fill.

scorecard.overall: Cheap way into the tournament's opening act: six matches, the first look at the New Zealand-Australia rivalry's form, and seats close enough to hear the hits. A lesser pick than the evening, but a genuine rugby morning.

significance.explanation: Pool play, so advancement positioning is all that is at stake. A first-day loss stings but does not end anyone's run.

experience.explanation: Evening kickoffs in a compact 27,000-seat stadium bring a louder crowd and softer light. This is the better of the opening-day slots.

starPower.explanation: Ilona Maher's possible return gives this session a household name, and the U.S. bronze medalists headline a deep women's field.

uniqueness.explanation: Host-nation debut under the evening sky, with the Maher storyline hanging over it. A lively pool night rather than a once-only occasion.

demand.explanation: Evening slot plus a possible U.S. appearance makes this the hotter ticket of the opening day. Expect American fans to push it up.

scorecard.overall: The home crowd's first real chance to roar, with Ilona Maher's comeback as the wildcard. If you want opening-day rugby with atmosphere, take the evening over the morning.

significance.explanation: Final pool round, where seeding and quarterfinal spots are settled. Stakes are as sharp as pool play gets, but no medals change hands.

experience.explanation: Thursday morning with teams chasing results gives urgency to a daytime slot. Close sight lines help, and the energy builds as scoreboards matter.

starPower.explanation: Canada, Australia and the U.S. all have Paris-level pedigree, and with stakes high the top names will be fully engaged.

uniqueness.explanation: Pool-deciding day with real jeopardy, in a sport back for a fourth Games. Tension is good, but it is still a group-stage session.

demand.explanation: A weekday-morning pool slot is among the easier tickets in the tournament. Still a Games ticket in a tournament tracking toward full houses.

scorecard.overall: Calculator rugby: lose and you fall to the 9-12 bracket, win and you are in the medal hunt. Good tension for a morning, and a smart pick for fans who like drama without a premium price.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinals: win and you are two steps from gold, lose and the medal race is over. The 9-12 matches add little but depth.

experience.explanation: Four win-or-go-home matches in a late-afternoon window at a compact stadium. First session where every match has heat.

starPower.explanation: Quarterfinals should carry New Zealand, Canada, Australia and likely the U.S., a strong cast of Paris semifinalists.

uniqueness.explanation: Knockout rugby with a possible Canada-U.S. rematch and New Zealand chasing a three-peat. Good storylines, though not a medal day.

demand.explanation: First knockout evening of the women's event, with the host nation likely in action. A prime-time session that should be competitive to book.

scorecard.overall: The first night where every match can end a medal dream. Three hours, four quarterfinals, and a good chance of a Canada-U.S. rematch with the home crowd loud.

significance.explanation: Two semifinals send winners to a gold-medal match and losers to bronze. A big step up, though the medals come that evening.

experience.explanation: Saturday afternoon, sun low and crowd settled, with two semifinals in a compact ground. Weekend timing helps the atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: The top four sides are on show, with Maddison Levi and possibly Ilona Maher. This is the sport's best women's talent in one session.

uniqueness.explanation: Semifinals in a sport with strong recent history of theater. Memorable, but the medal matches land in the later session.

demand.explanation: Weekend semifinals with the host nation a likely contender make this a hard ticket. It should be one of the first women's sessions to go.

scorecard.overall: Two matches decide who plays for gold, on a Saturday afternoon with nerves showing. If you want rugby's best women's sides under real pressure but at a lower price than the evening, this is it.

significance.explanation: Women's gold and bronze are decided in one night, the first rugby medals of the Games. Not a marquee sport, but two medals in one evening.

experience.explanation: Saturday night under lights, medals on the line, 27,000 fans close to the field. Rugby's best evening setup.

starPower.explanation: New Zealand, Australia's Maddison Levi, Canada and possibly Ilona Maher. A strong cast of faces, though rugby's stars are not global to the level of a football or athletics final.

uniqueness.explanation: First medals of the tournament, a possible New Zealand three-peat, and an Australia-New Zealand rivalry that produced a 22-21 comeback in New York. Rare stakes.

demand.explanation: Medal night in a sport that set Paris attendance records. With a possible U.S. bronze match, expect a scramble.

scorecard.overall: The women's gold medal match, with the sport's best rivalry plausibly on the pitch and a three-peat on the line. This is the prime ticket in women's rugby, in a venue that makes every try feel close.

significance.explanation: Opening men's pool play: advancement stakes only, with plenty of rugby to come. A slow start is recoverable.

experience.explanation: Sunday morning opener at a compact stadium with clear sight lines. Fun for fans, but short of evening atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: South Africa, France and Fiji are all among the likely entries. Big names in rugby, though Dupont's availability is unknown.

uniqueness.explanation: The men start after the women for the first time, so this morning marks a new order for the sport. A neat wrinkle for an otherwise routine pool day.

demand.explanation: Morning pool play is the softer ticket in the men's schedule. Still likely to sell, given rugby's crowds in Paris.

scorecard.overall: A fresh tournament, a new running order, and the first look at South Africa, France and Fiji. Take it for a lower-pressure morning with a chance to spot the team that arrives sharp.

significance.explanation: Pool play again, with seeding and quarterfinal routes the only stakes. Nothing is decided yet.

experience.explanation: Sunday evening in Carson, with Fiji's flair under lights. The atmosphere is the best of the pool days.

starPower.explanation: France, Fiji and South Africa are in the mix, and the Antoine Dupont question adds buzz even if the chance is slim.

uniqueness.explanation: Fiji looking to atone against a France side that took their crown in Paris adds spice. Still a pool game.

demand.explanation: Sunday evening with a strong field is the hotter men's pool ticket. The Dupont chatter helps.

scorecard.overall: Fiji's fireworks under lights, France's defence of the title, and a Dupont maybe. The best men's pool-play slot if you want evening buzz.

significance.explanation: Last pool round: quarterfinal places are on the line, but no medals. Teams that slip drop to the 9-12 bracket.

experience.explanation: Monday morning with scoreboard-watching tension makes for a good atmosphere, even in daylight. Close seats help.

starPower.explanation: Top sides need results, so the stars play. The U.S. and Argentina add recognizable names.

uniqueness.explanation: Pool-deciding games where one try can end a run. Tense, but a standard group-stage finale.

demand.explanation: A weekday-morning session is an easier ticket. Games scarcity keeps it from being easy.

scorecard.overall: Pool play's pressure cooker: one try can separate a quarterfinal from the 9-12 bracket. A good-value morning for people who like tension without a medal attached.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinals: four teams out of the medal race, four closer to it. Elimination stakes, but gold is still two rounds away.

experience.explanation: Four knockout matches in a Monday evening window in a compact ground. Elimination rugby gives every match heat.

starPower.explanation: South Africa, Fiji, France and New Zealand are all likely here. Strong names in the sport, even without a confirmed global star.

uniqueness.explanation: A possible first U.S. men's medal run in front of a home crowd gives this session an extra storyline. It is still a quarterfinal.

demand.explanation: Knockout rugby on a Monday evening, with the host nation possibly involved. A competitive ticket.

scorecard.overall: Every match is a possible elimination, and a home U.S. quarterfinal would be the loudest of the week. A strong pick for knockout drama a day before the medals.

significance.explanation: Two semifinals send winners to the gold match and losers to bronze. The medal match is the evening's business, so this is a step before it.

experience.explanation: Tuesday afternoon semifinals with the best men's teams in a close-in stadium. Strong, though the night session carries more atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: South Africa, Fiji, France and New Zealand are the likely semifinalists, with Dupont a possible wildcard. The best rugby sevens names on one pitch.

uniqueness.explanation: A South Africa-France or Fiji rematch with title stakes adds depth. Semifinals rather than medals, though.

demand.explanation: Semifinal day in a sport with proven crowd appeal. Likely to sell before the quarterfinal sessions do.

scorecard.overall: Two semifinals between the sport's biggest names, with Fiji, South Africa and France all in the frame. A strong afternoon if the evening finals are out of reach.

significance.explanation: Men's gold and bronze are decided in the final rugby session of the Games. Two medals in one evening, though rugby is not a marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Closing night of the rugby, under lights, 27,000 fans inches from the touchline. Fiji and South Africa supporters bring the volume.

starPower.explanation: France, Fiji and South Africa carry the rugby world's biggest names, and a Dupont return would lift this further. Tournament headliners, if not global ones.

uniqueness.explanation: The tournament's last match, with Fiji seeking revenge on France and the U.S. chasing a first men's medal. Rare stakes in a sport with a short Games history.

demand.explanation: Men's medal night, the closing session of a sport that drew record crowds in Paris. A scramble for seats.

scorecard.overall: Fiji's flair against France's champions, with South Africa as the form team, and a possible home-nation run. It is the finale of Games rugby and the best ticket of the men's week.

significance.explanation: Opening qualifying day for the kite fleet. Real points on the line for seeding, but nobody leaves with a medal or an elimination.

experience.explanation: Afternoon racing from the sand by Belmont pier, with kites close to shore. Easy to follow, though a qualifying format lacks finals-day roar.

starPower.explanation: Max Maeder, Lauriane Nolot, Daniela Moroz and Paris medalists are all on the water. Big names in a niche sport, so a mid-tier score.

uniqueness.explanation: A first look at a returning sport on the same Long Beach coast that hosted sailing in 1984. Qualifying day one is still routine.

demand.explanation: Free-feeling beach setting and a niche sport make this one of the easier tickets in a sold-out Games.

scorecard.overall: The softest ticket of the kite week, but a fun one: you see the whole fleet, the favorites settling in, and the shoreline set-up before finals-day crowds arrive. Good for sailing fans and curious locals.

significance.explanation: Qualifying races only, though windsurfing's opening day sets the early order on brand-new sail sizes.

experience.explanation: Two disciplines on the water at once off Belmont Shore, so there is plenty to watch. Afternoon sun, a beach crowd, and no medals yet.

starPower.explanation: Steinberg, van Opzeeland and Paris bronze medalist van Opzeeland headline windsurfing while Maeder and Nolot keep kite names in play.

uniqueness.explanation: Windsurfing's first racing day, on resized 8 and 7.3 square meter sails. Intriguing gear story, but still early-round racing.

demand.explanation: Two-discipline sessions add some appeal, yet qualifying in a niche sport remains a more accessible booking.

scorecard.overall: Come to watch windsurfing open with new sails and see whether the gear change reshuffles the order. It is a two-for-one afternoon with kite still running, but the real drama comes later in the week.

significance.explanation: Last kite qualifying day decides who reaches tomorrow's medal races. Cut-line pressure makes this more than routine.

experience.explanation: Cutoff tension on the kite course plus windsurfing day two, all visible from the sand. Pleasant, but no medal ceremony energy.

starPower.explanation: Reigning champions Reuveny, Maggetti and Bontus all race here, with Kantor and Stragiotti in the mix. A deep list of Paris names.

uniqueness.explanation: Watching a champion like Maggetti fight a bad stretch adds spice. Structurally it is still a qualifying day.

demand.explanation: Qualifying sailing at a beach venue is a less competitive booking, though the kite cut-off adds interest.

scorecard.overall: The best of the qualifying days: kite riders are fighting for finals spots and defending champions have little room for error. A smart, cheaper way to see the Paris names before medals.

significance.explanation: Two kite gold medals, the first of the sailing program, decided in one session. Windsurfing qualifying adds a little more.

experience.explanation: Medal races close to the beach, crowded shoreline, and every crash and gybe visible from the sand. Afternoon light on the Long Beach coast.

starPower.explanation: Maeder, Stragiotti and Bontus on the men's side; Nolot, Kampman and Moroz among the women. Confirmed world champions all over the fleet.

uniqueness.explanation: Kite's second Games medals and the first sailing golds of 2028, on 1984's sailing coast. Rare, though the sport itself is a returning one.

demand.explanation: Medal day for a mid-tier sport at a beach venue. Expect it to sell, with strong appeal for locals and sailing fans.

scorecard.overall: The first sailing medals of the Games come with a beach crowd, a Maeder versus Stragiotti duel, and Moroz chasing a medal on home water. Easily the best pick of the board-sailing week.

significance.explanation: Two windsurfing golds decided in a short session, the first medal races on the class's new sail sizes.

experience.explanation: Short, concentrated medal racing from the shoreline in the afternoon. Compact and tense, with a beach atmosphere rather than a stadium roar.

starPower.explanation: Reuveny, van Opzeeland, Steinberg, Kantor, Maggetti and Emma Wilson give this a Paris medal-stand reunion feel.

uniqueness.explanation: Closing the board-sailing program on resized sails adds novelty, and the head-to-head match-point format is unusual. Still a returning sport at a beach venue.

demand.explanation: Medal day for a mid-tier sport, with a compact window and a strong Israeli and Dutch following. Competitive, but more reachable than marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: A tight three-hour finale where nerve decides everything, with Israeli rivals and Reuveny against van Opzeeland on new gear. Go for a concentrated, high-tension medal show on the sand.

significance.explanation: Opening day of the dinghy qualifying series. Nobody wins a medal, but a bad first day can sink a week.

experience.explanation: Afternoon racing viewed from the San Pedro shore, with container ships as the backdrop. Sailing is harder to follow than most sports, but the setting is distinctive.

starPower.explanation: Fields include world champions like Vadnai and Charlotte Rose, plus Paris 2024 medalists if they qualify. Few household names, though.

uniqueness.explanation: Sailing returns to the harbor that hosted the 1932 regatta. The session itself is routine fleet racing, so the history carries the score.

demand.explanation: Opening-day sailing is the easier ticket of the regatta, with no medals and a niche following.

scorecard.overall: A quiet but atmospheric start, with sailing back on 1932 waters and giant ships passing behind. Come for the setting and the first look at the fleet, not for medal drama.

significance.explanation: Still all qualifying races, but with four fleets on the water and two new classes starting their series.

experience.explanation: Foiling Nacra 17 catamarans plus 470 dinghies make this the most varied watching so far, viewed from the shore.

starPower.explanation: Gimson and Burnet, Xammar and Cardona, and the Paris 2024 champion nations of Italy and Austria are all in play. Strong names mostly for sailing fans.

uniqueness.explanation: Early-round racing, though foiling multihulls sailing in front of a working port is a visual you will not see elsewhere.

demand.explanation: A prelim day in a niche sport, so an easier ticket, though the Games scarcity still applies.

scorecard.overall: The best early-week pick for variety, with foiling cats and tactical 470s sharing the bay. It is a prelim day with no podiums, but the shoreline view makes it a good first taste.

significance.explanation: Qualifying races only, with the skiff medals still three days out. Results shape the pecking order, not the podium.

experience.explanation: The fast, acrobatic skiffs debut alongside the other fleets, so the harbor is at its busiest.

starPower.explanation: Paris 2024 gold medalists Botín and Trittel, plus the 2026 world champions from New Zealand and Norway, start here.

uniqueness.explanation: A skiff opening day is still early-round racing. The full-fleet harbor scene adds some flavor.

demand.explanation: Skiffs arriving with four other fleets makes this a bit more sought after than the opening days, though no medals are awarded.

scorecard.overall: The skiffs bring the sharpest form guide of the regatta, with Spain, New Zealand and Norway all trading world titles. Go to scout the favorites before medals begin.

significance.explanation: Two dinghy golds are decided, ILCA 7 and ILCA 6. That is a double-medal day in a non-marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Medal-race drama viewed from shore, with skiffs and mixed fleets adding to the harbor activity. Sailing remains tricky for newcomers to follow.

starPower.explanation: Paris 2024 medalists Wearn, Kontides and Bouwmeester are possible, along with home hope Charlotte Rose and world champion Vadnai.

uniqueness.explanation: A standard medal day in an established sport, but with a possible American contender and a historic harbor setting.

demand.explanation: The first medals of the boat regatta and the possible home medal chance make it a more competitive ticket than the prelims.

scorecard.overall: The first boat medals of the regatta, decided by tiny margins in the dinghy fleets. If Charlotte Rose is in the mix, the shore crowd could get loud.

significance.explanation: Two gold medals, in the 470 and Nacra 17, are decided, with the skiff series moving into its third day.

experience.explanation: Foiling cats at 20-plus knots are the most thrilling sailing to watch, and the shoreline lets you follow the whole race.

starPower.explanation: Gimson and Burnet's three world titles, Xammar and Cardona, and Italy's defending Nacra champions bring serious pedigree.

uniqueness.explanation: Mixed-gender foiling and 470 finals are a standard medal format, but a foiling final beside a working port is memorable.

demand.explanation: Two medal events and the best viewing spectacle make this the pick of the sailing tickets before the final day.

scorecard.overall: The best spectacle of the regatta, with foiling catamarans racing for gold and a possible 470 rematch. It is a strong value for a medal day.

significance.explanation: The last two medals of the sailing regatta, men's and women's skiff, are decided in a short three-hour window.

experience.explanation: Fast skiffs sprinting in the harbor, with a short session that packs the drama into a few hours.

starPower.explanation: Spain's Botín and Trittel, Paris 2024 champions, face Menzies, who also co-helms an America's Cup boat, and the three-time world champions from the Netherlands.

uniqueness.explanation: Closing out the sailing programme gives this a finale feel, and last-race swings are likely on this stage.

demand.explanation: Final medals, a short session and a closing-day atmosphere make this the top sailing ticket.

scorecard.overall: Sailing's finale is the one to book if you can only see one session, with the last two golds decided and Paris 2024 champions in the mix. The finish could easily come down to a single point.

significance.explanation: Two gold medals in one long Saturday, men's and women's air rifle. Medal-deciding stakes in a non-marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Afternoon-into-evening session in a temporary hall beside the Long Beach waterfront. Hushed, tense and distinctive, though it's a sport that asks for patience.

starPower.explanation: Sheng Lihao and Ban Hyojin headline as Paris 2024 champions and recent world champions. Big names inside shooting, less so beyond it.

uniqueness.explanation: Gold medals in a standard, established format at a temporary hall. The convention center's 1984 fencing history adds a little local flavor.

demand.explanation: Mid-tier sport finals with two golds on offer. Games scarcity keeps it competitive, but it's an easier ticket than marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: A one-point margin decided the men's world title in Doha, and this session offers two chances at that kind of drama. It's a quiet, intense Saturday for people who like precision and scoreboard tension.

significance.explanation: Men's and women's air pistol golds are both decided before nine o'clock. Two medal finals in a single session.

experience.explanation: Sunday afternoon and evening in the Long Beach hall, with a compact format that keeps finals moving. Quiet, focused and easy to pair with nearby venues.

starPower.explanation: Manu Bhaker's Paris 2024 bronze gives it a global name if she qualifies, and China's Jiang Ranxin and Hu Kai bring world-title form.

uniqueness.explanation: An established-format medal day without a new twist. The Bhaker comeback storyline gives it some extra edge.

demand.explanation: Two golds and a possible Indian fan surge lift interest. Still a mid-tier sport, so a softer ask than marquee finals.

scorecard.overall: Air pistol is shooting at its most distilled, and Doha's 0.3-point women's final shows how thin the margin is. If Bhaker makes the field, the room gets a real storyline.

significance.explanation: Day one of skeet qualification: no medals, but a miss here can quietly end a campaign before the final field is set.

experience.explanation: A 9:30 AM start on open-air parkland, with stands right behind the stations. Pleasant and close-up, but a long daytime session without prime-time energy.

starPower.explanation: Vincent Hancock chasing a fifth gold, plus world champion Samantha Simonton and Paris champion Francisca Crovetto, gives this prelim real names.

uniqueness.explanation: Hancock's possible farewell lap adds a storyline, and shooting at Whittier Narrows is new for the Games. Still, it's a qualification day, not a deciding one.

demand.explanation: Qualification at a roughly 2,000-seat range. Home-crowd curiosity about Hancock keeps it competitive, but it's the easier skeet ticket.

scorecard.overall: The best way to watch Hancock and Simonton up close without finals pressure on ticket prices or crowds. You see who is dropping zero birds before the medal day, and the gold hunt starts here.

significance.explanation: Two mixed team golds are decided here. The shared score means each shot counts twice as much emotionally.

experience.explanation: Elimination format brings real momentum swings, and the late-afternoon start suits a hall that gets louder as teams drop out.

starPower.explanation: Sheng Lihao, Ban Hyojin and Hu Kai are likely to feature. Strong shooting names, mostly unknown beyond the sport.

uniqueness.explanation: One combined four-team elimination final replaces the old gold and bronze matches. A format debut makes this the freshest shooting session of the Games.

demand.explanation: Mid-tier sport but with medal stakes and a novel format. Competitive to book, though not at marquee-final levels.

scorecard.overall: The new four-team elimination final is the most dramatic format in shooting, and Doha showed it can end a favorite's run by under a point. This is the best pick for newcomers.

significance.explanation: Two gold medals in one day, with the new eight-shooter final. Every target counts when a single miss can swing the podium.

experience.explanation: All-day shooting with finals in the afternoon, a hushed crowd and clays crossing green parkland. Intimate, though the venue is small and the sport is quiet.

starPower.explanation: Hancock's world-record 36 and bid for a fifth gold headline, with Simonton, Crovetto and Jiang Yiting alongside. Few shooting days carry more recognizable names.

uniqueness.explanation: A possible historic fifth gold for Hancock at a home Games, in the new eight-athlete final format. Rare combination for shooting.

demand.explanation: Medal day for two events, and the hottest shotgun ticket thanks to the US storyline. The venue's small capacity keeps it tough to book.

scorecard.overall: This is the pick of the shotgun program: two skeet golds and Hancock's shot at history in front of a home crowd. Quiet, tense and intimate, with a longer final ladder that gives drama room to build.

significance.explanation: One gold-medal final in a morning session, decided under the new standing-and-elimination format.

experience.explanation: A 9:30 AM start in a quiet hall, with a long qualification before the final. Standing-only drama is a real payoff for patient viewers.

starPower.explanation: Liu Yukun is the Paris 2024 champion and Zhang Changhong holds a final world record of 363.0. Strong names in shooting circles.

uniqueness.explanation: The revised final format debuts here, with kneeling and prone merged and standing deciding medals. A rules debut gives it a rarer feel.

demand.explanation: Morning slot and a niche discipline make this an easier ticket among medal sessions. Still a Games gold.

scorecard.overall: Come early for the new standing-only final, where nerves show and a 0.2-point gap decided the last world title. It's a smaller stage, but a good one for sport fans and an easy pairing with Long Beach neighbors.
