significance.explanation: One women's gold-medal final decided in a morning session, under a new elimination-style standing finish.

experience.explanation: A 9:30 AM start in a quiet hall and a long qualification stretch. The standing finish gives a tense payoff for patient viewers.

starPower.explanation: Paris 2024 champion Chiara Leone, silver medalist Sagen Maddalena and Doha winner Aleksandra Stojadinovic give it solid names.

uniqueness.explanation: The new final format debuts here, and a possible home medal threat in Maddalena adds extra local color.

demand.explanation: Morning, niche discipline, one medal. A home-nation American hopeful could lift interest, but it's still a gentler booking.

scorecard.overall: Stojadinovic won Doha with her last shot, and the new standing finish should make that kind of ending more common. A Maddalena run would give Long Beach a hometown moment.

significance.explanation: Trap qualification day one. Eight final spots are at stake, but nothing is awarded and plenty of time remains to recover.

experience.explanation: Morning start, big field, and shooters rotating through stations in a park setting. Great for sport fans, slower going for casual visitors.

starPower.explanation: World champions Josip Glasnovic and Mar Molne Magrina, American Will Hinton, and Nathan Hales are all names to watch, even if shooting stars are lesser known.

uniqueness.explanation: A standard qualification day in an established discipline. Trap at Whittier Narrows is new, but the session itself is routine.

demand.explanation: Early prelim at a small venue is the easier shotgun ticket, though Games scarcity still means it isn't an automatic get.

scorecard.overall: A low-pressure way to see the whole trap field up close, and watch a favorite wobble. Hales finishing 78th in Athens shows that anyone can slip, which makes this prelim more interesting than it sounds.

significance.explanation: Qualification only. Men's rapid fire stage 1 and women's precision are about advancement, with no medals decided.

experience.explanation: A 9:30 AM start for two qualification stages in a quiet hall. Rewarding for sport fans, but long and low on spectacle.

starPower.explanation: Clement Bessaguet, Florian Peter and Manu Bhaker could all appear. Familiar names in shooting, though not household ones.

uniqueness.explanation: Qualification stages of established events, but rapid fire's five-target rhythm and the world-record chase give it a bit of intrigue.

demand.explanation: Daytime qualification of a niche sport is the easiest booking in this batch. Still, Games tickets are scarce.

scorecard.overall: This is the sport's study hall, and a good chance to watch rapid fire's strange rhythm up close without the finals crowd. It's an easy ticket and a great one for curious fans.

significance.explanation: Two trap golds are decided in one day, via the new eight-shooter finals. Medal stakes in a sport where every bird matters.

experience.explanation: Finals stretch into the late afternoon at a close-quarters range, with a hushed crowd and clays across the fields. Atmospheric rather than loud.

starPower.explanation: Adriana Ruano, Nathan Hales, Josip Glasnovic, Mar Molne Magrina and Will Hinton could all feature. Strong names for shooting, less so by global standards.

uniqueness.explanation: Guatemala's first-ever gold winner and Hales's Games-record final set up possible title defenses in a new eight-shooter format at a first-time venue.

demand.explanation: Medal day with limited seating at the range. A strong pick for those who miss out on skeet finals.

scorecard.overall: Two trap golds in a day, with defending champions Ruano and Hales facing a loaded field. Smaller stage than the marquee finals, but a tense, quiet and rewarding afternoon for those who like to watch the sport.

significance.explanation: Two golds in one day, men's rapid fire and women's 25m pistol, with an eight-shooter final and a full qualification run behind it.

experience.explanation: A long day running into the evening in the Long Beach hall. Hit-or-miss tension peaks in the finals, but the format asks for stamina.

starPower.explanation: Yang Jiin's world-record form, Bessaguet, Peter and Manu Bhaker's Games profile make this a strong shooting lineup.

uniqueness.explanation: The rapid fire final's expansion to eight shooters debuts alongside a women's pistol final built on hits and misses.

demand.explanation: Two medal finals and a Sunday evening finish make this the toughest shooting ticket in the batch outside the mixed team final.

scorecard.overall: This is shooting's big finale: eight men in rapid fire and the world-record shooter Yang Jiin in the women's final. If you only book one pistol day, make it this one.

significance.explanation: A single gold in the debut of mixed team trap at the Games. The four-team final means no safety net of a bronze match.

experience.explanation: Qualifying and the final in one day, with four teams shooting at once. A new format that should be easier to follow than usual.

starPower.explanation: Italy's Fabbrizi and Iezzi, San Marino's Berti and Perilli, and the US pair of Eller and Downs bring names, though less global fame.

uniqueness.explanation: Brand-new event for the Games, first run at home in a new four-team simultaneous final format. A genuine first for the sport.

demand.explanation: One medal and a smaller crowd, but novelty and the home team's chances keep it competitive. A less contested shotgun ticket.

scorecard.overall: A brand-new event with a new final format, and a USA pair that already has a world medal. Come to see something nobody has seen at the Games before; it's a smaller stage, but a rare one.

significance.explanation: Prelim round: 22 skaters fighting for finals spots. Real stakes for advancement, but no medals are handed out tonight.

experience.explanation: Late-afternoon light, an open-air course and skaters close at hand make for a relaxed, watchable session. The temporary Sepulveda Basin venue is more park than palace.

starPower.explanation: Leal, Yoshizawa, Oda and Matsumoto could all be on the course, and prelims are where you see them without final-round tension. Names are big within skating, less so beyond it.

uniqueness.explanation: A prelim in an established-again sport, though skateboarding's Southern California roots add some homecoming flavor. Still one step before the main event.

demand.explanation: Early-round skateboarding at a temporary venue should be an easier ticket than the finals, though Games scarcity still applies.

scorecard.overall: Watch the field sort itself out before the pressure peaks, with Leal's comeback bid and Japan's deep bench both on display. It's a relaxed way to see the stars up close, at a smaller stage than the final.

significance.explanation: Qualification round, with 22 skaters chasing a handful of final spots. Everyone in the field is in survival mode.

experience.explanation: Morning sun and an open course, but a 10:30 AM start at a temporary venue lacks prime-time buzz.

starPower.explanation: Horigome, Huston, Onodera and Shirai are the draws, and a Huston comeback would be the story. Headliners may be on course, though no one is guaranteed to be.

uniqueness.explanation: Huston's return from a skull fracture could be a real storyline here, but this is still a routine prelim in format.

demand.explanation: Morning prelim of a youth-driven sport at a park venue. Sellout momentum still applies, but this is among the easier skateboarding tickets.

scorecard.overall: A sunny-morning look at street skating's changing of the guard, with Huston's possible comeback against a young, fast Japanese wave. It's an easier ticket than the final and a good pick for genuine skate fans.

significance.explanation: Gold, silver and bronze are decided in a single evening final. A non-marquee sport, but this is the medal moment.

experience.explanation: Under the lights at 8:30 PM, the Sepulveda Basin course gets prime-time energy. Short, tense program with trick-by-trick swings.

starPower.explanation: Yoshizawa, Oda, Matsumoto, Leal and Covell form a deep, recognizable field of teenage stars. Few sports pack this many young headliners into one final.

uniqueness.explanation: Street finals regularly come down to the last trick, which makes this tense, but the format is established and the venue is temporary.

demand.explanation: Evening medal final with Japan, Brazil and Australia all in contention. One of the hottest skateboarding tickets on the schedule.

scorecard.overall: The best skate ticket for drama, with last-trick finishes the norm and the sport's teenage stars all in range. Under the lights in the Valley, it's the one to book if you want a medal and a gasp.

significance.explanation: Men's Street gold is on the line, a non-marquee final but a medal session where one last trick can reshuffle the podium.

experience.explanation: Night final under lights in the Sepulveda Basin, with skateboarding's loud, trick-by-trick crowd energy. A temporary park venue keeps it intimate rather than iconic.

starPower.explanation: Horigome, Eaton and Huston headline a field stacked with Japan's Shirai and Sasaki Toa. Skateboarding's best-known names, and a few household ones.

uniqueness.explanation: Street skating's Games medal round returns to its Southern California home turf, in a one-off temporary venue in the Valley, a first for the region.

demand.explanation: Prime-time medal session in a home-soil sport with American fan favorites. Expect a competitive ticket, even if the venue is modest.

scorecard.overall: Skateboarding comes home to California for a night final where the last trick can flip the podium. Horigome's defense against a deep Japanese wave and two Americans makes this the street ticket to chase, even on a smaller stage.

significance.explanation: Prelim round: 22 skaters fighting for a spot in the final. Real stakes for advancement, but no medal is handed out.

experience.explanation: Late-morning sun in a Sepulveda Basin park setting, a bowl-style run format that's easy to follow, and the whole field in one sitting. Daytime keeps it below the night finals.

starPower.explanation: Palmer, Schaar, Khury, Akio and world champion Bijueska are all expected to drop in, so top names are on the deck from the first run.

uniqueness.explanation: A temporary skatepark in the San Fernando Valley hosting the Games for the first time gives it a novelty edge, though this is still a preliminary.

demand.explanation: Morning prelim at a temporary venue, so easier to land than the finals, but skateboarding's cool factor and Games scarcity keep it moving.

scorecard.overall: The best way to see every contender in one sitting, with a chance to spot who's peaking before the final. It's the lower-pressure, easier-ticket route into park skating, but you give up medal-night drama.

significance.explanation: Qualifying round, so the stakes are advancement rather than medals. Still, a bad first run can end a podium contender's night.

experience.explanation: Night-sky session in the Valley, with lights, music and a bowl full of trick-heavy runs. Prime-time atmosphere without final-night pressure.

starPower.explanation: Hasegawa, Sky Brown, Hiraki and Trew form one of the most recognizable podium groups in the sport, and all are expected to skate here.

uniqueness.explanation: Seeing Japan's depth squeezed by the three-skater cap adds a layer of intrigue, but this is still an early round at a temporary venue.

demand.explanation: Evening slot plus a loaded women's field makes this a busier ticket than the morning prelim, though it is still short of final-night heat.

scorecard.overall: Night prelims with the full star lineup are a smart pick if finals are sold out. Watch for who is gaining momentum, and for which Japanese skaters survive the nation cap.

significance.explanation: Men's park gold in a non-marquee sport, with Palmer chasing a third straight title. A medal session in every sense.

experience.explanation: Wednesday night under lights with just 75 minutes of high-wire skating. Volatile runs keep the crowd on edge.

starPower.explanation: Palmer, Bijueska, Schaar and Khury make a final with real name recognition, with a California homecoming for Bottger and Palmer's San Diego ties.

uniqueness.explanation: Only the third men's park final ever, in the sport's home region. Palmer's potential three-peat adds a historic edge.

demand.explanation: Skateboarding finals at a compact Valley venue will draw crowds, and limited capacity makes this one of the hotter tickets of the Games' early days.

scorecard.overall: Skating's best kind of chaos: a prodigy world champion against a two-time Games champion, with a final that could be decided by a single clean run. Short, loud, and unpredictable.

significance.explanation: Women's park gold, in a non-marquee sport but with a podium race that could again come down to under a point.

experience.explanation: Thursday night under lights, a tight 75-minute final, and a field that routinely puts together huge runs. Compact and loud.

starPower.explanation: Trew, Hiraki, Brown and Hasegawa headline a final stocked with the biggest names in women's skateboarding.

uniqueness.explanation: Third women's park final, in skateboarding's home region, with the Paris podium's 0.87-point spread hanging over a likely rematch.

demand.explanation: Evening medal session with a star-heavy lineup, in a small temporary venue where seats are limited. Expect competition for tickets.

scorecard.overall: A rematch of a Paris final decided by less than a point, now with Hasegawa's record-setting run added. If you want one skateboarding medal night, this is the one with the deepest field.

significance.explanation: Round of 16 means survival only, but single elimination makes every match a cliff edge for 16 players in the draw.

experience.explanation: Evening start on the Back to the Future courthouse square, with temporary stands close to the glass. Novelty carries it more than the round.

starPower.explanation: Asian Games champions Ng Eain Yow and Sivasangari Subramaniam are locked in; top-ranked Egyptians may or may not open tonight.

uniqueness.explanation: The first squash match ever played at a Summer Games, staged on a film backlot. Opening-night bragging rights are the draw.

demand.explanation: A niche sport's opening round, but a small venue and the debut buzz keep it a competitive book.

scorecard.overall: Be there for the very first ball of Games squash, hit on a movie backlot under studio lights. The matches are early-round and the names uncertain, but you can say you saw the sport's opening night.

significance.explanation: One-and-done Round of 16 with real advancement stakes, but no medals in play yet.

experience.explanation: Night-time glass-court squash on a studio lot is a vivid setting; rallies are fast and easy to enjoy up close.

starPower.explanation: Could feature the 18-year-old Anahat Singh, who stunned eight-time champion Nour El Sherbini, plus Egyptian elite; not guaranteed.

uniqueness.explanation: Early round of a debut sport, with upset potential baked into a knockout bracket.

demand.explanation: Second night of an early round at a small temporary venue; likely to sell but less contested.

scorecard.overall: A good pick for upset hunters: a knockout draw, young challengers and a backlot setting that feels like a premiere. It is a cheaper way into the debut sport than the medal nights.

significance.explanation: Round of 16 stakes: win and you are in the quarterfinals, lose and the Games are over.

experience.explanation: Open-air backlot courts at night, with a mix of stars and qualifier stories keeping the matches varied.

starPower.explanation: England's ElShorbagy brothers, ranked ninth and 10th, are recognizable names to squash fans, with an elite supporting field.

uniqueness.explanation: Brothers possibly sharing a Games draw, plus a Seattle qualifier winner, give this debut-sport round a story.

demand.explanation: Mid-tier sport, early round, small venue; still a Games ticket but less of a scramble.

scorecard.overall: The ElShorbagy brothers and a qualifier-route Cinderella give this night more narrative than a typical early round. It suits squash fans who like the depth of the bracket.

significance.explanation: Last Round of 16 night finalizes the quarterfinal fields; high stakes for advancement, no medals yet.

experience.explanation: Closing the round at night under the lights, with matches that decide the bracket and a home crowd for American qualifiers.

starPower.explanation: Paul Coll and Diego Elias, the 2026 US Open finalists, could close the night; Egyptian stars are likely nearby.

uniqueness.explanation: Final night of the first squash round in Games history, played without retired legend Ali Farag.

demand.explanation: Still a Games session at a small venue, though bracket-setting stakes and home players add pull.

scorecard.overall: The last chance to see the field before the medal rounds, with big names like Coll and Elias possibly on court. Good value if you want top-level squash without medal-night prices.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinal: win and you are one match from a medal, lose and you leave with nothing.

experience.explanation: Stakes finally feel heavy, and the small temporary stands around the glass court make every rally intimate.

starPower.explanation: Mostafa Asal, back-to-back world champion, and Hania El Hammamy headline a deep Egyptian-led field.

uniqueness.explanation: Knockout round of a debut sport, where the first-ever medal hopefuls are decided.

demand.explanation: Quarterfinals with world champions on court; a hotter ticket than the opening rounds.

scorecard.overall: This is where stakes and star power meet: world champion Asal and El Hammamy are in the mix and a podium spot is one win away. Probably the best value in the tournament.

significance.explanation: Second quarterfinal night completes the semifinal lineups; the winners are guaranteed a shot at a medal.

experience.explanation: Late-night squash with semifinal places on the line, in a venue where the crowd sits within a few meters of the glass.

starPower.explanation: Coll and Elias could meet again after the US Open final; Amina Orfi and Olivia Weaver add women's draw pull.

uniqueness.explanation: No one has ever won a squash medal at the Games, and tonight decides who gets the first shot.

demand.explanation: Quarterfinal stakes and recognizable names make it a more contested ticket than the earlier rounds.

scorecard.overall: A strong quarterfinal night with Coll, Elias, Orfi and possible home hope Weaver, plus the first semifinal lineups in the sport's Games history. Pick it for star density.

significance.explanation: Women's semifinals: the winners reach gold and the losers still play for bronze, so medals are one step away.

experience.explanation: Late start, two matches, tense hush between points in an intimate backlot setting.

starPower.explanation: Amina Orfi, the youngest women's world No. 1, and Egypt's string of world champions likely feature; Weaver adds a US angle.

uniqueness.explanation: Semifinals of the first-ever Games squash women's event, with a historic medal race taking shape.

demand.explanation: Semifinal stakes in a debut sport at a tiny venue make seats scarce.

scorecard.overall: The women's semifinals offer the sport's best players one step from history. Egypt's depth against a two-per-country cap makes for sharp, high-level squash in a very small room.

significance.explanation: Men's semifinals send winners to gold and losers to bronze; a medal is within reach for all four players.

experience.explanation: Saturday night squash on the backlot, with the sport's biggest rivalries potentially in play.

starPower.explanation: Asal, Coll and Elias are the sport's biggest names, with two straight world titles and a US Open final between them.

uniqueness.explanation: First-ever Games squash semifinals for men, with a Farag-less field deciding who inherits the sport.

demand.explanation: Weekend semifinal night with top-ranked names; a hot ticket for a niche sport.

scorecard.overall: If you want the best men's squash at the Games, this is the night: Asal, Coll and Elias could all be fighting for a final berth on a Saturday evening.

significance.explanation: Two medal matches, bronze then gold, award the first women's squash medals ever at a Games.

experience.explanation: Podium-night atmosphere in a small temporary venue; the quiet before each serve will be electric.

starPower.explanation: Orfi, Gohar, El Sherbini and El Hammamy form the sport's elite; at least one should be on court.

uniqueness.explanation: The very first women's squash gold medal in Games history, handed out on a Hollywood backlot.

demand.explanation: Medal night in a debut sport with a few thousand seats; among the hardest squash tickets.

scorecard.overall: A coronation with no precedent: the first women's squash champion crowned in a Back to the Future courthouse square. Not a marquee sport, but the rarest squash ticket going.

significance.explanation: The first men's squash gold and bronze are decided, closing the tournament.

experience.explanation: Late finish near midnight on a film lot, with a bronze opener and gold match building tension.

starPower.explanation: Asal, Coll and Elias have all beaten each other on big stages; any pair gives a star-driven final.

uniqueness.explanation: The first men's squash champion in Games history, crowned at the final squash session ever held there.

demand.explanation: Closing medal night with a tiny venue capacity and global names makes it squash's top ticket.

scorecard.overall: The marquee night for squash: a first men's gold, likely featuring Asal, Coll or Elias, in a one-of-a-kind setting. It is a smaller stage than the big finals, but unrepeatable.

significance.explanation: Round 1 heats: real advancement stakes for 48 surfers, but no medals move and the heavy hitters may get byes or easy draws.

experience.explanation: Cold 7:30 AM start on the cobblestones, no permanent grandstands. The shoreline view is intimate, but it's a long, low-key day on the sand.

starPower.explanation: Names like Carissa Moore could appear, but the opening round is full of universality entries and surfers few fans would recognize.

uniqueness.explanation: Early round of a returning sport, but the capped crowd at a natural California break makes it feel unlike any stadium session.

demand.explanation: Early-round surf at a capped-capacity beach. Scarcity helps, but it's the easier surfing ticket to land.

scorecard.overall: The quiet curtain-raiser: fog, cobblestones, and a field you're meeting for the first time. Not the day for stars or medals, but the best way to see Trestles up close with a small crowd.

significance.explanation: Round 2 heats where a bad exchange can end a campaign, though still a prelim with no medals decided.

experience.explanation: Morning-to-late-afternoon surf from the sand at a temporary beachfront setup. Atmospheric, but it's a daytime prelim without stadium energy.

starPower.explanation: Fresh Trestles winners Miguel Pupo and Erin Brooks, plus Carissa Moore, could be in the water if they qualify.

uniqueness.explanation: Mid-draw heats of a returning sport at a one-off beach setup. Distinctive setting, routine round.

demand.explanation: Capped beach capacity keeps interest up, but Round 2 is less competitive to book than the medal day.

scorecard.overall: A better bet for surf fans than Round 1: the field has settled, Trestles regulars are testing their home knowledge, and early exits start to sting. Worth it for the heat-by-heat tension, not the trophies.

significance.explanation: Round 3 narrows the field toward the quarterfinals, so advancement is on the line, but it's still not a medal session.

experience.explanation: Tighter heats and a field down to its better surfers, watched from the shoreline at a wave built for high-performance turns.

starPower.explanation: Medina, Griffin Colapinto, Molly Picklum and Carissa Moore headline a pool where the top-ranked tour names are likely in the water.

uniqueness.explanation: Possible countrymen-versus-countrymen heats with three surfers per nation add a twist, but it remains a prelim round.

demand.explanation: Stars are in the water and capacity is tiny. It's a harder ticket than the opening rounds, though not medal-day hard.

scorecard.overall: The sleeper pick for surf nerds: the tour's best are all in play, and the Medina-Colapinto subplot could land on home water. You get near-medal-day quality without the competition for medal-day tickets.

significance.explanation: Two gold medals plus bronze matches and semifinals in one day. Non-marquee sport, but multiple medal events push it high.

experience.explanation: Medal day on a world-class wave with the crowd on the shoreline. No grandstands, but the setting and tension are hard to beat.

starPower.explanation: Defending champions Vaast and Marks, plus Moore, Medina, Toledo and the Colapintos, mean serious name recognition among the contenders.

uniqueness.explanation: One-day, no-second-chances medal finish at a break that used to host winner-takes-all finals. Capped attendance makes a shoreline spot truly rare.

demand.explanation: Medal day with tiny on-site capacity: the hardest surfing ticket by a distance. Expect a scramble.

scorecard.overall: This is the one surfing ticket to chase: quarterfinals through gold on a home break for several contenders, decided by a wave or two. If you can get on the sand, you'll have seen something genuinely rare.

significance.explanation: Technical routine is only half of the duet score, and no medal is awarded. It does set the leaderboard heading into the free routine.

experience.explanation: Late-morning session in an open-air temporary pool near the Long Beach waterfront. Strict, precise routines reward fans who know what to watch for.

starPower.explanation: Austria's Alexandri twins, Shortman and Thorpe, and China's new Lin Yanjun and Xu Huiyan pairing give it real names, though none are household outside the sport.

uniqueness.explanation: Opens the sport's first Games back in Southern California since 1984, with a freshly rebuilt Chinese duet on show. Preliminary round, but a meaningful curtain-raiser.

demand.explanation: Opening-day technical session with no medals handed out. A softer ticket than the finals, though a Games seat in a small venue still goes.

scorecard.overall: The sport's return to Southern California starts here, with China's reshuffled duet facing the Alexandri twins and a reunited Shortman and Thorpe. No medals yet, but it's the easiest way into a rare, precise sport.

significance.explanation: Duet medals are decided here, with the free routine added to the technical score. A gold-medal session in a non-marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Medal-session energy in a compact outdoor pool, with music and choreography that play well to a live crowd. Late-morning slot keeps it just short of prime time.

starPower.explanation: Tio Casas, a world champion in all four disciplines, plus Shortman and Thorpe and China's Lin and Xu. Strong names for the sport, and the Wang twins' status is still unconfirmed.

uniqueness.explanation: First duet medals awarded in Southern California since the sport's 1984 debut in Los Angeles. A medal round in a returning sport, but not a once-ever pairing.

demand.explanation: The duet medal session is the first of only two artistic swimming medal days. A mid-tier sport final, with seats going quickly in a small venue.

scorecard.overall: The first of the sport's two medal days, and the better pick for anyone who wants the artistry. China's Lin and Xu, Spain's Tio Casas and Britain's Shortman and Thorpe make a real three-way story.

significance.explanation: Opening routine of three, so it sets the standings without deciding medals. Real stakes for the team, but the podium comes Saturday.

experience.explanation: Short 90-minute morning session at a temporary outdoor pool. Eight swimmers moving in unison is a visual treat, but no medals on the line.

starPower.explanation: China's lineup includes duet standout Lin Yanjun and Xu Huiyan, but team events trade on national brands more than individual names. Possible Russian return adds intrigue.

uniqueness.explanation: Open teams with up to two men are still a fresh format, only introduced at Paris 2024. This is an early round in a returning sport.

demand.explanation: Short Thursday-morning technical prelim in a small venue. Among the easier artistic swimming tickets, though Games scarcity still applies.

scorecard.overall: A short, sharp look at China's push to defend its title and at the mixed-gender format in action. Go for the synchronization and the early read on the podium race, not for medal drama.

significance.explanation: Middle routine of the team event, so it counts toward the final total but hands out no medals. The standings still shift here.

experience.explanation: Free routines bring themes, music and formations, which makes this the most theatrical of the team sessions. Still a morning slot at a temporary venue.

starPower.explanation: Japan, Spain and the United States are all in the mix, but few individual names will register with casual fans. China's absence from Toronto adds some curiosity.

uniqueness.explanation: A mixed-gender team free routine in the sport's return to Los Angeles, with an open question over what China shows. Early round in a returning sport.

demand.explanation: Friday-morning prelim with no medals, but team event interest and the 1984 homecoming keep it a fairly steady ticket.

scorecard.overall: The pageantry session of the team event, where themes and formations count for as much as difficulty. A good pick if you want the theater without paying finals prices.

significance.explanation: Team medals are awarded after the final routine, with all three scores combined. A gold-medal session in a non-marquee sport.

experience.explanation: Throws, lifts and flips make this the most spectacular routine, and it closes the sport's program in Long Beach. Saturday-morning slot keeps it below prime-time level.

starPower.explanation: The United States, Paris silver medalists, are chasing China's defending champions. Duet standouts Lin and Xu add recognizable names in a mid-tier sport.

uniqueness.explanation: Last artistic swimming session of the Games, with a gold-medal showdown in an acrobatic routine that looks like nothing else. A medal round of a returning sport.

demand.explanation: The sport's final medal session, with a home team pushing for a podium. The best artistic swimming ticket on the schedule, in a small venue.

scorecard.overall: The sport's grand finale, where China's defense meets a home-crowd push from the United States. One missed catch can flip the podium, and the final day of artistic swimming is the one to book.

significance.explanation: Heats only, with the relay heats setting tonight's lanes. Real advancement stakes, but no medals are handed out before lunch.

experience.explanation: A 50-meter pool laid over an NFL field under a translucent roof is a spectacle even at 9:30 AM. Morning light, a lighter crowd.

starPower.explanation: Gretchen Walsh, Summer McIntosh and Katie Ledecky-level names are all in play, though stars sometimes ease through heats.

uniqueness.explanation: First morning of the pool program, with the first heats of the new 50m fly and 50m back. Novelty, not a medal.

demand.explanation: An easier ticket than the evening finals, but opening-day pool energy and cheap seats keep it moving.

scorecard.overall: The cheap way into the biggest pool in Games history. Catch the first-ever 50m fly and back heats and an early look at Walsh and McIntosh, with no medal drama to distract you.

significance.explanation: Four golds on night one: both 400m freestyles and both 4x100m freestyle relays. Few sessions in the pool carry more medals.

experience.explanation: Opening-night finals under the lights in a 38,000-seat stadium. Relay roars and a fresh crowd make this the best opening to the pool week.

starPower.explanation: McIntosh versus Ledecky for 400m gold, plus Walsh in the 100m fly semi and the American and Australian relay stars.

uniqueness.explanation: A women's 400m free with no Titmus and a new champion to crown. Night one of a record-sized swimming venue adds its own charge.

demand.explanation: First finals night, four medals, and the U.S. versus Australia relay rivalry. Among the hardest pool tickets.

scorecard.overall: The pool opens with a bang: a new women's 400m free champion, two relay showdowns, and 38,000 people. If you want one night of swimming, this is a very strong candidate.

significance.explanation: Heats with semifinal spots on the line, plus an all-or-nothing 400m IM heat where only eight advance to the final.

experience.explanation: A morning session in a spectacular stadium pool, with a mix of sprints and one distance medley to hold attention.

starPower.explanation: Marchand in the 400m IM and Tatjana Smith's comeback for the Netherlands. Sjöström and Ceccon-level sprinters add depth.

uniqueness.explanation: Smith's heat in a new cap is the hook; otherwise a standard morning of heats.

demand.explanation: Morning heats are an easier book, but Marchand's presence and the novelty of the venue keep interest steady.

scorecard.overall: Come for Marchand easing through a 400m IM heat and Tatjana Smith's first look in Dutch colors. It's a lower-pressure morning that rewards swim fans.

significance.explanation: Five medals, including the first-ever men's 50m fly and women's 50m back golds, plus the women's 100m fly. A heavyweight card.

experience.explanation: Five finals in two hours under stadium lights keeps the energy high. Sprint races over in seconds make for constant noise.

starPower.explanation: Walsh and Huske in the 100m fly rematch, Marchand in the 400m IM and Martinenghi defending. Plenty of marquee names.

uniqueness.explanation: First Games medals ever in the men's 50m fly and women's 50m back, all in one evening.

demand.explanation: Five finals and a Walsh-Huske rematch make this one of the toughest swimming tickets.

scorecard.overall: Five medals in two hours, with two brand-new events and an American 100m fly showdown against the clock. This is the night to see the sprint program born.

significance.explanation: Heats across six events. The 400m IM and 1500m free are straight-to-final, so only the top eight race on for medals.

experience.explanation: A broad morning sample of distances in a dramatic stadium pool. The 1500m heat is long, but the variety helps.

starPower.explanation: McIntosh in the 400m IM, Popovici and Hobson in the 200m free, and Marchand in the 200m fly.

uniqueness.explanation: First-ever heats of the men's 50m breaststroke give a debut feel to an otherwise routine morning.

demand.explanation: A daytime heat session, but McIntosh and Popovici make it an attractive and still easier ticket.

scorecard.overall: A rich morning for fans who like to scout the field. Popovici in the 200m free and McIntosh in the 400m IM are worth the early alarm.

significance.explanation: Four finals: women's 100m free, men's 100m back, women's 100m breast and women's 400m IM. Plenty of medals plus semifinals.

experience.explanation: Prime-time sprint finals in a packed stadium. The 100m races are short, loud and easy to follow.

starPower.explanation: McIntosh in the 400m IM, Sjöström in the 100m free and Tatjana Smith's comeback bid. Real marquee names.

uniqueness.explanation: Smith's comeback story is the unusual thread; otherwise a strong but conventional finals evening.

demand.explanation: Four medals and star swimmers make this a hot ticket, if a notch below the opening and closing-week nights.

scorecard.overall: Four golds, McIntosh in a distance medley and a possible Tatjana Smith comeback final. A great pick if you want sprints and a story.

significance.explanation: Heats only, though the 1500m free goes straight to a final, making Ledecky's morning swim her one chance to qualify.

experience.explanation: A daytime session with a long distance heat. The stadium setting is memorable, but the energy is lower.

starPower.explanation: Ledecky in the 1500m, McEvoy in the 50m free, and Dressel's possible return give real name value.

uniqueness.explanation: Ledecky's only 1500m heat is a quirk of the format. A decent draw but a routine round.

demand.explanation: Ledecky draws extra interest, but morning heats remain an easier ticket than the finals.

scorecard.overall: Watch Ledecky open her 1500m in the morning, with McEvoy's 50m free sprint as a bonus. Cheaper than the evening and still plenty of quality.

significance.explanation: Five finals including the first-ever men's 50m breaststroke, plus 200m free, 200m fly, 1500m free and women's 100m back.

experience.explanation: A deep finals night with very different race lengths. The 1500m builds a slow crescendo between sprint finals.

starPower.explanation: Popovici, Marchand, McKeown and a field of new 50m breaststroke contenders. Peaty's absence takes some shine.

uniqueness.explanation: The first medal ever in the men's 50m breaststroke, with an open field and no clear favorite.

demand.explanation: Five medals in one evening with Popovici and McKeown. One of the stronger sellers of the week.

scorecard.overall: Five finals and a brand-new event with no obvious winner. Popovici versus the 200m free field is the showpiece, and the 50m breast is wild to watch.

significance.explanation: Heats in four events, with the men's 4x200m free relay going straight to a final. Advancement is the only prize.

experience.explanation: A morning session with a relay heat for variety, and the debut of the women's 50m fly.

starPower.explanation: Marchand in the 200m IM, Kós in the 200m back, and Popovici and Hobson in the relay mix.

uniqueness.explanation: First-ever heats of the women's 50m fly give novelty, with the relay heat as a format quirk.

demand.explanation: A midweek morning session. Interest is steady, but this is a softer ticket than the evening finals.

scorecard.overall: A midweek morning for swim nerds: relay lane-setting, the first women's 50m fly heats and a possible Marchand 200m IM swim. An easier ticket with some real names.

significance.explanation: Five finals including Ledecky's 1500m free, the men's 50m free and the 4x200m relay. A heavy medal night.

experience.explanation: The 1500m builds the crowd lap by lap, then sprints and a relay bring it back up. Excellent range.

starPower.explanation: Ledecky, McEvoy, Douglass, Marchand in the semis and a possible Smith-Douglass breaststroke duel.

uniqueness.explanation: Ledecky's Los Angeles 1500m final at home is a once-only chance.

demand.explanation: Ledecky plus five medals makes this among the most sought-after nights in the pool.

scorecard.overall: Ledecky's 1500m at home is the headline, with Douglass versus Smith and a men's relay to follow. It is the best bet for anyone who wants a star-heavy night.

significance.explanation: Heats in four individual events and the women's 4x200m relay heat, which sets the eight finalists.

experience.explanation: A decent morning with a relay heat and a mix of sprints and middle-distance races.

starPower.explanation: McKeown, Regan Smith, Pan Zhanle, Popovici and McIntosh all could appear.

uniqueness.explanation: Australia's relay lane-setting is a good subplot; otherwise a standard prelim session.

demand.explanation: Star-heavy entries keep interest up, but it is a morning heat session and an easier book.

scorecard.overall: Morning heats with a lot of star names, including Pan Zhanle and McKeown. Go for the relay and the early look at the 100m free field.

significance.explanation: Four finals: men's 200m IM, 200m back, women's 50m fly and the 4x200m free relay. Tonight's semis feed later medals.

experience.explanation: A high-energy finals night with a world-record holder and a relay showdown under the lights.

starPower.explanation: Marchand in the 200m IM, Walsh in the debut 50m fly, Kós and McKeown. Hard to find a bigger bill.

uniqueness.explanation: The first Games gold in the women's 50m fly, and Marchand racing his own world record at home.

demand.explanation: Marchand's 200m IM and Walsh's debut event make this a top-tier pool ticket.

scorecard.overall: Marchand chasing a 200m IM gold with a world record to his name, plus the first-ever women's 50m fly. One of the best nights in the pool.

significance.explanation: Heats across five events, with the men's 800m free and mixed medley relay going straight to finals.

experience.explanation: An 800m free and a mixed relay break up the sprint heats. A decent morning in an excellent venue.

starPower.explanation: Milák, Grousset and Kolesnikov headline, though several top names may rest in the morning.

uniqueness.explanation: First heats of the men's 50m back and women's 50m breast, plus the mixed relay lineup puzzle.

demand.explanation: A weekday morning heat session. Interest is solid but less competitive than finals.

scorecard.overall: A quiet morning with a few puzzles: relay lineups, a long 800m free heat and the first 50m back and breast heats. Good for fans of the sport.

significance.explanation: Four finals: women's 200m back, men's 200m breast, women's 200m IM and the men's 100m freestyle.

experience.explanation: The men's 100m free final is a huge crowd moment, and the 200m races keep it building.

starPower.explanation: Pan Zhanle, Chalmers, Popovici, McKeown, McIntosh, Douglass and Marchand all on one card.

uniqueness.explanation: Early 50m back and breast semifinals add novelty, but the finals are classic format.

demand.explanation: The men's 100m freestyle and a star-heavy card make this one of the stronger evening tickets.

scorecard.overall: The men's 100m free is the marquee race of the week, and McKeown, McIntosh and Douglass fill out a stacked card. A premier night in the pool.

significance.explanation: Heats with the medley relays going straight to finals, so relay lineups are set. Advancement only.

experience.explanation: Sprint and relay heats in a big venue make for a lively, if early, morning.

starPower.explanation: Douglass, Walsh and Sjöström in the 50m free, plus the US relay stars. Strong name value for heats.

uniqueness.explanation: Douglass and Walsh in sub-24 form and the first look at relay lineups give this extra bite.

demand.explanation: A morning heat session that benefits from star power, but it is easier to get than finals.

scorecard.overall: A morning to watch sub-24 sprinters and see how the US builds its medley relays. Not a medal session, but a strong preview of the closing finals.

significance.explanation: Five finals in one evening, including two brand-new events and a mixed medley relay, with two semifinals on top. Swimming is a marquee sport, and this is a medal-heavy night.

experience.explanation: Prime-time 6 PM start with the pool on the stadium floor, canopy overhead and the ring video board lit up. Sprint finals keep the crowd on its feet.

starPower.explanation: Milák, Wiffen and a US-led mixed relay anchor the finals. Sjöström, McIntosh and Douglass in the semis add names even before the medals are handed out.

uniqueness.explanation: Two first-ever Games medal races, men's 50m back and women's 50m breast, are decided in one evening. That kind of history can't be repeated.

demand.explanation: Evening finals in a marquee sport in a 38,000-seat stadium make this one of the hot tickets of the pool program. Expect fierce competition to book.

scorecard.overall: Come to watch history being made twice: the first champions in the men's 50m back and women's 50m breast. Add Milák's butterfly defense, an 800m free final and a mixed relay, and this is a stacked night in the pool.

significance.explanation: Five gold medals are decided, including both medley relays and Ledecky and McIntosh territory. It's the final weekend of the pool program, with the sport's biggest events in play.

experience.explanation: A 3 PM start gives up some prime-time glow, but daylight under the canopy and a stadium full of fans watching relays is still a big atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Ledecky, McIntosh, Regan Smith, Sjöström, Douglass and Gretchen Walsh could all appear in one session. It's about as many household names in the water as the sport offers.

uniqueness.explanation: A stadium-sized pool and a possible world-record 50m free make it special, but it's a standard finals format rather than a debut. It's a strong closing-weekend slot more than a one-off.

demand.explanation: Women's sprint and distance finals, plus two relays on the final weekend, are an easy sell. The afternoon slot makes it a slightly easier get than the evening finals sessions.

scorecard.overall: Swimming's final weekend packs in the women's 50 free showdown, a possible Ledecky 800 and a McIntosh-Smith butterfly rematch before two relays. It's an afternoon of stars rather than prime-time spectacle, and a strong way to cap the pool program.

significance.explanation: Opening-round mixed doubles, where every team is fighting to advance to the quarterfinals but no medals are decided yet.

experience.explanation: Daytime start on Center Court under open sky. Good seats for a first look at the Carson hard courts, without prime-time energy.

starPower.explanation: No pairs confirmed yet, so top names may or may not appear in these early matches.

uniqueness.explanation: Mixed doubles now opens the whole tennis program in a new two-day format, which gives the first round extra novelty.

demand.explanation: Center Court seating for the program's first day should move quickly, though this opening round is less competitive than the medal sessions.

scorecard.overall: Tennis opens with three first-round mixed doubles matches on Center Court, the first step in a new two-day format. Seats here are the stadium's main draw, and the matches set the tone for the whole program.

significance.explanation: First-round mixed doubles where advancement is the stake and medals are still far off.

experience.explanation: Daytime session on a smaller show court. Close-up doubles in the sun, though without the stadium atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Court 1 pairings are unannounced, so the level of star power depends on late entries.

uniqueness.explanation: A first round in the new opening-day mixed doubles format, which is a fresh start to the tennis program.

demand.explanation: Smaller court keeps demand modest, though Games scarcity still means seats will not be easy to book.

scorecard.overall: Three first-round mixed doubles matches on Court 1 open the tennis program in the afternoon. The compact court puts fans near the net for quick doubles exchanges, with the winners returning later that evening.

significance.explanation: Two first-round matches where winners advance to the evening quarterfinals, with medals still to come.

experience.explanation: Daytime action on a small court with limited seating. Intimate, but the smallest stage of the opening day.

starPower.explanation: Lower-profile slot on the smallest court, so the names in these first-round matches are less likely to be familiar.

uniqueness.explanation: Routine first-round doubles at a secondary court, though it still opens the new mixed doubles program.

demand.explanation: Small court and limited seats make this an easier booking, though Games scarcity still applies.

scorecard.overall: Two first-round mixed doubles matches on Court 2 are a relaxed start to the tennis program. Fans sit very close to the baseline, which suits anyone who wants to see Games-level doubles without the crowds.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinals decide who reaches the semifinals and the medal round, so the stakes are real but not yet medal-deciding.

experience.explanation: Evening quarterfinals on Center Court as the sun drops. Prime-time energy in a strong open-air venue.

starPower.explanation: Quarterfinal mixed doubles teams may include tour players, though entries are not confirmed.

uniqueness.explanation: Quarterfinals are part of the new two-day format, and winners play again the next day, which adds some novelty.

demand.explanation: Evening Center Court seats are in demand, especially for the first real tension of the tennis program.

scorecard.overall: Two evening quarterfinals on Center Court make for a sharp, late opening-day session. Winners return the next morning, and the matches show how fast the new format tests stamina.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinal stakes, with winners moving on to the semifinals and a shot at a medal.

experience.explanation: Evening doubles on a smaller court. Close-up and energetic, though less spectacle than Center Court.

starPower.explanation: Court 1 quarterfinalists are not yet confirmed, so headline names are uncertain.

uniqueness.explanation: Evening quarterfinal in the new mixed doubles format, which is fresh but still early in the event.

demand.explanation: Smaller court and fewer seats make this a less competitive booking than the Center Court quarterfinal.

scorecard.overall: Two evening quarterfinals on Court 1 run alongside the Center Court matches. Fans get close to the action, and the winners move on to the July 20 semifinals.

significance.explanation: Semifinals decide who plays for gold or bronze, making this the first real medal-race session of the tennis program.

experience.explanation: Daytime semifinals on Center Court in an open-air stadium. Solid stakes, though without evening energy.

starPower.explanation: Semifinal teams may include strong players, though no entries are confirmed.

uniqueness.explanation: Mixed doubles semifinals in the new format, held on the same day as singles opens.

demand.explanation: Medal-round semifinal on the main court draws strong interest, though seats are easier than the final.

scorecard.overall: Mixed doubles semifinals on Center Court set up the first gold and bronze matches of the tennis program. Singles starts the same day, so players in both events face a demanding schedule.

significance.explanation: Round 1 opener on the first singles day. Every player is fighting to advance, but the medal stakes sit well down the bracket.

experience.explanation: Daytime-to-evening schedule on the first show court. Good sightlines and a full day of matches in the sun.

starPower.explanation: Early-round marquee names may appear, but top players could be adjusting after the grass-to-hard switch and aren't guaranteed.

uniqueness.explanation: Opening day of singles on a show court is a one-time moment, though first-round matches are standard.

demand.explanation: Singles opening day on a show court should sell well, though it is less competitive than later sessions.
